finals.label: dead-symbol-no-consumer-or-definition

skill_entry.name: 14. An added symbol, include, parameter, branch or header edit needs a consumer at HEAD (and a declaration needs a definition)
skill_entry.trigger: Any one, taken from `git diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t` (BASE = the PR's base.sha): (a) an added column-0 declaration: `constexpr TYPE NAME =`, a function body `TYPE NAME(` whose line ends in `{` or an open parameter list (not `;`), `using NAME =`, `extern ... NAME(`, or a member added inside a struct the diff touches; (b) an added `#include`, or a removed function body that leaves a bare prototype; (c) a hunk that adds a parameter line under an `@@` context naming a function; (d) an added `if (X)` on a flag or enum inside a block an enclosing `if (X)` / `if (!X)` ... `else` already guards; (e) a statement after `TRON_ASSERT(false`, `std::unreachable` or `abort(`, or a second `TRACE_EVENT_END`, unlock or release for one span in one function; (f) a declaration in the 5 lines above `#ifdef X`; (g) a touched header no other file under h/, src/, t/, bin/ or ingest/ includes.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Names (a): `git grep -n -w NAME HEAD -- h src t bin ingest`, minus the declaration and definition lines. Zero = item. A member: zero reads outside the struct. 2. Zero-caller function: grep the 10 lines of comment above it for 'called (between|after|before)|reset|clear|release'; a hit sends you to the lifecycle code and to every writer of the fields it clears. 3. Prototype without definition: with call sites = link error (Normal); without = declaration ahead of its code (minor). 4. Include X in file F: list the names X provides (fixed table for standard headers, namespace prefix for out-of-tree headers, grep for in-tree headers); grep F for them outside the include line; compare with BASE:F (already used there = the include added nothing); `git log --no-merges BASE..HEAD -- F` for a move-out commit; `uniq -d` for duplicates, blamed on the commit that added the second copy. 5. Parameter (c): the argument at every call site and the later writer of the field it fills. 6. Branches and statements (d, e, f): walk the enclosing conditions by hand; TRON_ASSERT is unconditional. 7. Includers per touched header (g). 8. Lift test on the title and body; fold minor-tier items into one 'fwiw' line on a lift PR. 9. One item per name; chain 'and this?' under the first.
skill_entry.question: Which line at HEAD, other than its own declaration, reads, calls, includes or compiles this, and if none does, what is it in the PR for?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A test-only or debug-only helper: ask for the label, not removal ('this `xfer_k_entry` is a UT-only utility function. We should document that clearly', 3866590750). A kept-for-later function once the author says so (PR 1920 approved with both dump functions present). A return after an always-failing assert when the author answers it mirrors the old logic (Wade asked 3120804824; author replied 3125423449; not pressed). An include the PR body names with its reason ('header hygiene (<cmath>, <cstdlib>)', PR 2646). Dead code outside the diff (another branch, a pre-existing file): 'fwiw' only (2941308844, 3866653656). Commented-out lines (separate nit). .py, .json, .txt, CMake test rows, doc and register-map regenerations. Helpers of a new test file. Lift PR (title or body says 'step N', 'phase N', 'lifts', 'pulls in', 'from the X branch'): minor-tier items fold into one 'fwiw' line; normal-tier items still fire (3029165954 is on 'phase 1' PR 2287). A member with readers that duplicates a sibling belongs to redundant-code-simplify.
skill_entry.finding_shape: "I don't see where `<name>` is used? (<file>:<line>; at <HEAD> `git grep -w <name>` finds only the declaration.) <left over from <the move to <new file> | the merge> | just for completion/future enhancement?>" and, when the name or comment promises a behaviour: "how come I don't see this being called anywhere? We should be <clearing these flags> <between forward passes> right?" For an include whose names BASE already used: "what does this #include get us?" On a lift PR, one line: "fwiw, <names> have no consumer at this head; they exist on <source branch>, so I assume they land with the next step?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Never 'nit' for this check; always a question. Minor when the leftover compiles to nothing: an unused include, alias, constant, a prototype with neither definition nor caller, or a kept-for-later function ('Just for completion/future enhancement?', 'left over cruft', 'don't need this bf16.hpp include now right?', 'what does this #include get us?'). Normal when a missing consumer means a missing behaviour or a missing definition: 'how come I don't see this being called anywhere? We should be clearing these flags between forward passes right?', 'where's the actual implementation for this now?' (five call sites, no definition), 'if we always call `fill_attn_job_template` with an empty set for 'shards' vector, what's the point?'. Informational ('fwiw') for dead code outside the diff and for minor-tier items on a lift PR.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (enclosing conditions, the whole include block, the function body for a second end/release); callers (git grep over h/ src/ t/ bin/ ingest/ at HEAD and at BASE for an include's names); other files (the header the PR shrank, the new file the code moved to, the callee of a new parameter, CMakeLists.txt for a new definition file); commits (the move-out commit of F, the commit that added a duplicate include, merge commits); PR title and body only for the lift test and for an include's stated reason. Not CI, not runtime. Line numbers come from the comment's original commit, not the corpus `commit` field.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: an added symbol, include, parameter, branch or header edit needs a consumer at HEAD

Setup. `BASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha)`. When gh is unavailable and HEAD is a merge commit of the base branch, `BASE=$(git -C WT rev-parse HEAD^2)`. Verify with `git -C WT diff --shortstat BASE HEAD` against the PR's changed_files/additions/deletions from `gh api` (PR 1920: 8 files, +1742 -29 at b604cb860a). Never use `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` for a merged PR: it returns HEAD (PR 1920, PR 2233) and every step then finds nothing.

1. Added declared names.
   Constants: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -oE '^\+\s*(inline\s+)?(static\s+)?constexpr\s+[A-Za-z_0-9:]+\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -u`.
   Function definitions (column 0 only; the character class must not contain a space, comma or digit, or indented statements and local `std::vector<T> name(n)` declarations match): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -E '^\+(inline |static )?[A-Za-z_:<>]+ [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' | grep -vE ';\s*$' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' | tr -d '(' | sort -u`. Drop names that `git -C WT grep -n -w "$n" BASE -- h src t bin` already finds; only functions the PR introduces remain.
   Aliases and externs over h, src and t (not h alone, or `using json = nlohmann::json;` in t/t_hwattention.cpp is never listed): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -E '^\+\s*(using [A-Za-z_]+ =|extern )'`.
   Struct members: read each touched struct in `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE` and take the added member lines by hand (no grep separates members from locals). A member that has readers but duplicates a sibling (nshards next to shards.size(), 3010846319) belongs to redundant-code-simplify, not here.
2. Consumers per name, declaration excluded: `for n in NAMES; do c=$(git -C WT grep -n -w "$n" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v -E "constexpr [A-Za-z_0-9:]+ $n *=" | wc -l); printf "%-28s consumers=%s\n" "$n" "$c"; done`. For a function also use `-w` and subtract the definition line and the prototype line, when one exists; do not use `NAME\s*\(` (a9a9cf30a4:h/tron/models/model.hpp:2825 `base_load` has 4 uses by `-w`, 0 by the paren form). consumers=0 is an item. For a member list writers too; a writer the diff deletes, or that only mirrors a superseded field, counts as dead.
3. Promise in the comment of a zero-consumer function: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L-10)),${L}p" | grep -n -i -E 'called (between|after|before|on|when)|reset|clear|release|must be|should be'`. Only a hit sends the item to the lifecycle search: grep the point the comment names (`git -C WT grep -n -E 'forward pass|reuse|create_children' HEAD -- h/tron/scheduler h/tron/models`) and every writer of the fields the function writes (`git -C WT grep -n 'k_complete_\|v_complete_' HEAD -- h src`). A Doxygen block without a hit (dump_kv_cache_from_hbm, 2d53016b44:h/pos/hwattention.hpp:1135-1144) stays minor from step 2.
4. Declaration without definition: `for n in EXTERN_NAMES; do git -C WT grep -n -E "^[A-Za-z].* $n\(" HEAD -- src h; done`; `git -C WT grep -n '<defining file>' HEAD -- 'src/*/CMakeLists.txt'`; confirm the defining file is in `git -C WT ls-tree HEAD <path>`. No definition at HEAD and none at BASE: if `git -C WT grep -n -w "$n" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest` finds a call site, it is a link error, Normal ('where's the actual implementation for this now?', 3463077403: five call sites, no definition; 4d2a3951e7 adds `models/hw_attn_config.cpp` to src/tron/CMakeLists.txt while the file is absent from the tree, d71d7cfc13 adds it two days later). No call site either: the declaration is ahead of its code, minor; on a lift PR it goes into the one 'fwiw' line (7f993bc2db:h/tron/hardware/driver.hpp:231, :246, :331, :337, :344 on PR 1707, Wade silent).
5. Added includes: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -E '^\+\+\+ |^\+#include'`. Per include X in file F:
   Names X provides, three cases. (a) Standard header, fixed table: <fstream> -> ifstream, ofstream, fstream; <thread> -> std::thread, this_thread, jthread; <atomic> -> atomic; <exception> -> std::exception, terminate, rethrow; <random> -> mt19937, random_device, uniform_; <cmath> -> std::abs, isnan, isinf, sqrt, pow, exp, log, floor, ceil, round; <cstdlib> -> getenv, malloc, free, abs, strtol; <cstdint> and <cstddef> never a finding. (b) Header not in the tree (spdlog, fmt, catch2, nlohmann): grep F for the namespace prefix the header owns (`fmt::`, `spdlog::`, `nlohmann::`, `Catch::`). (c) In-tree header: `git -C WT show HEAD:X | grep -oE '^(extern |inline |constexpr |static |template)?[A-Za-z_:<>*& ]+ [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\($' | tr -d '('`, plus `^(struct|class|using|namespace) NAME`, plus the namespace of every `#include ... // IWYU pragma: export` line in X (common/json.hpp:5 exports nlohmann::json).
   Uses: `git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep -n -w -E 'NAME1|NAME2|...' | grep -v '#include'`. Zero = item. A use under `#ifdef` counts as a use (that case belongs to debug-switch-or-output-left-on).
   Already used at BASE: `git -C WT show BASE:F | grep -n -w -E 'NAME1|...'`. Every name already used there = the include changed nothing that compiles; ask what it is for, minor ('what does this #include get us?', 2729005716: BASE b604cb860a model.hpp used fmt::format_string at :639, :654, :669 before bundled/core.h entered at :20).
   Body reason: `gh pr view N --json body -q .body | grep -n -i -F 'X'`; a body line that names the include with its reason ('header hygiene (<cmath>, <cstdlib>)', PR 2646) is the author's answer, do not ask again.
   Move history, both directions: `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' --no-merges BASE..HEAD -- F` and `git -C WT show --stat <commit>`; a commit that removes more than half of F's lines while creating a new file (PR 1920: dd2ced785b, t/t_hwattention.cpp -466, t/t_hwattention_replay.cpp +524) marks every zero-use include or alias in F as 'left over from the move to <new file>'. Keep `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' BASE..HEAD -- X` and `git -C WT log --format=%h -S'NAME' BASE..HEAD -- X` for the header-shrank case (PR 1997: 735a4ffb2d moved relerr/abserr/comberr out of bf16.hpp).
   Duplicates: `git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep '^#include' | sort | uniq -d`; then `git -C WT log --format='%h %p %s' -S'#include "X"' BASE..HEAD -- F` and call it a merge artifact only when the commit that added the second copy has two parents; otherwise name the commit (PR 1920: model.hpp `#include "pos/lib.hpp"` at :19 and :29, added by 11cbfa723a, one parent).
   An alias with zero uses in its file follows the same use grep (`git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep -c -w ALIAS` minus 1).
6. Added parameter: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^@@ -[0-9]+,0 \+[0-9]+ @@ .*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' -A1 | grep -E '^[0-9]+-\+\s+[A-Za-z_:<>&* ]+ [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*,?$'` (a hunk that adds lines and removes none, whose `@@` context names a function, whose added line is a parameter declaration); take FUNC from the `@@` context (PR 2233, BASE de8081fac4 HEAD af9438799a: `@@ -241,0 +260 @@ extern void fill_attn_job_template(` with `+    const std::vector<shard_layer_t>& shards,`). Then `git -C WT grep -n 'FUNC(' HEAD -- h src t`, record the argument at each call, and `git -C WT grep -n -E 'FIELD =|->FIELD\[' HEAD -- h src` for the later writer of the field the parameter fills (work_req->nshards written again at self_attention.hpp:634-640).
7. Branches and statements. Candidates: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+\s*if \('` (PR 1920: 29). Keep only those whose condition is a bool field, flag or enum compare that also appears in an `if` of the same function at HEAD; read those by hand, walking the braces outward (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=LINE 'NR<=L && /^\s*(if|\} else|else)/ {print NR": "$0}' | tail -8` is a candidate list, not a verdict; it does not track nesting). `git -C WT diff -U3 BASE HEAD | grep -n -A3 -E 'ASSERT\(false|std::unreachable|abort\('` for a statement after an always-failing assert (TRON_ASSERT is `if tron_unlikely (!(cond)) tron_abort(...)` at h/common/assert.hpp:69-74, and assert.hpp:3-4 undefines NDEBUG). `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n 'TRACE_EVENT_END("SPAN")'` for a second end of one span (cef0fb5b64:src/pos/worker.cpp:775 unconditional and :777 under `#ifdef PERFETTO_CMD_WDS_LOG`; at d4d6524dd5 one remains). For a declaration above `#ifdef X`: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L)),$((L+20))p" | grep -n NAME` and the whole file for uses after the block.
8. Touched headers: `for f in $(git -C WT diff --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp'); do b=$(basename $f); c=$(git -C WT grep -l -E "#include .*$b" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v "^HEAD:$f$" | wc -l); printf "%-40s includers=%s\n" "$f" "$c"; done`. Zero = nothing compiles the hunk; say whether the PR adds an includer later (3a8544cd35:t/t_gof_staging_leaks.cpp:43 `// IWYU pragma: keep`).
9. Lift test: `gh pr view N --json title,body -q '.title + " " + .body' | grep -n -i -E 'step [0-9]|first step|second step|third step|phase [0-9]|first phase|lifts?\b|pulls? in|merge of|from the [a-z_-]+ branch|originally authored by'`. One hit plus a named source branch (hwattention_sync, bill-attn-merge) = lift PR. Minor-tier items (unused constant, unused include, zero-caller helper with no promise, member with no reader, prototype with neither caller nor definition) fold into one 'fwiw' line listing the names and confirming they exist on the source branch (`git -C WT grep -w NAME origin/<branch>`). Normal-tier items still fire.
10. Report one item per name, include, parameter or branch; chain follow-ups in the same file ('and this?', 'same here') under the first item. Cite the commit Wade's comment was made on, not the corpus `commit` field (2915258232 and 2915281835 show 8f22c93862 but the state exists at 4491ff73db; 3463077403 shows 39396c8728 but the missing definition exists at 4d2a3951e7).

On PR 2903 (HEAD 64ea13a671 at the comment, BASE 947d045a14): step 2 lists inwork_ring_size consumers=1, max_cmd_fifo_depth consumers=1, short_timeout_ns consumers=0 (h/pos/config.hpp:49 `inline constexpr uint64_t short_timeout_ns = 1000;`, sibling timeout_ns at :46); at b8739108f7 (final head) `git grep -w short_timeout_ns` returns nothing (author: "no longer used. removed"). Step 5 on the same PR: pos/minfifo.hpp, <atomic>, <cstddef>, <cstdint> and common/assert.hpp have consumers in their files (device.hpp:265, minfifo.hpp:66/:73 and :34/:49/:71, driver.cpp:76, minfifo.cpp:9); no duplicate lines and no merge commit. h/pos/device.hpp:7 `#include <thread>` has no thread symbol in the file at 64ea13a671 or at b8739108f7 (only comments at :263/:266 and `pthread_barrier_t` at :581), so step 5 flags one include Wade did not raise; he did flag the standard header <fstream> on PR 1920, so no standard-header exemption is supported and this hit is recorded as an unraised step-5 result.
On PR 1920 (HEAD 2d53016b44, BASE b604cb860a = base.sha): step 1 with the column-0 regex gives exactly 13 functions; step 2 gives callers=0 for exactly dump_kv_cache_from_hbm (h/pos/hwattention.hpp:1145) and dump_qkv_data (:1177), 1 to 5 for the other 11. Step 5 on t/t_hwattention.cpp: <fstream> (:2), common/json.hpp (:13) and `using json = nlohmann::json;` (:27) have zero uses while t/t_hwattention_replay.cpp uses std::ifstream at :129, :234, :328, :378 and the same alias at :27; `git log --no-merges BASE..HEAD -- t/t_hwattention.cpp` lists dd2ced785b "break the replay test out into it's own test file as t_hwattention_replay". model.hpp:20 bundled/core.h: fmt:: used at HEAD :643-676 and :1376, and already at BASE :639, :654, :669 without the include (2729005716). Step 5 also lists the duplicate `#include "pos/lib.hpp"` in model.hpp (:19, :29; 11cbfa723a, one parent), which Wade did not post.
On PR 2287 (HEAD c459e255d9): callers=0 for clear_kv_complete (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:560) and >=1 for mark_k_complete, mark_v_complete, is_kv_complete; step 3 hits 'called between forward passes' at :559. On PR 4007 (HEAD 29a39ac33e): step 8 gives h/pos/hwattention.hpp includers=18, h/pos/hwattention_dump.hpp includers=0.
Silent-PR probe 2026-10-06: tron-3756 (36 files), tron-2875, tron-2135, tron-2774 produce no item; tron-4353 produced two only through the paren grep and the wide regex (base_load, inverse_speed), zero with the column-0 regex and `-w`; tron-1707, tron-1722, tron-2646 (lift PRs) produce 17 minor-tier items that step 9 folds into one fwiw line each.
finals.widen_delta: New check 14, not a widening of an existing one. Check 10 asks whether a hunk belongs to the feature (its candidate test needs removed BASE lines, so a pure addition never qualifies); check 12 asks for owner sign-off on a header change (its unobserved-guarantee half needs a comment that says a revert is undetectable). Neither searches for a consumer of a declared name, an include, a parameter or a header, nor for a missing definition. Count 21 comments over 12 PRs. The agent-run procedure reproduced Wade's item on PR 2903 (short_timeout_ns) plus one hit he did not post (device.hpp:7 <thread>, step 5); on PR 1920 it reproduced dump_kv_cache_from_hbm and dump_qkv_data, the three t_hwattention.cpp leftovers and the bundled/core.h question (after the BASE comparison was added), plus one unposted duplicate include in model.hpp; on PR 2287 clear_kv_complete; on PR 4007 hwattention_dump.hpp with 0 includers. On eight silent PRs it fires only on three lift PRs, which the lift rule folds into one 'fwiw' line each. The setup line changes for this check: BASE is the PR's base.sha, not the merge-base, because merged heads return themselves. The description line of SKILL.md gains "symbols, includes and parameters with no consumer, declarations with no definition, branches an enclosing guard already fixes" and the thirteen questions become fourteen.

skill_entry.name: 14. Spelling, wrong names and over-wide lines in added comments, strings and Markdown
skill_entry.trigger: The diff adds a prose line (a re-indented line counts as added): a `//`, `/* */` or ` * ` comment or a string literal in a C++ file under h/, src/, t/ or doc/, or a line of a .md file that lies outside a fenced code block (fence parity taken from the full file at HEAD). Shell, CMake and Python files, unchanged context lines, commit messages and the PR body are outside the trigger. Mechanical form: step 1 of the procedure (prose.py over `git diff BASE HEAD`).
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Extract added prose lines with HEAD line numbers. 2. Build the allow list: every word at BASE in h/ src/ t/ (identifiers split at underscores; comment and string words included), identifiers on code lines at HEAD in the touched C++ files, and file basenames at HEAD. 3. Spell-check with pyspellchecker; drop plurals, affix forms and 4-letter prefixes of code words; a word on two or more added lines is author vocabulary; read each one-off hit with no correction (run-together words). 4. Identifier-shaped tokens in comments and .md text: whole-tree count at most 1 and a one-letter-edit neighbour with two or more code hits. 6. Added .md heading case against siblings. 7. Added .md line wider than 1.25 times the widest unchanged line of its hunk.

finals.disposition: widen_existing (check 13). The stem procedure for value-suffixed families stays. The trigger widens from "adds a value-suffixed constant" to five more diff shapes that make up 17 of the 18 member rows (A 10, B 3, C 1, D 2, E 1); the suffix shape F keeps one row (6021333114). skill_entry.name: 13. A number in production code carries its role: a name in reach, a derivation, or the stem alone (the suffix convention stays inside the author's kernel files)
skill_entry.trigger: In h/ or src/, never t/, any one: (A) an added production line, or an unchanged line of a function the diff changes by more than a rename, uses a numeric literal other than 0 and 1 in arithmetic, an index, a comparison, a shift, a mask, an array dimension, a capacity argument or a plain argument, and no comment on that line or the line above names what it measures; an unchanged line counts only when the diff changes, or a hunk contains, the definition of the constant that would replace the literal (2948416014, 3350031805). (B) A removed line names a constexpr or macro and the added line in the same hunk spells that slot as a literal, a sizeof or an expression (2915275194). (C) The diff changes a named constant's value and a message in a file that uses it still prints the old value (3350031805). (D) A new sizing constant, or an added allocation or address formula that multiplies by one, has no derivation (3350173837, 2947992404). (E) A count constant is returned as a failure value (3235796275). (F) The diff adds or renames a value-suffixed constant; report the stem, never the suffix.
skill_entry.procedure: Scan added lines, comments and strings stripped, for literals of 2 or more and hex literals; drop a literal the paired removed line already carried. Scan the whole body of a touched function only where the hunk adds or removes a statement; keep an unchanged-line literal only when a same-value name is defined in the same file or h/pos/config.hpp and the diff changes that definition or a hunk contains it. Per literal, look up a constexpr or #define of the same value (or value plus one for a last-index comparison) whose name states the same quantity; prefer the name the file already pairs with the other operand. With no name: sibling operand named, an explanation of an equal literal removed in the hunk, count the file's bare literals, name the config file. Pair removed names with added literals (equal value: merge artifact?). For changed constants, grep the old value in messages that print its quantity. For sizing constants: derivation, sibling limits, use sites, whether a test can shrink it. Sentinel: point at INVALID_*. Suffixed: existing stem procedure.
skill_entry.question: Can a reader at this line say what the number measures without asking the author, either from a name that already exists in reach, from a comment that derives it, or from the stem of the constant alone; and if a name used to stand in this slot, why did it leave?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Literals 0 and 1 and the guide's exceptions (zero init, reset, comparison, empty value with the parameter name visible; a one-use alignas). A literal 2 in a pair or halving role (`num_fetchers / 2`, `pdci < 2` drew nothing in 2789750267) unless the hunk removes the comment that explained an equal literal (3454926024); a commented `/ 2` elsewhere in the file does not count. Any literal in t/. A lane width, shift amount or packing factor in SIMD or kernel code (no corpus row). A literal that only bounds or formats diagnostic output; inside a debug-gated block fire only when an existing name stands in reach (2737603648). A literal in a log string that is the claim itself. A literal an adjacent comment marks temporary. A value-suffixed name inside the author's own kernel files (6021333114). A stem that names a role (`BF16_BITS_16`); namings of 1, true, false. An author's written deferral: nit, never block. A message mismatch unrelated to a changed constant, a missing comment on an env default, and placement belong to other checks.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (A), (D), (E): "`<expression>` (<file:line>) uses the hard-coded <N>; <config file:line> already names that quantity `<name>` [| nothing in h/ names it, and the file has <k> more bare literals (<list>)]. Should we use `<name>` here rather than <N> [| name it next to `<siblings>` in <config file>, or add a comment saying what <N> measures]? Nit." (D) sizing: "where did <N> come from? <sibling limit> is <M> on the <other> side; is <new constant> meant to be independent of it? Could <class> take the size as a constructor argument defaulting to <new constant>, so tests can reach wrap-around and full with a small queue?" (B), (C): "why replace `<name>` with hard-coded `<N>`? They are the same value, so <bound> is unchanged; merge artifact? [| the value changed from <old> to <N>: was this intentional? If so, a comment or a named constant for <N>.]" (F): the existing stem shape, unchanged.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Nit for an existing-name substitution, a sentinel or a shape comment: `just a nit, but returning `NUM_CLASSES` as an *error* condition seems non-intuitive` (3235796275), `can we add a short comment explaining the `/ 2` above?` (3454926024), a ```suggestion block when the fix is one line (2737603648, 2789750267, 3350031805). Minor question for a name that became a literal: `why replace `tron::hardware::hwkv_max_layers` with hard-coded `32`?` (2915275194), `was this intentional? If so, should probably note what's special about `1000`` (3307459854), `why 64? perhaps a comment explaining...` (3120756577). Normal, as a design question with two readings, for a sizing constant with no derivation (`Are you intentionally decoupling TX from RX here?`, 3350173837) or a constant that fixes a model parameter (ending `Right?`, 2947992404). General statements are filed as clean-up remarks with a smiley: `I really don't like all these magic numbers we use everywhere ;)` (2636393495), `We really should try to use some constexpr values or something... instead of these magic numbers :-)` (2915246595). On a merge or port PR, report no-name findings as one such remark, not per line. Never blocking: he approved PR 1666 eight minutes after the comment (2620219338 at 17:15:25Z, APPROVED 17:23:55Z, before the author replied at 18:05:31Z) and PR 1730 seven minutes after (2636393495 at 21:48:02Z, APPROVED 21:55:36Z, no author reply in the corpus).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (the whole touched function at HEAD where a statement was added or removed, because two rows sit on unchanged lines; the removed comment lines of the hunk; the file's other bare literals; the file's own constants, since the 2948416014 name lived in the same file); other files (h/pos/config.hpp and the headers the file includes, for an existing name with the same value; the partner file on the other side of the data path, for spellings; t/ for a test that reaches wrap-around with a smaller size); commits (`git log -m -S` for the merge that kept a branch's literal; the non-merge commit that wrote it). PR body or title to detect a merge or port PR and a stated reason to retire a constant. Runtime only as a question to the author (`How deep do we get in your tests?`). Hardware meanings (8 KV heads, 32 pseudochannels) are not in the repository: the agent asks what the literal measures and never asserts the meaning.

## Check 13: a number in production code carries its role (widened 2026-10-06)

0. BASE for a merged PR or a reviewed commit older than the final head (the common setup's `merge-base HEAD origin/main` is wrong when the PR targets another branch, and `merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD itself once the PR is merged): `MERGE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N -q .merge_commit_sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $(git -C WT rev-parse $MERGE^1))`. Check `git -C WT diff --stat BASE HEAD | tail -1` against the PR file count on GitHub. (PR 2176: BASE 1794cdf67d for reviewed commit 9553cd0a11; 15 files.)

1. Bare literals in added production lines, comments and string contents stripped: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -E '^\+' | grep -vE '^\+\+\+' | sed -E 's#/\*.*\*/##g; s#//.*$##; s#"([^"\\]|\\.)*"#""#g' | grep -vE '^\+[[:space:]]*(#|\*|/\*)' | grep -nE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.])([2-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)([^A-Za-z0-9_.]|$)|0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+'`. Map each hit to HEAD file:line through the `@@` headers. Paired removed line: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- FILE | grep -B1 -F '<added line>'`; drop the literal when the `-` line directly above carries the same literal (a line that changed only another token keeps its old literals out: the `4` in `4 * n_kvheads * head_size * sizeof(bf16)` at src/pos/hwattention.cpp:51, PR 2176). Drop a literal when the line, the line above, or the only other use of the same literal in the same file carries a comment naming what it measures; keep it for step 3 anyway when a same-value name is reachable (2789750267 fired on `pdc == 31` under a comment). Literals inside a multi-line block comment or an `#if 0` block survive the sed and must be dropped by hand.

2. Unchanged lines of touched functions, only for hunks that add or remove a statement (never rename-only or signature-only hunks: tron-3756, 36 files, approved silently). Hunk starts at HEAD: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3)} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); print f" "a[2]}' | sort -u`. Enclosing function for FILE L: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=L 'NR<=L && /^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][^;=]*\)[[:space:]]*(const|noexcept|override)?[[:space:]]*\{[[:space:]]*$/ && !/^[[:space:]]*(if|for|while|switch)\b/ {s=NR; ind=match($0,/[^ ]/)-1} NR>L && s && !e && match($0,/[^ ]/)-1==ind && /^[[:space:]]*\}/ {e=NR} END{print s, e}'` (do not rely on the `@@` funcname text, often `struct x {` or `public:`, nor on `git diff -W`: for 2948416014 the hunk changes lines after the function's closing brace). skill_entry.name: 14. A debug switch, a debug dump, a debug-only include or a trace promotion that ships on
skill_entry.trigger: In a file under h/ or src/ (never t/), judged against BASE: (a) FLIP: a `+#define NAME` line whose hunk twin is `-// #define NAME`, or a new uncommented `#define NAME` with no twin whose stem contains DEBUG, DUMP, TRACE, VERBOSE, LOG_, HEXDUMP or TIMERS (the `// #define NAME` ladder is the project's switch convention: off when the line starts with `//`). (b) UNGUARDED DUMP: an added debug_hexdump, debug_bf16dump or dump_* call outside every debug-switch `#ifdef`, in a file where a same-named call sits under one. (c) WRONG SWITCH: an added `dbg_<a>_log(` call whose text names the subject of a `dbg_<b>_log` macro the same diff adds. (d) DEBUG-ONLY INCLUDE: a header `#include` whose every use sits under one off switch. (e) TRACE PROMOTION: a TRACE_EVENT category changed from `<cat>-detail` to `<cat>`. (f) LEFTOVER: a log line starting with the author's initials, or a bare literal that gates debug text.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. BASE = merge-base of HEAD and the PR's base.sha from `gh api` (never origin/<branch> on a merged PR); to reproduce a posted comment use its original_commit_id. 2. Flips: diff the `#define` lines; keep `+#define NAME` with a `-// #define NAME` twin or no twin; drop `+//` lines and value edits. 3. Per NAME list its `#ifdef` blocks at HEAD, name what ships, count the ladder's off switches. 4. Intent: PR body, commit subjects, target branch. 5. Dumps: guard walk with a stack that counts `#ifndef`, skips comments and macro lines; GUARDED only under a ladder switch or a DEBUG-stem name. 6. Wrong switch: classify each added dbg_*_log call by its message subject. 7. Include: enumerate the included header's symbols, walk each. 8. Trace: read perfetto/apponly.cfg. 9. Leftovers: initials from `gh pr view --json author`. One question per site.
skill_entry.question: Is this switch, dump, include or trace meant to ship enabled in the target branch, and if not, which guard that the file already uses (`#ifdef GUARD`, `dbg_<subject>_log`, `<cat>-detail`) should it sit under?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: - A define that stays or arrives commented out (`// #define DEBUG_WLR` worker.cpp:86 at 247c8a4c22; `+// #define DEBUG_SAVE_KV 1` in silent PR 1722). - A value or comment edit inside an already guarded block (silent PR 2135, TOKEN_IDX_FOR_DEBUG). - A switch already on at BASE (`#define DEBUG_INFLIGHT_INIT` device.cpp:56 at worktree HEAD); the check is on the flip. - A direct spdlog::debug or spdlog::info with no adjacent dbg_*_log call, including inside another switch's block (silent PR 1827 self_attention.hpp:324 under MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG; silent PR 1973 hwattention.hpp:205-221; PR 2135 driver.cpp:294). - A dump on a path ending in std::terminate or debug_exit (2d53016b44 hwattention.hpp:503). - A dedicated debug module (src/pos/debug.cpp, PR 1707). - Anything in t/. - A trace change the PR body names as its subject. - Never block: he approves after the author answers (1973, 2011).
skill_entry.finding_shape: "`NAME` is now `#define NAME` at <file:line> (it was `// #define NAME` at BASE), so every `#ifdef NAME` block (<lines>: <logging on every dbg_x_log call / a file dump / an include>) ships; intend to leave this enabled in <branch>?" Variants: unguarded dump: "wrap in `#ifdef <GUARD>`?" (the sibling at :<line> is); wrong switch: a one-line suggestion block `dbg_<new>_log(` then "... right?", and "here too maybe?" on each further site; debug-only include: "IMO we should wrap this include in the `#ifdef <NAME>` guard"; leftover log: "still need this log?"; trace promotion: "do you really want to change this away from \"<cat>-detail\"?" with the reason from perfetto/apponly.cfg; flipped line under an "uncomment to ..." comment: "can we comment this back out before merge?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: A bare lowercase question, one line, no severity word: 'leaving enabled intentionally?', 'intend to leave this enabled?', 'wrap in `#ifdef WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS`?', 'still need this log?'. The wrong-switch case is a suggestion block plus '... right?', a nit by shape. 'can we comment this back out before merge?' is the strongest form (PR 2499, target branch hwattention_sync, flipped line directly under the file's own 'uncomment to ...' comment). Never 'Nit:' or 'Coverage gap:' labels, never CHANGES_REQUESTED; he approves after the author answers, even when the switch stays on (1973, 2011; PR 3016 is still OPEN with COMMENTED reviews only).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the flip or the added call); full file at HEAD (switch ladder, dbg_*_log macros, the #ifdef blocks the flip turns on, sibling guards, the depth of a printed local's declaration); BASE state of the define; other files (perfetto/apponly.cfg buffer size, fill policy and disabled_categories; h/common/perfetto.hpp category table; symbols the included header declares; includers of the header that gained the include; callers of a formatter); PR body, commit subjects and author name (initials); target branch name; comment original_commit_id when reproducing. Runtime: the Perfetto overflow rate is operator knowledge, reported as Insufficient data unless an operator statement is cited.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a debug switch, dump, include or trace promotion that ships on

Setup: `BASE_SHA=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $BASE_SHA)`. Never use `origin/<base branch>` for a merged PR: the merge-base is then HEAD itself and the diff is empty (2d53016b44 against origin/hwattention_sync). When reproducing a posted comment, HEAD is `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/comments/ID --jq .original_commit_id` and the line is `.original_line`; the digest's `(commit X)` is GitHub's current `commit_id`, often a later head where the author already applied the fix.

1. Flipped or new switches: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@)|^[-+] ?(// ?)?#define [A-Z_0-9]*(DEBUG|DUMP|TRACE|VERBOSE|LOG|HEXDUMP|TIMERS)[A-Z_0-9]*'`. Keep a line only if it starts with `+#define NAME` (no `//` before `#define`) and either (i) the same hunk has `-// #define NAME` (a flip) or (ii) no `-` line in the hunk names NAME (a new enabled switch). Discard `+// #define NAME` (a new off switch) and a `-#define NAME <old>` / `+#define NAME <new>` pair (a value edit). A flip whose stem the regex misses (13 of the 43 `// #define` lines at worktree HEAD: TRON_CALLED_ONCE, HEAP_SHADOW, PREFILL_WITH_NANS, SERIAL_DEVICE_INIT, SHOW_UNUSED_DEVICES ...) is caught by the twin rule: also run `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^-// ?#define [A-Z_0-9]+' ` and pair each with a `+#define` of the same NAME. Map to HEAD lines through the `@@` headers.
2. What the flip turns on: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -E '#ifdef NAME|#if .*NAME|defined\(NAME\)'`; read each block and name what ships (a `dbg_*_log` macro that expands to spdlog::debug and its call count `grep -c 'dbg_x_log('`, a file dump, a fixed TOKEN_IDX_FOR_DEBUG compare, an include). Ladder context: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -E '^(// ?)?#define [A-Z_0-9]+( [0-9]+)?$'`; a lone enabled line on a ladder of commented ones is the leftover shape. Name the other enabled switches of the ladder in the same comment (Wade named MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG from the hunk at DEBUG_GET_ALLKV).
3. Intent: `gh pr view N --json body,baseRefName -q '.baseRefName, .body' | grep -n -i -E 'debug|dump|trace|log'`; `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' --no-merges BASE..HEAD | grep -i -w -E 'enable|enabled|turn off|disable|disables|comment out|debug'`. The grep is a hint only (a misspelled subject such as 'diable it' escapes it); step 1 at the final head decides. Note the target branch. Every flip comment in the corpus (1973, 2011, 2499) is on a PR targeting the hwattention_sync feature branch; the author may answer that the switch stays on, and Wade approves. No corpus example of a flip on a main-targeted PR exists (Insufficient data for a main-specific rule).
4. Dumps and direct logs: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*(debug_hexdump\(|debug_bf16dump\(|[^a-z_]dump_[a-z_]*\(|spdlog::debug\()' | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+ *(//|inline |void |static )'`. spdlog::info is never a trigger of this check. Hits inside a file or function the PR adds as a dump module (every function named dump_*) are a do-not-fire case; list them once as a group. Per file: ladder and macros `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -E '#define dbg_[a-z_]*log|^// ?#define|^#ifdef'`, then the guard walk `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk '/^#if/{d++; g[d]=$0} /^#el(se|if)/{g[d]=g[d]" [else]"} /^#endif/{d--} /PATTERN/ && $0 !~ /^ *\/\// && $0 !~ /^#define/ {printf "%d: depth=%d", NR, d; for(i=1;i<=d;i++) printf " <%s>", g[i]; print ""}'` with PATTERN = `debug_hexdump\(|debug_bf16dump\(|spdlog::debug\(`. The walk counts `#ifdef`, `#ifndef` and `#if` (the old `/^#ifdef|^#if /` form missed `#ifndef NDEBUG` and gave model.hpp:1378 depth 0), prints the full guard stack only when depth > 0, marks an `#else` branch, and skips comment lines and the `#define dbg_x_log(...) spdlog::debug(__VA_ARGS__)` macro line. A hit is GUARDED only when some entry of its stack is `#ifdef NAME` or `#if defined(NAME)` with NAME on the file's ladder (`grep -n -E '^(// ?)?#define NAME' FILE` returns a line) or NAME matching the DEBUG|DUMP|TRACE|VERBOSE|LOG|HEXDUMP|TIMERS stem. A hit whose only enclosing guard is a build-configuration test (`#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16`, `#ifndef NDEBUG`) counts as unguarded; a hit under `#if 0` belongs to the disabled-code check, not here. Finding (dumps only: debug_hexdump, debug_bf16dump, dump_*): an unguarded added call whose same-named sibling call in the file is GUARDED (name the guard), unless the unguarded call sits on a path that reaches std::terminate() or debug_exit() within the same block. Direct spdlog::debug: never the sibling rule (the project writes spdlog::debug inside other switches' blocks, silent PR 1827); a finding only when the statement immediately before or after it (within 3 lines) calls the file's dbg_<x>_log macro and the call is at depth 0 or inside the `#ifdef` block of that macro's own switch (620d1e83ba worker.cpp:1143 under DEBUG_HWATTN_CMD_GEN, the switch of dbg_hwattn_cmds_log). Report it as a consistency nit with a suggestion block naming the macro. Mention `[[maybe_unused]]` only when a local the call prints is declared outside that guarded block: grep the local and compare its line with the block's `#ifdef`/`#endif`. A local used only inside the guarded block is the dead-symbol check's finding (2915258232), not this one.
5. Wrong switch: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+#define dbg_[a-z_]*log'`; for each file with a new macro, `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- FILE | grep -n -A1 -E '^\+.*dbg_[a-z_]*log\($'` and `... | grep -n -E '^\+.*dbg_[a-z_]*log\("'`; classify each added call by the subject its message text names (reuse, legacy wcmd, WLR); report every call on an older macro whose text names the new macro's subject, one comment per site.
6. Debug-only include: for each `+#include` in a header, enumerate the names the included header defines: `git -C WT show HEAD:INCLUDED | grep -oE '^(inline|static|constexpr|struct|class|using|void|bool|int|auto)[A-Za-z_0-9<>:, *&]* ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*) *(\(|\{|=|;)' | sed -E 's/ *(\(|\{|=|;)$//' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -u > syms.txt`; then for each name run the step 4 walk on the includer with PATTERN = `[^A-Za-z_0-9]NAME[^A-Za-z_0-9]`. Never use a namespace as the pattern: tron::hardware is shared by several headers (on 2d53016b44 self_attention.hpp `hardware::` gives 20 depth-0 hits from other headers). If every hit is at depth >= 1 under one `#ifdef NAME` and the includer has `// #define NAME`, the include belongs under that guard. Reach of the new edge = includers of the header that gained the include (`git -C WT grep -l '<includer basename>' HEAD -- h src t bin | wc -l`) times the size of the included file (`git -C WT show HEAD:INCLUDED | wc -l`); report both numbers.
7. Trace promotion: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -B1 -A1 -E '^[-+].*TRACE_EVENT\('`; keep pairs that differ only in the category string, plus new events. Category table: `git -C WT show HEAD:h/common/perfetto.hpp | grep -n -A2 'perfetto::Category('`. Capture config: `git -C WT show HEAD:perfetto/apponly.cfg | grep -n -E 'size_kb|fill_policy|enabled_categories|disabled_categories'` (at 4d2a3951e7, 590ff29f34 and HEAD: size_kb 2097152, fill_policy DISCARD, enabled_categories "*", disabled_categories "driver-detail", "hwattention-detail", "loading"; file present since dbe388bacb, 2025-10-15). A move from a category listed under disabled_categories to one that is not adds the event to the default capture; state that from the config. Name the enclosing function and its rate (hw_prepare: once per request per layer). The overflow rate is operator knowledge: write Insufficient data unless an operator statement is cited, and ask the question instead of asserting overflow.
8. Leftovers: initials from `gh pr view N --json author -q .author.name` (mcherba -> MRC); `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*spdlog::(debug|info|warn)\("INITIALS '` and `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*\b(XXX|TEMP|HACK)\b'`. Subsystem tags (ATEM, RX, TX, FUSE, TSC, JSON, KV, HW, SW, DMA, HEAP, SLOW: 45 lines at worktree HEAD) never fire. Gating literal: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*\? *[a-z_]+ *: *""'`; for a hit, `git -C WT grep -n '<formatter>()' HEAD -- src h` lists the callers and whether they already select which entries print.
9. One question per site; record the author's answer; a feature-branch "stays on" answer closes the item.

On PR 1973 (BASE ec16f160f5, HEAD 5e0606f0d8): step 1 lists exactly three flips, h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp @@ -20 +20 @@ DEBUG_GET_ALLKV and @@ -25 +25 @@ MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG, src/pos/worker.cpp @@ -80 +80 @@ DEBUG_HWATTN_CMD_GEN; step 2: MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG blocks self_attention.hpp:26, :315, :353, :425, :458, :483, :783 (TOKEN_IDX_FOR_DEBUG 385 compare files), DEBUG_GET_ALLKV :21 (include pos/hwattention.hpp) and :500 (Q/K/V dump), DEBUG_HWATTN_CMD_GEN worker.cpp:117 (dbg_hwattn_cmds_log becomes spdlog::debug at its 13 call sites) and :1144; the ladder :73-:86 has 14 switches, 13 of them `// #define` and this one enabled; step 3: body has 0 debug mentions, commit 0dd3e57c66 "enable debug and shift ktok calculation", no turn-off commit, base branch hwattention_sync; step 4: four spdlog::debug adds at h/pos/hwattention.hpp:205-:221 in a file whose only switch is `// #define WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS` and that has no dbg_*_log macro, so no finding (Wade was silent on them). skill_entry.name: A comment, log label or doc clause must match the code line it describes
skill_entry.trigger: Any one of these on an added line of the diff, in h/ or src/ (*.md hunks only for steps 7 and 8). (a) A comment that names a snake_case or backticked identifier inside a claim about code (captured from, comes from, set by, is set, sets, reads, waits on, waits for, already set, uses, performs, divides). (b) A comment with an angle-bracket placeholder (`<bdf>`), a path with a slash and an extension, a Q-notation token (`Q.61`), a negated parenthetical (`(no shuffle)`), or a trailing `?`. (c) A log or format call whose format string carries a label beside its argument list. (d) A hunk of at most 40 removed lines that replaces `type old = expr` with `type new = expr2` while a string or comment in the same block keeps the old stem. (e) A trailing comment whose first token is the declared name.
skill_entry.procedure: Map each line to HEAD through the `@@` headers; drop lines that also appear as removed lines after whitespace normalization (moved text). Identifier: confirm the token exists at HEAD; find the first assignment, wait loop or call of the sentence's subject in the next 90 lines (a header comment describes the body, not the signature); list that statement's identifiers. Token absent and a same-stem or same-struct sibling present is a finding, compared by name even when both hold one value. Label: pair each label with its argument, resolving a local alias one assignment back; grep the block L-20..L+40 for a stem the hunk re-derived; sort format strings for duplicates fed different objects. Placeholder: compare with the formatter argument in src/; grep h/ for the copy source. Path: resolve at HEAD, under h/, in an `#include` line or the PR file list. Tense, question, notation, negation: see the commands.
skill_entry.question: Does every identifier, placeholder, path, label, tense and negation in this sentence match the code line it describes, read at HEAD, and does a first-time reader get exactly one meaning from it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A token that matches no symbol at HEAD (typo item). A token present in the described statement, or read only inside a callee (`hold_if_evictable` reading use_count, PR 2875). A trailing comment on a name no rename in this PR made self-describing, or one that disagrees with its own declared name (identifier-name-states-role). A default, plural or `or` subject (claim-wider-than-code). An include-form or resolving path (`runtron/stream_generate.hpp`, PR 2875); a non-resolving path in a *.md body (doc/pos_heap_v2.md:689, PR 2713 approved). A question-form one-liner above a constant whose name answers it (h/pos/config.hpp, PR 1707 approved). A stem surviving in another file. Moved text. Doc structure, kernel arithmetic, benchmark text, .py/.json/.yaml/CMake, comment-only PRs (3799, 4551 approved with no text). Never block: PR 2915 was approved in the same minute as the Q3.61 nit.
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<comment or label text>` (<file>:<line>) says <X>, but the line it describes (:<N>) uses `<Y>`, so a reader of the comment looks for the wrong thing. you mean `<Y>`? ```suggestion <corrected line> ``` ... right? per line <N> below. Or: fix the code so the comment is true, when the comment states the intent. When the hunk does not show the old derivation a label depends on: `Insufficient data: old derivation not in the hunk`.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit to minor, stated by form rather than by a word: a suggestion block with the corrected line plus `... right?` (3405930260, 3437533506, 3120684367), or a one-line question (`you mean 'hw_prepare'?`, `why are you calling this `HW O` if you're printing the Ra value?`, `would this read better if it said ...?`, `I think technically this should be `Q3.61` right?`, `probably won't exist for anybody else but you ;p?`). The one `normal` row (2771718489) is a debug label that misreports the quantity under comparison; it is still a question, and he approved the PR 22 minutes 39 seconds later at c502e4d61a. He flags one instance per stem and approves (worker.cpp:1070 `prep_done` and alloc.hpp:226 `<bdf>` were left unflagged).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk, then the full file at HEAD (the statement below the comment, the block L-20..L+40 for surviving old stems, the alias one assignment back), then other files (the formatter in src/ that produces a quoted string, the declaring header where sibling identifiers live, the sibling comment the text was copied from, `git cat-file -e` for paths), and for two rows hardware knowledge the hunk must show (the removed `/ *hw_sume` line: O = Ra / SUME; the stated integer-bit count: Q3.61). Not the PR body, commits, CI or a runtime run.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a comment, log label or doc clause must match the code line it describes

Setup addition (for a merged PR, or when `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself): take the merge commit of the PR, `git -C WT log --first-parent --format='%h %p %s' origin/main | grep -m1 '#N'`, its first parent P (same as `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha`), and set BASE = `git -C WT merge-base HEAD P`. On PR 3008 at HEAD c68ea87f48: merge aabd416676, P = 8811bdd35f, BASE = dd5dd82caf, pr.diff 1233 lines (merge-base with origin/main gave HEAD and an empty diff).

1. Harvest. `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src > pr0.diff; grep -n -E '^\+\+\+|^@@|^\+\s*(//|/\*|\*)|^\+.*(spdlog::|_log\(|fmt::format\(|TRACE_EVENT\()' pr0.diff > step1.txt` and `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- '*.md' | grep -n -E '^\+\+\+|^@@|^\+[^+]' > step1-md.txt` (prose lines carry no comment prefix; steps 7 and 8 read them, step 5 does not). Map each `+` line to HEAD file:line through the `@@` headers (a 12-line python over the headers). Drop a `+` line that also appears as a `-` line in pr0.diff after whitespace normalization (moved text; Wade reads it as unchanged). Record three counts: harvested, moved, new. Tokens per line: `grep -oE '\b[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)+\b|`[^`]+`|<[a-z_]+>|\b[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[a-z]+\b|Q\.?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?|\((no|without) [a-z_ ]+\)'`, run on the `+` lines only, never on the `+++` header.

2. Identifier check. Pre-filter: `grep -E '^\+\s*(//|\*).*\b(captured from|comes from|set by|is set|sets|reads|waits? (on|for)|already set|uses|performs|divides)\b' step1-new.txt | grep -E '\b[a-z][a-z0-9]*_[a-z0-9_]+\b|`[^`]+`'` (no bare `calls` or `returns`: they hit prose such as 'invariants between calls' and 'Always returns true'). For each token: `git -C WT grep -q -w TOKEN HEAD -- h src || echo "NO SYMBOL: typo item"`. Described statement: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'L,L+90p' | grep -n -E '\bSUBJECT\b *=|\bSUBJECT\.(load|store|wait)|\bSUBJECT\('` and take the first hit (a header comment describes the body, not the signature: on PR 3008 the comment is :1112, the signature :1118-1129, the assignment :1138). List the identifiers of that statement with the token regex of step 1. Token absent: siblings by stem `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'L,L+90p' | grep -oE '\b[a-z]+STEM\b' | sort | uniq -c` and by struct `git -C WT grep -n -E 'TOKEN|SIBLING' HEAD -- <declaring header>`. A callee that reads the token internally is not a sibling. Compare by identifier, never by value: both `wres_fields.fields.hbm_cnt` and `ares_fields.fields.hbm_cnt` are set from `hbm_count` at :656-657, and the row is still a finding.

3. Label check. 3a pairs: for each added format call `grep -n -A3 -E '_log\("|spdlog::|fmt::format\("' full/FILE`; read the label before each `{}` against the argument in that position; resolve a local alias one assignment back (`sed -n 'L-15,Lp' full/FILE | grep -n 'ARG *='`; `prepare_tail {}` fed `dbg_wqe_idx` matches because :1725 reads `dbg_wqe_idx = dev->prepare_tail`). Only an argument whose source statement names a different quantity is a finding. 3b renamed quantity, bounded: keep hunks with at most 40 removed lines (`@@ -a,r +b,s @@`, r <= 40); inside one such hunk pair `^-\s*(float|double|auto|int|uint64_t|size_t) [a-z_]+ =` with `^\+\s*(float|double|auto|int|uint64_t|size_t) [a-z_]+ =`; keep the pair when the new name differs and the expression differs beyond the rename (a dropped `/ *hw_sume`). Then `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'L-20,L+40p' | grep -n -E 'OLDSTEM'` in strings and comments; list every survivor inside one finding per stem. A stem that survives in another file is not this check. When the hunk does not show the old derivation and the label needs hardware meaning (O = Ra / SUME), write `Insufficient data: old derivation not in the hunk`. A refactor hunk above 40 removed lines goes through 3a only. 3c duplicates: `grep -oE '^\+.*_log\("[^"]*"' pr0.diff | sed 's/^+ *//' | sort | uniq -d`; read the argument lists; identical arguments are not a finding.

4. Placeholder check. `grep -n -E '^\+.*(//|\*).*<[a-z_]+>' pr0.diff`; take the literal prefix and `git -C WT grep -n -F 'PREFIX' HEAD -- src`; compare placeholder i with argument i of the `fmt::format`. Copy source: `git -C WT grep -n -F '<bdf>' HEAD -- h` (replace the placeholder). Member test: `git -C WT show HEAD:<declaring header> | grep -n -w bdf`.

5. Path check, comments in h/ and src/ only: for every path token from step 1 run `git -C WT cat-file -e HEAD:PATH 2>/dev/null || git -C WT cat-file -e HEAD:h/PATH 2>/dev/null || git -C WT grep -q -F "\"PATH\"" HEAD -- h src t || grep -q -E "(^|/)PATH$" prfiles.txt || echo "MISSING PATH"`.

6. Tense. For each present-tense mechanism sentence naming function F: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- FILE | grep -n -E '^-.*(recurs|F\()'` and `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk '/F\(/{p=1} p' | sed -n '1,200p' | grep -c -E 'recurs|F\('`. Removed by the diff and 0 at HEAD: the sentence must be past tense.

7. Open questions. `grep -n -E '^\+\s*(//|\*).*\?\s*$|^\+.*(originally thought|proposed change|TODO: decide|should we)' step1.txt step1-md.txt`. Fire only when the question is about a mechanism or a decision AND the same PR either implements the answer in the statements below (fields, waits, branches: dma_xfer_state end_desc/readback fields) or removes a sibling comment that posed the same question (`git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^-.*(Proposed change|originally)'`, PR 2011 driver.cpp). A one-line question above a constant whose name answers it (`// How many metadata entries does the device hold?` above `metadata_entry_count`) is house style, not a finding.

8. Notation and wording. `grep -oE 'Q\.?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?' <comment block>` versus the integer-bit count stated in the same block and `git -C WT grep -n -E '_q[0-9]+\b' HEAD -- FILE`. Negation: for `(no X)` or `without X`, `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk '/F\(/{p=1} p' | grep -c -i X`; 0 hits = the sentence states an absence (`(no failure path on this leg)` with no false return) and is not a finding; hits where X is done to the input before the call = precondition, propose `pre-X`. Docs: `grep -n -E '\([A-Za-z0-9 ]+ (excepted|accepted|aside|excluded|included)\)' step1-md.txt`, write both full-sentence readings. Trailing restatement: `grep -n -P '^\+\s*[A-Za-z_:<>, ]*\b([a-z_]+);\s*//\s*\1\b' pr0.diff` (Perl mode; `grep -E` with `\1` fails on ugrep).

9. One finding per line, siblings of the same stem listed inside it: the comment or label, the deciding code line, a suggestion block with the corrected line, `... right?`. Both repairs named.

On PR 3008 (HEAD 17c6e0117d, comment commit c68ea87f48, BASE dd5dd82caf): step 1 = 133 added comment and log lines, 63 moved, 70 new, all in src/pos/worker.cpp; step 2 pre-filter hits c68ea87f48:src/pos/worker.cpp:1112 "hbm_cnt is captured from ares_fields before any WLR mutation" (tokens ares_fields, hbm_cnt); the described statement is :1138 `hbm_cnt = wres_fields.fields.hbm_cnt;`; ares_fields is absent from it and the sibling wres_fields is present (12 uses versus 9 in :1112-1200; both out-params of prepare_cmd_words at :563-564). Finding = 3437533506; applied at 17c6e0117d:1112 "wres_fields". Other pre-filter hits (:1130, :1153, :1217, :1235, :1348, :1373, :1476-1478, :1502) pass the identifier test or carry no identifier. Step 3a: 18 added log lines, 0 findings after the alias rule (:1727, :1746). On PR 2980 (comment commit 247c8a4c22): step 4 hits h/pos/device.hpp:663 `<bdf>`; the formatter src/pos/device.cpp:625 and :630 passes dev->idx; `bdf` is not a PosDevice member (only `int idx` at :255); copy source h/pos/alloc.hpp:226 `<bdf>` whose formatter src/pos/alloc.cpp:366 and :371 also passes dev->idx. Finding = 3405930260; applied at a62d15a3dc:device.hpp:663 `<idx>`; alloc.hpp:226 still `<bdf>`. On the silent set (15 PRs probed): PR 1707 h/pos/config.hpp:51 no longer fires (step 7 narrowed) and PR 2875 token_tree.hpp:324 `runtron/stream_generate.hpp` resolves under h/ (step 5); 0 findings on the rest.

skill_entry.name: 14. New code re-derives what an existing helper already provides
skill_entry.trigger: Any one of these in the diff's added production lines (h/ and src/, never t/; greps in procedures.md): (a) a `getenv("NAME")` (environment-variable read) or other configuration read whose topic (HW_ATTN) an existing function already reads or decides, under any variable name; (b) a busy-wait loop on a memory word where the project has a wait primitive (mwaitx); (c) a numeric literal passed to a configure, init or setup call whose parameter is a model- or hardware-derived quantity (scalar, head_size); (d) a per-model formula (`1.0f / sqrtf(head_size)`) a constructor or config object already computes with more branches; (e) a one-formula helper the diff adds while the same operands stand inline elsewhere; (f) an added if/else whose bodies differ ONLY by a type name or one string literal, shown by a line diff; (g) a commit/guard/push sequence copied whole to a second site under an ordering comment; (h) a call right after a loop whose callee walks the same container; (i) a grow loop beside a `resize` on a sibling member.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Collect candidates with the kind (a)-(i) greps over `git diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src`. Drop a line whose paired removed line carries the same call or formula (a re-spelling, tron-3756). 2. Find the owner outside the hunk at HEAD and at BASE: topic stem for (a) (TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN -> HW_ATTN), the wait primitive name for (b), the parameter stem for (c)(d), the formula operands for (e), each call name for (g); list the owner's callers. 3. Only when BASE has no owner, search the base branch with `--not HEAD` and `--until` the review date. 4. Read both sides; write every difference: operand type, alignment, element state, extra branches, the differing tokens of twin branches, a conjunct the helper does not cover. 5. For (g) confirm the hunk added the whole sequence, count the copies at HEAD, find the originating commit. 6. For (a) across the layering rule propose an `extern` declaration. 7. Report with per-kind counters.
skill_entry.question: Does a function or expression that already exists at HEAD, or on the PR's base branch before the review date, compute this value, decide this predicate, perform this wait or carry this ordered sequence, and can the author name a difference in what that helper accepts or produces that the output depends on?
skill_entry.do_not_fire:
- The helper cannot accept the input: operand type or alignment (1920, loop kept at the approved head), or element state the stdlib call does not produce (2461, Wade withdrew). A second configuration knob (another variable name, default or read-once) is NOT a difference: that knob is what the helper replaces (2287).
- A value a local or sibling member in the same scope already holds (`nshards` beside `shards.size()`): the redundant-code check (3029340601, 3010846319, 2913598312).
- A bare literal with no owning value in h/ or src/: check 13.
- Duplicates inside t/.
- A long pre-existing function grown further (3405172585: later step).
- Re-spelling, rename, formatting (tron-3756, tron-3741).
- A hot-path cost argument alone.
- Near-twin branches differing by an intrinsic, an argument or a return (tron-2693, 1707, 2646).
- An inline copy kept for another consumer at the approved head (441e81178b self_attention.hpp:797, :837, :1499).
skill_entry.finding_shape: "`<new expression or loop>` (<file:line>) re-derives <quantity> that `<helper>` (<file:line>) already <computes | reads | waits for>; `<site A>` (line <a>) and `<site B>` (line <b>) call the helper. Suggest one helper for all <N>, so the copies can't drift if the convention changes." Question form when the helper is a project primitive: "couldn't we use `<helper>` for this (and the <sibling site>)?" Statement form when the value has one owner: "the <quantity> needs to come from the model... `<literal>` is not the correct value, currently". For a conjunction name only the conjunct to replace (2287 kept `have_devices &&`). For a copied sequence: a numbered list of the copies and the consequence sentence, no block.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: "Nit:" for a key computed two ways (4147010638). No severity word, a plain question, for a primitive the project already has ("couldn't we use mwaitx::wait_for_not_event for this", 2719158416; "you should be able to use `resize` for this...?", 3102140611). Plain statement when he owns or knows the helper ("this should be replaced with the `fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` function I just added early this week", 3029194687) or when the literal is wrong for the model ("1.0f is not the correct value, currently", 2897190682). For a copied safety-critical sequence: a numbered list of the copies and the consequence sentence ("a missed copy would be a silent staging-lifetime bug rather than a compile error", 3907214892), still no block and no CHANGES_REQUESTED. His softest form is a question with an admitted constraint: "could we maybe ... just looking for an alternative" (3454460758); he does not use the word minor there.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at the reviewed commit (three line numbers across one file, 4147010638); other files in h/ and src/ at HEAD and at BASE (the helper's definition, the model state constructor, the layering rule in README.code-org.md); callers of the helper; the PR's base branch log before the review date, excluding the PR's own commits; the commit that introduced an ordered sequence (git log -S; Wade's own attribution '#3928' in 3907214892 is his, the log gives PR 2906 and 3385). Not the PR body, not CI, not runtime.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: new code re-derives what an existing helper already provides

Common setup as above (HEAD, WT, N), with two changes for this check. BASE is the merge-base with the PR's own base branch, not origin/main: `BASE_REF=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$BASE_REF)`. For a merged PR, BASE is the parent of the PR's first commit (`git -C WT rev-parse <first commit>^`). Record `git -C WT rev-list --count --no-merges BASE..HEAD`; more than about 100 commits means the base branch is wrong (PR 2287: base hwattention_sync gives ba1bed266d and 5 commits; origin/main gives 77195bba8c and 462 commits).

1. Candidates, production code only:
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src > prod.diff
# (a) configuration reads
grep -n -E '^\+.*(std::)?getenv\("[A-Z0-9_]+"' prod.diff
# (b) busy-wait loops on a memory word
grep -n -E '^\+.*while \(\*?[A-Za-z_>.-]+ *!= *[A-Za-z_]+\)' prod.diff; grep -n -E '^\+.*(rdtsc\(\)|ns_to_cycles|timeout_cycles)' prod.diff
# (c) literal arguments inside a configure/init/setup call (comment lines dropped)
grep -n -E '^\+[^/]*(configure|_init|setup)[A-Za-z_]*\([^)]*\b[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+f?)?\b' prod.diff | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+ *//'
# (d) per-model formulas written out (sqrt or a division next to the operand; a bare head_size argument is not a formula)
grep -n -E '^\+.*((1(\.0f?)?|1\.f) */ *(std::)?sqrtf?\(|rsqrt\(|/ *(std::)?sqrtf?\([^)]*head_size)' prod.diff
# (e) one-formula helpers the diff adds
grep -n -E '^\+ *return [A-Za-z_.()]+ *[-+*/] *[A-Za-z_.()]+( *[-+*/] *[A-Za-z_.()]+)?;' prod.diff
# (f) if/else candidates: list added `} else {` lines
grep -n -E '^\+ *\} else \{' prod.diff
# (g) ordered sequences
grep -n -E '^\+.*\.(commit|push|push_back)\(' prod.diff
# (h) loops over a sized container, (i) resize calls
grep -n -E '^\+.*(while|for) \(.*\.size\(\)' prod.diff; grep -n -E '^\+.*\.resize\(' prod.diff
```
   Filters applied to the collected lines before step 2:
   - Drop a line whose paired removed line (the `-` line of the same hunk) carries the same call name, member name or formula: a re-spelled argument, a rename or a reformat adds no copy (tron-3756 src/tron/gof.cpp:272 re-spells `tracker.push(static_cast<uint32_t>(sh->dev->idx),` as `tracker.push(` with the typed id).
   - (c): open the callee's declaration; keep the hit only when the parameter name stem is a model or hardware quantity (scalar, scale, head_size, n_heads, n_layers).
   - (f): map the hit to its HEAD line through the `@@` header, print 40 lines around it (`git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n 'L-20,L+20p'`), find the matching `if (` and the closing brace by indentation, record A1,A2 (if body) and B1,B2 (else body). Skip a hit whose else body is one log or return statement.
   - (g): keep a hit only when the same two or three call names appear in the same order within five added lines at a second site, and either site, or the function at BASE the sequence came from, carries a comment with 'order', 'before', 'after', 'must', 'live' or 'disarm'. Record dropped sites as 'no ordering comment'.
   - (h): keep only when the first call after the loop's closing brace names a function whose body walks the same container (open it). (i): keep only a `while (x.size() < n) x.push_back(...)` or `for` grow loop within five lines of a `.resize(` on a sibling member.
   Record the count per kind and the count dropped per reason.
2. For each surviving candidate, the owner outside the hunk, at HEAD and at BASE:
```
git -C WT grep -n '<operand>' HEAD -- h src | grep -v '<candidate file>:<candidate line>'
git -C WT grep -n '<operand>' BASE -- h src
git -C WT grep -n '<helper>' HEAD -- h src      # the owner's callers
```
   Operand per kind. (a): the topic stem of the variable name, with the prefix (TRON_, POS_, RZ_) and the verb word (USE_, ENABLE_, DISABLE_, NO_) stripped; run `git -C WT grep -n -E 'getenv\("[A-Z0-9_]*<STEM>[A-Z0-9_]*"' HEAD -- h src` (every environment read on the topic) and `git -C WT grep -n -i -E '<stem>_(enabled|disabled|on|off)\(' HEAD -- h src` (the predicate helpers). On 2287 (HEAD 4274d5878a) stem HW_ATTN yields USE_HW_ATTN at hw_attn_config.hpp:19 inside `fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` (:17) with callers stream_generate.hpp:429, model.hpp:1434, self_attention.hpp:387, :699, :945; the raw variable name TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN finds only the hunk. (b): `wait_for_not_event\|wait_for_event\|wait_for_geq` (h/pos/mwaitx.hpp at early-2026 heads). (c),(d): the parameter stem (`pre_attn_scalar`, `hw_attn_cfg`). (e): the helper's formula operands (`num_workers() - n_attn_workers`). (g): each call name.
3. Only when step 2 found no owner at BASE, search the base branch:
```
git -C WT log --format='%h %ad %an %s' --date=short --until=<review date or today> -S'<operand>' BASE..origin/$BASE_REF --not HEAD -- h src
```
   `--not HEAD` removes the PR's own commits (tron-4353: without it, `-S'TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT'` lists the PR's own 1dcb88ca28). Commits after the review date are not evidence. On 2287 the helper commit 45eb1fe682 (2026-03-27, Wado-posi) is an ancestor of BASE ba1bed266d, so step 2 at BASE already finds it; step 3 lists only this PR's own later merges (7eae660633, 99e5c61b1e).
4. Read both sides: `git -C WT show HEAD:<helper file> | sed -n '<a>,<b>p'` and the candidate's enclosing function. Write every difference: operand type and alignment (1920: the helper takes `volatile uint64_t*`, the V address at fcc9b0de95 hwattention.hpp:400/:405 is `- 6`, 2 bytes off 8-byte alignment); element state after the call (2461: `resize` fills `nullptr`, the loop fills `make_unique`); branches the owner has that the candidate lacks (2302: the softcapping branch reads `query_pre_attn_scalar`); the tokens twin branches differ by, from `diff <(git show HEAD:<file> | sed -n 'A1,A2p') <(git show HEAD:<file> | sed -n 'B1,B2p')` (2980: `weights_cmd_attn_fields` vs `weights_cmd_matmul_fields` and one space); statements between two adjacent loops (4258: none). When the candidate is a conjunction, match each conjunct: a conjunct the helper covers is replaced, one it does not cover stays (2287 at 1a88e897e1:827 keeps `have_devices &&`, replaces the getenv). A difference in the configuration knob itself (variable name, default, read-once) is not a do-not-fire reason.
5. For (g): confirm the added lines contain the whole sequence; then count copies at HEAD and which keep the comment, and date the sequence:
```
git -C WT grep -n -E 'reservation\.commit\(\)|guard\.commit\(\)|tracker(->|\.)push\(' HEAD -- h src
git -C WT grep -n 'Descriptors are live\|disarm rollback' HEAD -- h src
git -C WT log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -S'<call name>' -- <file>; gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/<sha>/pulls --jq '.[].number'
```
   On 4128: `-S'guard.commit()'` -> 576843b189 (2026-06-02, PR 2906, also the 'Descriptors are live' comment); `-S'reservation.commit()'` -> 2bae8c454b (2026-07-22, PR 3385). Wade wrote '#3928' in 3907214892; quote that as his attribution: the PR 3928 merge cb255d352d does not touch src/tron/gof.cpp.
6. For (a) across layers: `git -C WT show HEAD:README.code-org.md | sed -n '/Dependencies (aspirational)/,/^$/p'` ('Only tron/hardware should directly depend on pos/'). If the helper's header is in a layer the file must not include, the remedy is an `extern <signature>;` declaration (3016: Wade asked for it in device.cpp; the author put `namespace tron { extern bool fwd_hw_attn_enabled(); }` in h/libpos.hpp:29-31 (dca7ace69b), reached through h/pos/device.hpp:22, and src/pos/device.cpp:166 calls it at 39396c8728).
7. Report per candidate: new site file:line, owner file:line, the sites that already call the owner, the named difference (or 'none'), the smallest edit (call the helper; pass the stored member instead of the literal; one loop or `set_passes(passes, items)`; one dispatch helper for the copied sequence; never new infrastructure beyond the nearest helper). Add the step-1 counters: candidates per kind and drops per reason (2287: a=1 kept, b=0, c=1 dropped as comment line, d=0, e=0, f=5 dropped by body shape, g=8 dropped for no ordering comment, h=2 and i=4 dropped after reading the callee).

On PR 4596 (reviewed commit 0f784c44ff, BASE 66c7bb8db1): (a) one getenv added, `std::getenv("TRON_ATTN_STATS")` at h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:163; step 2 finds no other reader at HEAD or BASE, candidate cleared. (e) the diff adds `pool_worker` with body `return n_workers - n_attn_workers + attn_ix;` (attn_stats.hpp:431-435, prod.diff line 440); grep of the operands at HEAD h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp: inline `tp.num_workers() - n_attn_workers + worker_ix` at :797 (pre-existing at BASE :761, feeds `stats_ref.note_attn_job(pool_worker_ix, ...)` at :855 and the speedometer at :837), inline in a log string at :1498 (BASE :1396), helper calls at :1343 and :1485; named difference: none. Finding = Wade's 4147010638. At the commit he APPROVED, 441e81178b (2026-09-30T19:34Z), :856 calls `stats_ref.pool_worker(worker_ix, n_attn_workers)`, :797 stays for the speedometer at :837, and the log string at :1499 still spells the formula. (h)(i): 3 lines (attn_stats resize :386, :463; loop :1004), none a grow loop or a re-walked container.

On PR 2287 (reviewed commit 4274d5878a, BASE ba1bed266d, base hwattention_sync): (a) one hit, model.hpp:820 `if (have_devices && !getenv("TRON_DISABLE_HW_ATTN"))`; step 2 by stem HW_ATTN finds `fwd_hw_attn_enabled()` at hw_attn_config.hpp:17 with five callers at HEAD and at BASE; difference: the `have_devices` conjunct, kept at the fix 1a88e897e1:827.
