finals.label: type-and-initialization-choice

skill_entry.name: Declaration types and initializers: unsigned for counts, initialized struct locals, const literal globals, no redundant initializer sweeps
skill_entry.trigger: Production files (h/, src/), any one: (a) SIGNED COUNT: an added or re-added local, parameter, out-parameter or member of type int, int32_t, int64_t or long whose name carries a count word (count, cnt, blocks, bytes, size, _per, total, idx, index, num_, len), while the same quantity is unsigned at the reviewed commit: a producer, a sibling helper's parameter, the field it is stored to (in that field's header), or a `(uint64_t)(name` cast. (b) UNINITIALIZED STRUCT LOCAL: an added local of struct type with no initializer, the struct declared in the diff or in a header the diff touches, with no user-provided constructor. (c) MUTABLE LITERAL GLOBAL: an added UPPER_CASE namespace-scope variable initialized from a literal, with no const or constexpr. (d) INITIALIZER SWEEP: the PR body says it adds default member initializers across a struct.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. (a) Grep the diff for signed count declarations. Take names from the hits and line numbers from a full-file grep at the review commit (REV). Collect every type REV gives each name, the field the value is assigned to and that field's header type, and every `(uint64_t)(name` cast. A `< 0` or `= -1` use clears the name. Names declared together form one group; one unsigned anchor makes the whole group a finding. 2. (b) Print the struct at REV; count members with an initializer. Some missing: note a read after a loop that is the only writer. 3. (c) Grep writes, excluding the definition line; none: finding. 4. (d) Find the `new T` spelling and whether T has a user-provided constructor; state the rule from the standard. 5. Answer guideline questions with 'no written rule'. 6. Rerun 1 and 2 at every push.
skill_entry.question: Can this value ever legitimately be negative or change after startup, and does the code that produces, stores or consumes it already use the unsigned (or const, or initialized) form at the commit under review?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A pre-existing signed declaration left in place where the hunk only adds an initializer (PR 2193 5e2d19d362:h/pos/device.hpp:215,221). Scalar locals and scalar members without initializers (PR 2011 src/pos/driver.cpp:850-852, h/pos/dma/queue.hpp:45-46). A global initialized from a function call (src/pos/mwaitx.cpp:27). Mixed unsigned widths (17c6e0117d:src/pos/worker.cpp:1095-1100). A struct whose members all carry initializers at REV (Wade withdrew, 2790148917). A local whose struct lives in an untouched header or has a user-provided constructor (PR 3008 h/pos/regs.hpp locals; tron-3756 process_device_id). A class member of struct type. Constant spelling (check 13). Post the pattern once per group, not per line (PR 2011: two of four locals commented). Never block; approve while open.
skill_entry.finding_shape:
(a) Round 1, one prose comment on the declaration group: '`<name>` and `<siblings>` (<file>:<line>) are `int`; <anchor> at :<line> is `uint64_t`. never expected to be negative, right? wouldn't `uint64_t` make more sense? same for `<sibling>`?' Later push: one ```suggestion block per signed signature line that remains. (b) '```suggestion
  <T> <x> = {};
```
? (`<T>` at <header>:<line> has no default member initializers at <commit>; initializers in the struct are the alternative)'. (c) '```suggestion
const <type> <NAME> = <expr>;
```
that is... if we don't plan to ever change this value?'. (d) 'a bit pedantic: <T> has <no user-provided constructor, so `new T()` already zero-initializes | a user-provided constructor, so <members> are the only ones this covers>; being explicit is fine. Approved.'
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit or minor; his own words are 'these 3 variables below are never expected to be negative right?' (3430026641), 'a bit pedantic' (4125818552), a bare '?' after a suggestion block (2789725609), and 'that is... if we don't plan to ever change this value?' (2380221355). He approves while these stay open (PR 3008 approved 2026-06-18 after the three suggestion blocks were applied; PR 2438 approved in the same review that called it pedantic). 'kinda pedantic' (2789826297) is a different nit in PR 2011 about default parameter values and belongs to missing-explanation-at-declaration.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at the commit the review is on (REV: producer and consumer signatures, struct definition, writes to the global); callers in the same file; the header that declares the field the value is stored to (h/pos/device.hpp) and the struct definition (h/pos/device.hpp, h/pos/dma/queue.hpp); PR body for pattern (d) (the stated reason and 'values already set by constructor or init()'); no CI, no runtime.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check: declaration types and initializers

Placeholders: WT (worktree), N (PR number), HEAD (final head), REV (the commit the review is on; HEAD when reviewing the final head), BASE (see 0), FILE, HEADER, NAME, T.

0. BASE. For an open PR `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main`. For a merged PR take the merge commit M (`gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N -q .merge_commit_sha`) and use `git -C WT merge-base REV M^1`. Confirm `git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor BASE REV` exits 0 before any step. (`merge-base REV origin/main` returns REV itself once the PR is merged.)

1. Signed count declarations added by the diff:
   `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE REV -- src h | grep -E '^\+[^+].*\b(int|int32_t|int64_t|long)[ &]+([a-z_]*(count|cnt|blocks|bytes|size|total|idx|index)[a-z_]*|[a-z_]*_per(_[a-z_]*)?|num_[a-z_]*|len|[a-z_]*_len|len_[a-z_]*|[a-z_]*_len_[a-z_]*)\b'`
   Take only the NAMES from the hits. Take REV line numbers from the step-2 full-file grep; do not compute lines from `@@` headers (a 499-line hunk gave numbers 2 lines off).
   A hit counts as added when its declaration sits inside a function the PR creates or rewrites (the enclosing function has `+` or `-` lines in the -U0 diff, or the declaration is removed in one hunk and re-added in another: PR 3008 locals at BASE :1187-1192 reappear at REV :1693-1696 and Wade commented). A declaration left in place where only an initializer is added is the do-not-fire case (PR 2193 `int num_devices = 0`).
2. For each NAME, every type the file gives it:
   `git -C WT show REV:FILE | grep -n -E '\b(int|int32_t|int64_t|long|uint32_t|uint64_t|size_t)[& ]+NAME\b'`
   Cast anchors: `git -C WT show REV:FILE | grep -n -E '\(uint64_t\)\(NAME\b'` (every hit; PR 3008 has four).
   Field anchor: `git -C WT show REV:FILE | grep -n -E '\.[a-z_]+ = NAME;'`; take the field F from the hit, then `git -C WT grep -n -E '\b(uint32_t|uint64_t|size_t) F;' REV -- h`. A `return NAME;` in another function is not an anchor.
   Negative use (clears the row): `git -C WT show REV:FILE | grep -n -E 'NAME *(<|<=) *0|NAME *= *-1'`.
   Grouping: names declared in one out-parameter list or one consecutive block form a group. One unsigned anchor for any member makes the group the finding; name the anchored member first and the rest as siblings. The fix width is the anchor's width at round 1 (uint64_t from h/pos/device.hpp:139 on PR 3008) and the width the author already chose at a later round.
3. Uninitialized struct-typed locals added by the diff:
   `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE REV -- src h | grep -E '^\+\s+(struct )?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_:<>]*\s+[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*;\s*(//.*)?$' | grep -v -E '^\+\s*(return|co_return|throw|delete|goto|break|continue|using|typedef)\b' | grep -v -E '^\+\s+(std::|boost::)' | grep -v -E '\b(int|uint[0-9]+_t|int[0-9]+_t|size_t|bool|float|double)\s'`
   For each type T find its header: `git -C WT grep -l -E 'struct T\b|class T\b' REV -- h src`. Keep the line only when that header is in `git -C WT diff --name-only BASE REV` or T is declared in the diff, the line is a local (not inside a class body), T has no user-provided constructor (`grep -n -E '\bT\(' HEADER` inside the struct body is empty), and the local does not exist verbatim at BASE. Otherwise drop it (PR 3008: nine h/pos/regs.hpp register-field locals, header untouched, Wade silent).
   Struct at REV: `git -C WT show REV:HEADER | sed -n '/struct T {/,/^};/p' | grep -n -E '^\s+[A-Za-z_].*;'`; count members with an initializer (`=` or `{...}`) and without.
   Zero-iteration read: `git -C WT show REV:FILE | sed -n 'L1,L2p'` around the local; note whether the only writer is inside a `for`/`if` and a read follows it.
4. Mutable literal globals added by the diff:
   `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE REV -- src h | grep -E '^\+[A-Za-z0-9_:<>]+\s+[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+\s*=' | grep -v -E 'const|constexpr|\w+\([^)]*\);$'`
   Writes, definition line excluded first:
   `git -C WT grep -n -E '\bNAME\b' REV -- src h | grep -v -E '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:\s*[A-Za-z0-9_:<>]+\s+NAME\s*=' | grep -E 'NAME\s*(=[^=]|\+\+|--|\+=|-=)|&NAME\b'`
   A remaining assignment, increment, address-of or non-const reference argument is a write. Empty: finding. (PR 1485 at 08b5f10085: empty; uses :60 and :83 are `"a"(MWAIT_C0)` asm input operands.)
5. Initializer sweep (pattern d):
   `gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json title,body -q '.title + "\n" + .body' | grep -n -i -E '(add|default|explicit|consisten|safe)[^.]{0,80}initializ|initializ[^.]{0,80}(add|default|explicit|consisten|safe)'`
   A sentence that removes initializers (tron-2774 'removing runtime field initialization') does not trigger. Pattern (d) also needs an added count above zero:
   `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE REV -- HEADER | grep -c -E '^\+.*(= 0;|= false;|= nullptr;|= \{\};|= -1;)'`
   Creation spelling: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'new T\b' REV -- src h`; record `()`, `(args)` or nothing per hit. Constructor: `git -C WT show REV:HEADER | sed -n '/^  T(/,/{/p'`; a `T(...)` with a body or initializer list is user-provided.
   Rule to state: `new T()` value-initializes a class with no user-provided constructor, so every member is zero before default member initializers apply, with or without any such initializer. `new T` without parentheses default-initializes, so members without a default member initializer stay indeterminate. A class WITH a user-provided constructor runs it under either spelling; members neither in its initializer list nor given a default initializer stay indeterminate. Grade each added initializer redundant-but-harmless or needed; approve either way.
6. Guideline check: `git -C WT ls-tree --name-only REV AGENTS.md t/AGENTS.md .github/AGENTS.md ingest/AGENTS.md` first (git grep ignores a missing pathspec silently; at 40e4cea98609 only AGENTS.md and ingest/AGENTS.md exist), then `git -C WT grep -n -i -E 'initializ|unsigned' REV -- <files that exist>` (empty at 2026-10-06) and `grep -n -i -E 'unsigned|initializ' ~/.claude/skills/cpp-coding-guide/SKILL.md` (only the literal-0 line). Say 'no written rule'.
7. At every later push rerun steps 1 and 3 against the new REV: the author applies the ask to the locals and misses the helper signatures (PR 3008), or moves the fix into the struct (PR 2011); withdraw or narrow the finding accordingly.

On PR 3008 (merge commit 17c6e0117d; BASE dd5dd82caf for the review commits 40e4cea98609 and c68ea87f48, BASE 8811bdd35f for the final head): at 40e4cea98609 step 1 lists 22 src/pos/worker.cpp lines: block_layout members :1083-1086, compute_block_layout :1096-1098, `int pad_per` :1103, new helper out-parameters :1118-1121 and :1240-1242, fill_rxinfo :1480, write_rx_descriptors :1506-1507, locals :1693-1696 (`int expected_blocks = 0; int res_per_block = 0; int res_bytes_per_block = 0; int64_t pad_bytes = 0;`, re-added from BASE :1187-1192). Step 2 adds the pre-existing producers :565-568 and :750-752 (`int&`, `int64_t&`, present at BASE as :558-561 and :743-745), the field anchor :1492 `rx_entry.results_per_block = res_per_block;` -> h/pos/device.hpp:139 `uint64_t results_per_block;`, the casts :1519, :1524, :1532, :1555; no negative use; the group of four locals is the round-1 finding (3430026641). At c68ea87f48 step 1 lists exactly :1481 `int res_per_block,` :1507 `int res_bytes_per_block,` :1508 `int64_t pad_bytes) {` (3437522787, 3437526764, 3437527579). At 17c6e0117d step 1 is empty. Step 3 at 40e4cea98609 lists nine h/pos/regs.hpp locals, all dropped (header untouched, present at BASE). On PR 2011 (BASE ab75e61d83, REV e091f3f799): step 3 lists h/pos/hwattention.hpp :502, :578, :627, :657 `dma_xfer_state`; the keyword filter removes seven `return` lines; the struct at e091f3f799:h/pos/device.hpp:187-196 has 0 of 5 members initialized (finding, :627 read at :646 after the `for` at :635); at d4795f37a5 (commit c2d72e6a7f) 5 of 5 (withdraw). On PR 1485 (08b5f10085): step 4 lists src/pos/mwaitx.cpp:16 `uint32_t MWAIT_C0 = (0xF << 4);`, write grep empty (finding), :27 `bool MWAITX_SUPPORTED = is_supported();` filtered. On PR 2438 (fc4fc8780a, merge-base 9ebe06083e): step 5 counts 50 added initializers in h/pos/device.hpp, `new PosDevice(index++, ...` at src/pos/device.cpp:72, user-provided constructor at h/pos/device.hpp:340-356 (idx, enqueued_work, dequeued_work, pci_*, iommu_group, vfio_fd(-1), regions(), allocator_), so the explicit initializers are the only guarantee for the members the constructor and init() do not set. Silent corpus (15 diffs): step 1 lists tron-1707 src/pos/fake.cpp:160 `int idx` and tron-4353 h/tron/models/model.hpp:2877 `int64_t total`, both cleared by step 2; steps 3, 4, 5 list nothing after the filters.

Width when siblings disagree (uint32_t vs uint64_t) has no corpus precedent; the procedure takes the anchor's width.
The step-4 definition-line exclusion assumes the global is defined on one line with the type immediately before NAME; a definition split across lines would count as a write and suppress the finding.
Dates in precedent_note come from the digests (review timestamps); 2941290531's own timestamp was not read, the PR 2193 review range 2026-03-16 is assumed.

finals.label: identifier-name-states-role

skill_entry.name: 14. An identifier states its role (members, parameters, flags, functions, labels)
skill_entry.trigger: The diff adds or renames a member, parameter, flag, function or label, and one holds. (a) Generic last token (layers, data) while the removed line or comment names the quantity. (b) The trailing comment qualifies with the identifier's kind of token but another value (per-Q versus per_b). (c) A one-to-three-letter parameter, neither a word nor role-typed, abbreviating a name the body or call site uses, ten times its hits at BASE. (d) Two flags share a stem and gate different `if` lines, or a member shares a constructor parameter's name. (e) An absolute word (indefinitely, once) bounded by a body operand, or a phase word (prepare, launch) with a differently-phased callee. (f) A workflow label cased unlike repository labels sharing a word.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. BASE: when `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD (merged PR), use the merge-base of HEAD and the merge commit's first parent; never `<commit>~1`. Map every added line to file:HEADline with the awk command (procedures.md). 2. Bin added lines: trailing-comment declarations, `-`/`+` member pairs, bool or counter locals, signatures with one-to-three-letter parameters, absolute or phase words, `_untraced|_impl|_inner`, `labels.*.name`. 3. Per bin compare the name with: comment qualifiers (prefix and standard abbreviations match); removed tokens; same-stem siblings and their `if` lines; BASE whole-word counts (a short-name hit naming another quantity counts zero); the whole function for a bounding operand; the header access label for a wrapper split; the repository label list (network). 4. Report the proposed name in a suggestion block.
skill_entry.question: Reading only the identifier at its use site, can a reader tell what it holds, which event it is the first of, or what the function does, and does the name agree with its own trailing comment, with the names beside it in the same scope, and with the spelling the rest of the code base uses for the same quantity?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A name the diff only moves (B, MAX_B, tok_ix on PR 2287). A token with ten or more hits at BASE (tok_ix, idx, `_q`) is a convention; only (b) fires on it. A comment that expands or defines the identifier (gqa, tron-1707). A parameter whose type names the role (process_device_id), a word (pos, key), a forwarding lambda, both spellings new in the PR (q_lo, tron-4353), four-or-more-letter abbreviations. A local caching a same-named accessor. A name stating one of several guards. A wrapper split whose private header declaration shows callers inherit tracing (3769729340). A move named in the body or a reply (3001991780). The author's rename spelling. Constants (13), test names (5), typos, formatting, data files, mechanical renames.
skill_entry.finding_shape: "`<name>` (<file:line>) <holds | gates | is> <what the comment, the removed names or the body say>, but the name only says <generic noun | per_b | first>; <the comment says '<word>' | `<sibling>` at :<line> already gates <other thing> | the call site passes `<long name>`>. <Nit | a bit of a nit>: `<proposed name>`?" with a ```suggestion block when the fix is one line. For a behavior word: "this function is named '<word>' but <bounding statement at :<line>> means it <does not>, right? Should the name or the comment change?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit to minor, never blocking: 'a bit of a nit, but I prefer to see more descriptive param names ;)' (2897235803), 'definitely a nit' (3001991780), 'just a trivial nit' (3580238651), 'IMHO' (3769684790), 'I would prefer something like' (2982403509). He approves while the rename is open (PR 2103 approved at 20:13:01 after the 20:12:13 comment; PR 3302 approved 94 s after the comment). A name that contradicts the function's behavior is still a question, framed as learning ('newby-probe here :)', 2380263378), normal severity.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (the enclosing function or struct at HEAD, the header declaration for a wrapper split); other files (the call site, the dominant spelling at BASE over h and src, sibling workflow files); network for the repository label list (`gh label list`); the instruction reference for an instruction operand (AMD APM vol. 3, MWAITX). PR body and replies only to learn of a planned move. Not commits, CI or runtime.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: an identifier states its role

Common setup for this check. `base_ref=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.ref)`. When `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$base_ref` prints HEAD itself, the PR is merged: `git -C WT log --merges --format='%H %P %s' origin/$base_ref | grep <PR head>` gives the merge commit, and `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD <first parent of that merge commit>)`. Never use `<commit>~1` as BASE (on PR 3302, 57368de081~1 is the PR commit before the merged head and already holds the new workflow file). On PR 2089: base_ref hwattention_sync, merge commit 1794cdf67d, first parent b618bda79a, BASE 97f0f99674 for HEAD 57af5033da.

1. Added lines mapped to HEAD: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src .github/workflows | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3); next} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); n=a[2]-1; next} /^\+/{n++; print f":"n": "$0}' > added.txt` (one line per added line, `file:HEADline: +text`; 1024 lines on PR 2089, gof.hpp:79 and gof.cpp:55 verified against `git show`). Bin before reading anything: (b) declarations with a trailing comment `grep -E '\w+\s*(\{\}|= [^;]*)?;\s*//' added.txt` -> step 2; (a)/(d) a `-` member line and a `+` member line in one hunk of a header -> step 3; (d) `grep -E '\+\s*(bool|int|size_t|uint32_t|uint64_t)\s+\w+\s*(=|\{|;)' added.txt` -> step 4; (c) `grep -E '\w+\s*\(.*\)\s*(noexcept|\{|const|;)' added.txt | grep -E '\b(const\s+)?[A-Za-z_:<>]+[*&]?\s+[a-z]{1,3}\s*[,)]'` -> step 5 (8 lines on PR 2089, gof_configure twice among them); (e) `grep -E '\b\w*(indefinitely|forever|never|always|once|all|every|traced|untraced|prepare|launch)\w*\s*\(' added.txt` -> step 6; `grep -E '_(untraced|impl|inner)\s*\(' added.txt` -> step 7; `grep -E 'labels\.\*\.name|label\.name' added.txt` -> step 8.
2. Name versus own comment. Split the identifier on `_`; list the comment's qualifiers (per-X, k/v, tx/rx, first/last, HBM/host, count/base; examples, not a closed list). A comment word matches an identifier token when the token equals it, is a prefix of it of two or more letters, or is a standard abbreviation (tok/token, ix/idx/index, dev/device, hw/hardware, q/query, kv/k/v). Flag only when a comment qualifier and an identifier token are of the same kind and differ (per-Q against per_b). Skip when every comment noun expands a token, states what the flag gates, or names who uses the member (tron-1707 device.hpp attn_req, tok_ix, bypass_read_q; driver.hpp gqa; PR 2089 shard.hpp:28 `base_tok_ix // first token index`: all approved with no text).
3. Name versus removed names: for a `-`/`+` pair in one struct, `diff <(echo '<old ids>' | tr '_' '\n') <(echo '<new id>' | tr '_' '\n')`; a specific token the `+` identifier dropped and the `+` comment kept is the finding, and the proposed name restores it.
4. Name versus siblings. For each bin-(d) local take the first `_`-token as the stem; `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk 'NR>=A && NR<=B'` for the enclosing function, then `grep -nE '\b<stem>\w*\b'` and `grep -nE 'if \(<stem>\w*\)'` inside the range. Compare only pairs where both names are read in an `if (` line and gate different statements. For a member: `grep -n '<struct>(' <header>` and `git -C WT grep -n '<struct>::<struct>(' HEAD -- src` for a constructor parameter of the same name holding another thing. Two counters whose second tokens state distinct roles (dma_start / dma_done) are not a pair; a local that caches a same-named accessor (kv_cache.hpp v_ptr, tron-2693) or views a longer-named parameter (plan / plan_state, tron-4353) is not a pair.
5. Name versus repository spelling, the gate for (c). Exclude first: a dictionary word (pos, key, len), a type that names the role (process_device_id, std::shared_ptr<node_base>), a lambda or forwarding function of three lines or fewer that passes its parameters unchanged (model.hpp:773-778 on PR 2089, silent), four-or-more-letter abbreviations (n_kvheads, didx, dlen on tron-1722, silent). Then `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'A,Bp'` for the body (`<field> = <param>`, log strings) and `git -C WT grep -n '<fn>(' HEAD -- h src` for the call site arguments. Count at BASE: `for w in <short...> <long...>; do printf '%s ' $w; git -C WT grep -w -c "$w" BASE -- h src | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END{print s+0}'; done`. A short-name hit at BASE that names another quantity (hs = heap_start at src/pos/driver.cpp:738-746) counts as zero. Stop unless the long form has at least ten times the short form's hits; both spellings new in the PR (q_lo/q_hi against q_begin/q_end on tron-4353, 0 versus 0) do not fire. Report the long names in one suggestion block.
6. Name versus behavior (needs the instruction reference; cite the manual section or write Insufficient data). `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'A,Bp'` for the whole function; `grep -nE 'timeout|options|break|return|while|for \(|SUPPORTED'` inside the range. For an instruction operand cite AMD APM vol. 3, MWAITX: ECX bit 1 enables the EBX timeout in TSC cycles. Quote two inline comments on one statement that contradict each other. A name that states one of several guards (coalesce_if_unpinned_single_child, tron-2875) does not fire. For a phase word: `git -C WT grep -n '<callee>(' HEAD -- h src` to list the chain, then `grep -n -i -E 'scheduler|follow-up|later PR|moved' body.md` and the thread replies for a planned move.
7. Wrapper split: after the `_(untraced|impl|inner)` grep require `git -C WT show BASE:<file> | grep -n '<public name>\s*('` to find the old body under the public name at BASE; a helper with no BASE occurrence (on_save_impl, gof.cpp:208 on PR 2089) is new, not a split. Then `git -C WT show HEAD:<header> | grep -n -B3 '<name>_untraced'` and read whether it sits under `private:`; `git -C WT grep -n '<name>(' HEAD -- h src t` lists the callers that inherit the wrapper. Private body plus public name on the wrapper: stop.
8. Label strings (needs network): `git -C WT grep -n -E 'labels\.\*\.name|label\.name' BASE -- .github/workflows`; `gh label list --repo positron-ai/tron --limit 200 | grep -i <word>`; `grep -n '<new string>' <new workflow file>` to confirm every site spells it the same.

On PR 2089 (HEAD 57af5033da, BASE 97f0f99674): step 1 bin (c) lists src/tron/gof.cpp:55 `void gof_configure(size_t nk, size_t nh, size_t hs, float scalar)`; step 5 body :57-59 assigns `gof_params.kv_head_size = hs; gof_params.n_kv_heads = nk; gof_params.n_heads = nh;`, log :64 prints `n_kv_heads={} n_heads={} head_size={}`, call site h/tron/models/model.hpp:761 passes `n_kv_heads, n_heads, head_size`; counts at BASE: n_kv_heads 202, n_heads 92, head_size 383 versus nk 0, nh 0, hs 4 (all four heap_start, counted zero); at HEAD the 13 nk hits are the PR's own files; Wade's suggestion block 2897235803 = the long names; applied in de3bb7c7 gof.cpp:55.

On PR 2287 (open head 1a88e897e1): step 2 hit h/pos/device.hpp:85 `std::array<size_t, tron::hardware::MAX_B> tok_ix_per_b{};  // per-Q token indices`; qualifier per-Q against token per_b, same kind, different value; :84 `tok_ix  // legacy single-Q path`; MAX_B pre-existing at h/libpos.hpp:35 and bounding device.hpp:60, 61, 92, 138; Wade asked for `tok_ix_per_q` (3075717295); no reply.

On PR 2103 (021072570b): step 4 src/pos/driver.cpp:910 `bool first = true;` and :911 `bool firstcheck = true;` in wait_for_xfer_blocks; `firstcheck` gates check_for_tsc_errs at :932-935, `first` gates the 'DMA XFER saw wait time' log at :939-942; suggestion `first_tsccheck` (2842854014); head b1c1523c27 :911 `bool firsttsccheck = true;`; the `first` flag in readback_check (:852, gating :868-871) drew no comment.

On PR 3302 (dd07038737): step 8 `gh label list` (read 2026-10-06) returns `benchmark`, `bench-experiment` (lower case) beside `Skip benchmarks`, `Continuous integration`, `Run CI`, `Intel`; workflow siblings at the PR commit before the head are 'Run CI' (5 sites) and 'Continuous integration' (test-release-build.yml:16), all cased like 'Benchmark only', so the repository label list is the comparison set that reproduces 3580238651; fixed to 'dev-benchmark-only' at 57368de081 lines 6, 16, 34, 36.

finals.label: missing-explanation-at-declaration

skill_entry.name: 14. Explanation at the declaration: a new parameter, environment variable, routine, test-only helper, moved default or term must be explained where a reader meets it
skill_entry.trigger: (a) New parameter with a default or hedge-word name, absent from the leading comment at HEAD, hedge-named or never left at its default by any caller. (b) New getenv("VAR") read, absent at BASE, named nowhere else at HEAD. (c) New 20+ line function, absent at BASE, no comment above it; or an uncommented new t/ file. (d) Touched header function with only t/ callers, forwarding a parameter every production callee call passes as one constant, doc block silent. (e) src/ definition drops a default kept in the header, comment silent. (f) Design-spec prose introduces a quoted or bold term at first occurrence, no glossary row, link or gloss. (g) Prose demotes a document ('superseded', 'legacy') without deletion or retirement plan.
skill_entry.procedure: 1 Parameters: grep added defaulted parameters; grep the leading comment at HEAD for the name; hedge-word check; read callers' arguments. 2 Env vars: grep added getenv reads; drop ones read at BASE; grep HEAD for another mention. 3 Routines: `+` definitions absent at BASE, uncommented; brace-count bodies; fire once per PR, largest, nit. 4 Test-only helpers: classify callers of touched header functions; for an all-t/ helper read its `return CALLEE(` line and what production passes there. 5 Moved defaults: pair `-`/`+` definition lines; confirm the header holds it; grep the definition comment. 6 Terms: first occurrence versus hunk line, glossary, doc-tree link. 7 Superseded documents: grep the status section for a retirement plan. 8 One finding per candidate, at the declaration.
skill_entry.question: If a reader opens only this file at HEAD, can they learn what the new thing is for, when it applies and why it has this shape (why a 'hint', why a parameter production never varies, what the variable's format and default are, where the term is defined), without opening the PR thread?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A plain bug fix needs no Note; the ask is a short comment, never a Note (3866668853 questioned one). A parameter the doc block already covers. A plain-named defaulted parameter some caller leaves at its default (tron-4353 q_begin, q_end). A getenv read named by a comment, assertion message or log line (tron-4353, tron-2475). A moved, renamed or converted function; a self-describing member (debug_string); helpers under 20 lines, lambdas, fixtures. A test-only helper whose callee takes a variable in production (xfer_v_entry, silent in PR 4007 and tron-3756). Zero-caller symbols: dead-symbol check. A dereferenced hedge-word parameter: identifier-name check. An env var no wrapper forwards: observability check. A stale comment: comment-contradicts-code. README, comment and shell-help terms (tron-1727). Document structure, renames, comment-only PRs.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Code: "can we document `<name>` (e.g. why is it a '<hedge word>' / why it keeps `<param>` when production always passes `<CONSTANT>` / how to use `<VAR>`, its format and default)? a reader of <file> alone cannot tell; a short comment at <the declaration | definition | read> would do." Test-only helper: "this `<helper>` is a UT-only utility function (only caller t/<file>:<line>). We should document that clearly, as well as the fact that it purposely uses `<param>` rather than `<CONSTANT>`." Prose: "first mention of '<term>'... is there a link/reference pointer to where this is better described (e.g. how it's enabled/disabled/driven)?" Document: "what is our retirement plan for <older doc>? It's confusing to come across multiple specs in multiple locations."
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit when he says so himself: 'I know this is a pretty simple routine, but I'm a fan of comments :)' (3036997452), 'kinda pedantic' (2789826297). minor is the default: a lowercase question with one reason ('can we document `kv_hint` (e.g. why is it a 'hint' :-p)?', ''erased'?'), and approval is not withheld (docs-51 approved three minutes after the ask, 16:54:17Z to 16:57:13Z on 2026-08-25; PR 2302 approved 37 seconds after the ask, 3036997452 at 15:32:55Z, APPROVED at 15:33:32Z on 2026-04-05). normal only for the retirement-plan case, where the reason is the cost to newcomers ('It's confusing (esp. for newer folks)'). Never blocking; he approved every member PR.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk + full file at HEAD (the leading comment block, the glossary section, the status or roadmap section) + callers (`git grep` over h src t bin ingest at HEAD, classified production versus t/) + BASE (is the function, variable or parameter new) + other files (the header declaration for a moved default; README and doc/ for an environment variable; the callee's production callers for a forwarded parameter) + prior PR and branches for a superseded document (`gh api .../branches`, open PRs). PR body only to confirm a documented claim (PR 4007 body: 'Two helpers / carry doc comments answering questions raised in review', split over a line break). Not commits, not CI, not runtime.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: explanation at the declaration

Common setup additions (apply to every check): for a review commit already merged, `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself and pr.diff is empty. Use the first-parent main commit that is an ancestor of HEAD: `for c in $(git -C WT log --first-parent --format=%H -n 400 origin/main); do git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor $c HEAD && { BASE=$c; break; }; done` (PR 4007 at 29a39ac33e: BASE 21162f5568, pr.diff 282 lines, 4 files). The installed awk is mawk 1.3.4, which has no `\s`; write `[[:space:]]` in every awk and grep pattern.

Trigger detail. (a) A `+` line inside a parameter list (previous diff line of the hunk ends with `,` or `(`) that carries a default value or a hedge word in the name (hint, tmp, temp, opt, maybe, hack); the function's leading comment block at HEAD does not name the parameter; and either the name carries a hedge word or no caller at HEAD under h, src or t leaves the argument at its default. (b) A `+` line reads getenv("VAR") where no `-` line of the same hunk reads VAR and no file at BASE reads it, and `git grep -w VAR HEAD` finds no comment, README, doc, log-format string or assertion message naming VAR outside the read. (c) A function definition of 20 or more lines (brace-depth count) whose definition line is a `+` line, whose name and first body line are absent at BASE (not moved, renamed or converted from a TEST_CASE), and whose nearest preceding line that is not blank, a `#` directive, a `template <...>` line or an attribute macro (`TRON(...)`, `[[...]]`) is not a comment; or a new file under t/ with zero `//` lines. (d) The diff adds a header function, or changes a parameter it forwards, whose every call site outside its own definition and doc block is under t/, and the helper forwards a parameter to a callee that every production caller under h or src passes as one named constant, and the doc block neither says test-only, UT-only or not production nor names that constant. (e) A definition in src/ drops a default (`-` line with `= value`, `+` line and continuation lines without) because the default now lives in the header declaration, and the doc comment above the definition does not state the default. (f) A prose hunk in a design specification (docs/ or doc/ of a specification repository, or a tron doc/ design note) introduces a quoted, bold or capitalised term whose first occurrence in the file at HEAD is inside the hunk, with no glossary row, link or parenthetical definition before or at that line. (g) A prose hunk says an existing document 'is no longer the authority', 'remain(s)', 'superseded', 'deprecated' or 'legacy' and neither deletes it nor turns it into a pointer nor states a retirement plan.

1. Parameters: `grep -n -E '^\+[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_:<>*&]+ [A-Za-z_0-9]+ = [^,;()]+(,|\)[^;{]*\{)$' pr.diff`; keep a hit only when the previous diff line of the same hunk ends with `,` or `(` (inside a parameter list); do not exclude by type name (`size_t q_begin = 0,` is a parameter); discard shell lines (`exit 2`, `shift 2`) and `struct X {`. Map each to FILE:LINE through the `@@` headers. Leading comment block: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | head -n $((LINE-1)) | tac | awk '/^[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*|\/\*)/ {print; next} NF {exit}' | tac | grep -c NAME` (0 = candidate). Hedge word: `echo NAME | grep -E 'hint|tmp|temp|opt|maybe|hack'`. Use in the body: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -E "\bNAME\b"` (an `if (NAME &&` guard means optional; `->` or `*NAME` means required). Callers: `git -C WT grep -n -A6 'FUNCTION(' HEAD -- h src t | grep -v "FILE:LINE"`; read the argument in that position at each call; drop the hit when the name has no hedge word and at least one caller omits the argument.
2. Environment variables: `grep -n -E '^\+.*getenv\("([A-Z0-9_]+)"' pr.diff`; drop VAR when a `-` line of the same hunk reads it (re-spelled read) or `git -C WT grep -c 'getenv("VAR")' BASE -- h src t bin` hits a file other than FILE (pre-existing variable; PR 2302 TRON_LOG_LEVEL). Then `git -C WT grep -n -w VAR HEAD -- README*.md doc h src t bin | grep -v 'getenv("VAR")'` (0 hits = candidate; a comment, a log-format string or an assertion message counts as a mention). Record the parse at the read line (`stoul(..., 0)` = any base, default value, bound).
3. Uncommented routines: `for f in $(grep -E '^(h|src|t)/' prfiles.txt); do git -C WT show HEAD:$f | awk -v F=$f '/^(static |inline |template)?[A-Za-z_:<>*&, ]+ [A-Za-z_0-9:]+\(.*\)[^;]*\{$/ && $0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*:/ && prev !~ /^[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*|\*\/|\/\*)/ {print F":"NR": "$0} {if ($0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*$/ && $0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*(TRON\(|template[[:space:]]*<|\[\[|#)/) prev=$0}'; done` (constructor initializer lines and attribute, template and directive lines are skipped). Keep a hit only when its definition line is a `+` line in pr.diff, the name is absent at BASE (`git -C WT show BASE:FILE | grep -c 'NAME('` = 0), the signature is on no `-` line of pr.diff, and the first body line is absent at BASE (`git -C WT show BASE:FILE | grep -c -F 'FIRST_BODY_LINE'` = 0; this removes moves and TEST_CASE conversions). Body length by brace count: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=LINE 'NR>=L {n++; d+=gsub(/\{/,"{"); d-=gsub(/\}/,"}"); if (d>0) seen=1; if (seen && d==0) {print n; exit}}'` (keep >= 20). New file: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -c '^[[:space:]]*//'` (0 = no comment in the file). Fire once per PR on the largest; nit.
4. Test-only header functions: `awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} /^@@/ && f ~ /^a\/h\// {print f": "$0}' pr.diff | sed 's/@@.*@@//' | sort -u`; drop context lines that start with struct, class, public:, private:, static const or contain `=`. For a hunk whose context is a struct, scan upward from the hunk's new-side start line for the nearest member signature: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v S=START 'NR<=S && /^  [A-Za-z_].*\) *(const)? *(noexcept)? *\{$/ {n=NR; s=$0} END {print n": "s}'` (k_hwcacheblock::xfer for the :461 hunk on PR 4007). Per NAME: `git -C WT grep -n -E "\bNAME\(" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v -E "HEADER:(DEFLINE|DOCLINE)"`; all remaining hits under t/ = test-only; zero hits outside the function's own file = dead code, record for the dead-symbol check (3866653656 'dead file'), do not fire here. Doc block: `git -C WT show HEAD:HEADER | sed -n 'DOCSTART,DEFLINEp' | grep -E '\b(UT|[Tt]est|[Tt]est-only|[Pp]roduction)\b'` (no `-i`; `-i` on UT matches input, output, without). Forwarded call: `git -C WT show HEAD:HEADER | sed -n 'DEFLINE,/^}/p' | grep -n -E 'return [A-Za-z_]+\('` gives CALLEE and the forwarded argument list; `git -C WT grep -n -A3 'CALLEE(' HEAD -- h src` lists production calls; read the argument in each forwarded position by hand. Fire only when every production call passes one named constant in a forwarded position (PR 4007: HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE from k_hwcacheblock::xfer). Otherwise pass silently (xfer_v_entry at 29a39ac33e and 7206e88cc2: callee shuffle_v_entry takes kv_head_size at production calls :598/:619 and :620/:641). Never report a sibling helper Wade passed as a second finding.
5. Moved defaults: `grep -n -E '^-[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_:<>*&]+ [A-Za-z_0-9]+ = (nullptr|false|true|0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+)\)? *(noexcept)? *\{' pr.diff` (a typed parameter line, not an `if` or `for` line); keep a hit only when the paired `+` line and its continuation lines carry no `=` default and `git -C WT grep -n -A8 'FUNCTION(' HEAD -- h` shows the default in the header declaration. Definition comment: the step 1 tac/awk block over SRCFILE at DEFLINE piped to `grep -i -E 'default|OPTIONAL'` (0 = candidate). Remedy = a comment line at the definition (C++ allows a default argument once per scope); nit.
6. Terms: `awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} (f ~ /\.(md|txt)$/ || /^\+[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*)/) && /^\+/' pr.diff | grep -E "(^|[ (])'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z -]+'([ ,.)]|$)|\*\*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z /-]+\*\*"`; skip a line whose quotes are possessives (`'s `). Only files under docs/ or doc/ of a specification repository, or a tron doc/ design note, count; README usage notes, code comments and shell help text do not. Per TERM: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -i -w "TERM" | head -3` (first occurrence versus hunk line); `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -i '^#.*gloss'` then grep that range for TERM; `git -C WT grep -n -i -l "TERM" HEAD -- doc docs README*.md`. First occurrence in the hunk, no glossary row, no link = candidate. For a repository outside WT: `gh api "repos/ORG/REPO/contents/PATH?ref=HEAD" --jq .content | base64 -d > spec.md` and run the same greps on spec.md.
7. Superseded documents: `awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} (f ~ /\.md$/ || f ~ /\/doc/ || /^\+[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*)/) && /^\+/' pr.diff | grep -n -i -E 'no longer (the )?(stated )?authority|superseded|deprecated|legacy|remain(s)? (on|in|but)|older (doc|spec|model)'`; an identifier such as `legacy_attention_storage_schedule()` does not count. Per document: `git -C WT ls-files DOC`; `gh api repos/ORG/REPO/branches --jq '.[].name'` for branch-only drafts; `gh pr list --repo ORG/REPO --search DOC`; then `grep -n -i -E 'retire|tombstone|delete|remove|close(s)? (PR|#)' spec.md` inside the status or roadmap section (0 = candidate).
8. One finding per candidate, phrased as a question at the declaration line, the read, the definition or the first use; remedy = comment, @param line, glossary row, link or roadmap row. Never a Note, never a code change.

finals.label: index-count-or-wait-set-mismatch

skill_entry.name: 14. A count, index or completion wait must cover the set it stands for
skill_entry.trigger: Added h/ or src/ lines: (a) A count (`v.size()`, `a * b`) bounds a loop or index into a compile-time-capacity member (`std::array<T, CAP>`, `T[CAP]`). (b) A `break` in an array-filling loop while a caller-read count (out-parameter or returned member) was set before the loop from the full input. (c) A helper's returned or out value starts as a sentinel (`0`, `nullptr`), is set in one arm of an explicit if/else or request-kind split, and its comment names the value. (d) A wait after a per-device loop names one device by a literal (`get_device(0)`) or carries a comment claiming it covers the loop. (e) A literal device index (`get_device(0)`, `(*pos_list_devices())[0]`) chooses a new object's device on a path every configuration runs.
skill_entry.procedure: (a) CAP from the struct; `git grep` every writer; from assignment to first indexed write record assert, clamp, return or NONE. (b) Each `break` path must reset the pre-loop count from the fill index; find its caller. (c) List out-value assignments with conditions; input classes from explicit branches or request kinds only; find a class that skips all and its consumer. (d) Read the function, the per-iteration callee (its device or queue) and the wait definition (what the completion check reads); compare the comment. (e) Grep other choosers of the object and tp2/tp4 aliases. For `<= (x / n) * n` evaluate at x = n; ask for a diag test. Grep replies for deferrals.
skill_entry.question: On every path, does this count, index or wait cover exactly the set it stands for (the array's capacity, every device the loop issued work to, the device this object binds to, the value its comment promises), and if not, which member is missed and who reads the result?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A count every writer asserts or clamps against CAP. A `break` path that resets the count from the fill index. A wait on the loop's last handle (PR 1722, silent), a one-queue loop whose comment names the member it ends on (PR 2008 'we always end on pdc 31'), or stated FIFO order. A sentinel the consumer tests before reading. A loop bound that is a model or device dimension. A `[0]` in a fake path or reading a property of an already-selected object. A line re-spelled from BASE. A written deferral: report once, accept. Token-index waits: concurrency check; two-count containers without compile-time capacity: state-ownership check. Never recompute kernel arithmetic, dispute CAP, run the test yourself, or block.
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<count|index|wait>` at <file:line> comes from <source>, but <the array|the loop at :<line>|the object> is <capacity CAP | one transfer per device through `<callee>` | bound to one device>, and nothing between :<source> and :<use> ensures <count <= CAP | every device is waited | index 0 is right under TP2/TP4>. Wait only: the definition at <file:line> reads `<handle member>`, not its device argument, so N-1 devices are never waited; the comment at :<line> says '<quote>'. As is, <the caller `<fn>` reads the wrong `<count>` | we wait on `<member>` only>. <check `<count> <= CAP`? | wouldn't it be better to capture the device per iteration and wait on each? | perhaps a quick diag test with <boundary input>?>
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal, with no label word; his own phrasings are an imperative ('something somewhere should ensure that `nshards` is <= `MAX_B`', 'check `work_req->nshards <= MAX_B`'), a fact-then-'As is' consequence with a two-alternative question ('wouldn't it be better to ... As is, we aren't actually waiting ...'), an endorsement of a bot finding that separates today's behaviour from the mechanism ('I do think there's merit to this complaint. Not sure it has to do with your current behavior ... but for sure ...'), and an admission plus a test ask when reading cannot settle it ('hard to truly analyze visually... perhaps a quick diag test would be worth it'). A relayed LLM item keeps the tool's own label ('**1. Low**'). He approved two of the four member PRs: PR 2011 at d4795f37a5 (2026-02-10T20:39:02Z, 28 minutes after the author's deferral reply) and PR 3008 at 17c6e0117d (2026-06-18T18:58:35Z). On PR 2233 he only commented (bham0n approved d634595662 on 2026-03-27; merged 2026-03-30 as merge commit 2bcd7f250e). PR 2287 is still open with no approval. Both PR 2011 sites were left unchanged at head with the author's written deferral. He never requested changes on any of the four.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk + full file at HEAD (the whole function around the loop, the wait or the helper) + other files (the struct that declares the array and its capacity constant; the definition of the wait call and the per-iteration callee that names the device or queue; the consumer of the out-value) + callers (the function that reads the out-parameter or the returned struct) + repository evidence of multi-device configurations (tp2/tp4 executor aliases in h/tron/models/common.hpp) + author replies (a written deferral). Runtime only as an ask to the author for an exact-boundary case; the reviewer does not run it.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a count, index or completion wait must cover the set it stands for

Setup addition (BASE for a PR whose base branch is not main, or that has merged): `BASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha)`. `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD itself once the PR is merged into that branch, and `origin/main` gives a base weeks too old (PR 2011: 16aeb26d83 instead of ab75e61d83). Offline: the second parent's base from the PR's merge commit (`git -C WT log --format=%P -1 <merge commit>`) or the digest header. Note that an open PR's base.sha moves with the base branch (PR 2287 answers 9b6988c009 today; the review was run at 5f37572171).

Mapping a `-U0` diff hit to a HEAD line (the installed awk is mawk and rejects `match(s, re, arr)`; use python):
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src > pr-u0.diff
python3 -I - < pr-u0.diff <<'EOF'
import re,sys
f=None;n=0
for i,l in enumerate(sys.stdin,1):
    m=re.match(r"^@@ -\S+ \+(\d+)",l)
    if l.startswith("+++ "): f=l[6:].strip()
    elif m: n=int(m.group(1))
    elif l.startswith("+"): print(i,f+":"+str(n)); n+=1
EOF
```
Read the row whose first number equals the grep line number (PR 2011: 350 -> h/pos/hwattention.hpp:645, 364 -> :674).

1. Candidates (five patterns) from the added lines of h/ and src/:
   (a) `grep -nE '^\+.*[a-z_]+ *= *[a-z_]+\.size\(\)|^\+.*(num|n)_?[a-z_]* *= *[0-9a-z_]+ \* [a-z_]+' pr-u0.diff`
       then `grep -nE 'std::array<[^>]*, *[A-Za-z_:0-9]+>|\[[A-Z_][A-Z_0-9]*\]' pr-u0.diff` for fixed-capacity members in the touched structs. Keep a count only when a later added loop, memcpy or index uses it against such a member; allocation sizes (`xferlen = a * b`) are not candidates.
   (b) `grep -nE '^\+\s*break;' pr-u0.diff` plus `grep -nE '^\+\s*(early_release|early_exit|release_early)\b' pr-u0.diff`; keep a hit only when the enclosing loop writes `arr[idx++]` or `arr[w_idx]` and a count set above the loop is read after it. Plain `return` statements of helpers are not candidates (42 hits over 12 silent diffs, all plain returns).
   (c) `grep -nE '^\+\s*(uint(8|16|32|64)_t|int|size_t|auto) +[a-z_]+ *= *(0|-1|nullptr|std::numeric_limits)[^x0-9]' pr-u0.diff`; drop struct default member initializers (the enclosing `@@` context names a `struct`) and default parameter values (the line ends with `)`, `,` or `) noexcept;`). Keep a hit only if the same function returns the name or stores it into a returned or by-reference struct: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk '/<helper signature>/,/^}/' | grep -nE 'return .*<name>|\.<field> *= *<name>|return \{.*<name>'`.
   (d) `grep -nE '^\+\s*[a-zA-Z_:>.-]*(wait|join|flush|sync)[a-z_]*\([^;]*\);' pr-u0.diff | grep -vE '^[0-9]+:\+\s*(extern|inline|static|void|bool|int|auto)\b'` so that only call statements survive (declarations such as h/libpos.hpp:276 and definitions such as src/pos/driver.cpp:892 drop out). Keep a call whose device argument is a literal (`get_device(0)`, `devices[0]`) or that carries a coverage comment ("after the last xfer", "all devices"), and that sits after a loop over `get_num_devices()` or `pos_list_devices()`. A call whose argument is the loop's own last handle (`dev`, `xfer` assigned in every iteration) is not a candidate (do_not_fire, PR 1722). On PR 2011 this grep returns 3 call statements: the two Wade sites and src/pos/driver.cpp:1009 `wait_for_xfer_blocks(dev, xfer)` (one transfer, no loop; dropped).
   (e) `grep -nE '^\+.*(get_device\(([0-9]+|process_device_id\{[0-9]+\})\)|(devices|devs|instances|ranks|shards|queues)[a-z_]*(\(\))?\)*\[0\]|\.front\(\))' pr-u0.diff`. Drop a hit whose removed partner line exists at BASE with only the rename map applied (a re-spelling, check 10), a hit under a comment that defers the device choice in writing ("DEPRECATED", "next pass", "hardcodes devs[0]"), and a hit that reads a property of an object the code already selected (`job.incomplete_shards[0]->dev`, `saved_shards[0]->base_tok_ix`).
2. Pattern (a): `git -C WT show HEAD:<struct file> | grep -n -E '<array member>|<CAP>'` and `git -C WT grep -n '<CAP> *=' HEAD -- h` record the capacity. `git -C WT grep -n '<count> *=' HEAD -- h src` lists every writer. For each writer: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<assign line>,<first indexed write line>p' | grep -n -E 'TRON_ASSERT|<= *<CAP>|< *<CAP>|return'`; NONE = finding, one finding per shared array.
3. Pattern (b): `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<loop start>,<loop end>p' | grep -n -E 'break;|return|<count> *='`; an exit with no `<count> = <fill index>` above it = finding. Caller: `git -C WT grep -n '<out-param>' HEAD -- src h`, then confirm the loops `for (wi = 0; wi < <count>; ...)` and the tail advances.
4. Pattern (c): `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk '/<helper signature>/,/^}/' | grep -n '<value> *='` lists the assignments with their enclosing `for`/`if`. Enumerate the caller's input classes from explicit branch conditions or request kinds only (PR 3008: attn_req true or false gives `num_metadata_wds > 0` or `== 0`); a loop bound that is a model dimension or a device property (n_kvheads, head_size, num_fetchers) counts as one class, never zero. A class that skips every assignment = finding. Consumer: `git -C WT grep -n '<stored field>' HEAD -- src h`; if every consumer tests a companion field before reading the value (driver.cpp:916 `if (xfer.readback_addr)` before `readback_value` at d4795f37a5), the sentinel is a designed absent value and not a finding. Old behaviour: `git -C WT show BASE:<file> | grep -n '<value>'`.
5. Pattern (d): `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<function start>,<function end>p'`; record the loop set and the per-iteration call. Open the per-iteration callee (`git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk '/<callee signature>/,/^}/'`) and record the device or queue it submits to (PR 2011: xfer_v_entry has `PosDevice* dev = devices[fpga_index];` and `hardware::xfer_blocks(dev, dev->load_weight_q, ...)`). `git -C WT grep -n -E 'void <wait fn>\(' HEAD -- src` and read which argument the completion check reads. State the covered set as the member whose handle the wait dereferences. Compare the comment above the wait with that set. Siblings: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n '<wait fn>(get_device'` (never grep the on-disk file: the worktree checkout is not at HEAD) and `git -C WT grep -n '<wait fn>(' HEAD -- h src`; report each sibling, linking the first.
6. Pattern (e): `git -C WT grep -n -E 'pos_list_devices\(\)|get_num_devices\(\)' HEAD -- h src` for the other choosers of the same object; `git -C WT grep -n -E 'using tp[24] = ' HEAD -- h/tron/models/common.hpp` for multi-device configurations; `git -C WT grep -n -E '<object>\(PosDevice\* dev' HEAD -- h` for the binding.
7. Exact-boundary loop bound: `grep -nE '^\+.*<= *\([a-z_]+ */ *[a-z_]+\) *\* *[a-z_]+' pr-u0.diff`; evaluate at x = n by hand; name the allocation site of the block at x; the remedy is a test ask, not a bug claim.
8. Author replies and deferrals: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/comments --paginate | jq -r '.[] | select(.in_reply_to_id!=null) | [.user.login,.body] | @tsv' | grep -i -E 'next pass|upcoming PR|future|phase' | grep -v '\[bot\]'` (the word "phase" also hits a cursor[bot] reply on PR 2287). Offline: `grep -n -i -E 'reply by .*(next pass|upcoming PR|future|phase)' corpus/pr/tron-N.md`. A written deferral by the author or a branch contributor is reported once and accepted.

On PR 2011 (BASE ab75e61d83 from the GitHub base.sha, head d4795f37a5, base branch hwattention_sync): pattern (d) hits h/pos/hwattention.hpp:645 and :674 `wait_for_xfer_blocks(get_device(0), xfer)` after the loops at :635 and :666 `for (idx = 0; idx < get_num_devices(); idx++)` that call `xfer_v_entry(..., idx, ...)` at :640-641 and `xfer_k_entry` at :669-670; the literal `get_device(0)` and the comment at :643-644 'after the last xfer, wait for completion' are the trigger. src/pos/driver.cpp:892-893 declares dev `[[maybe_unused]]`; :899 `DmaQueue* q = xfer.queue;` and :912 `xfer.queue->check_xfer_complete(xfer.end_desc, xfer.end_wrap_count)` check completion through the handle; dev is read only in log strings (:903, :938, :980) and on the timeout diagnostic path (:954 `dev->hbm_kv_offset`, :958-961 `dev->hbm_map`/`dev->hbmw_map`, :975 `debug_exit(label, dev->idx)`), never in the completion check. So only the last device's transfer is waited and the first N-1 are not; Wade's 'first device' wording (2789792758) describes the dev argument, the mechanism misses N-1 devices either way. skill_entry.name: 14. Silent fallback where an assert belongs
skill_entry.trigger: Added under h/ or src/: (a) std::min/max/clamp of a shape or index value against a named limit (*_MAX_*, *_SIZE) or a literal; (b) a bare early exit (return, continue, break; no log or assert) on an index or count, where the fall-through hands the value to a callee that TRON_ASSERTs the same bound, or a comment within five lines names tests, 'defensive', 'just in case', 'sanity' or 'for now'; (c) `if (this != &other)` in a move assignment; (d) a sentinel branch (`== 0`, `!p`) in a function that then builds a hardware command; (e) a pause-only wait loop with no counter, deadline or debug_exit; (f) a new TRON_ASSERT on a shape or limit parameter with no placeholder.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Run the procedures.md greps on the -w diff; BASE = parent of the PR's first commit if HEAD is on main. 2. Clamp: grep the limit constant; a sibling TRON_ASSERT or a screen returning false makes a bad value unreachable; t/-only callers = nit. 3. Exit: read the next callee for TRON_ASSERT_LT; grep t/ for tests needing it (fix the fixture). 4. Self-move: grep movers. 5. Sentinel: read to the end with the value fixed; logging is no exit. 6. Wait: who clears the flag and can it be stuck; compare with worker.cpp's tx wait and h/system/mwaitx.hpp. 7. Assert: one placeholder per value. 8. Unreachable -> assert with the value; reachable -> comment says when; wait -> bounded exit.
skill_entry.question: Can a bug-free caller reach this condition? If not, why does the code clamp, return or spin here instead of asserting (or debug_exit), and when the assert fires, does the message say which value tripped it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A feature switch (`if (!enabled) return;`), a checker's success return, a null check after a lookup that fails by contract (weak_ptr::lock, find, getenv, free(nullptr)), an equality of two values, a planner filter skipping a candidate (PRs 2875, 4353: no comment). A release no-op after the callee's assert (PR 2713). A guard the author explains by history (3307621121). A self-move guard called 'just defensive coding' (2825161209): approved unchanged. A wait with counter, deadline, snapshot and timeout error (worker.cpp tx wait). An external-input or chunk bound, a bool or pointer assert, a line present at BASE. A deliberate head_size parameter in a test-only helper (3866590750): ask to document; a clamp inside still counts. Never block on a spin-wait.
skill_entry.finding_shape: should we just assert this? `<guard>` (<file:line>) <clamps | returns | spins> on <condition>, but <upstream screen | callee> already <asserts | steers> at <file:line>, so a bug-free caller never reaches it. In production a wrong <value> would quietly <be truncated | go uncounted | hang> instead of failing. Prefer TRON_ASSERT with <value> in the message (or debug_exit when a device command is half built), and fix the test fixture instead; or say in the comment that <state> is expected and when. Wait loop: no way to break out and debug_exit; does <existing backpressure> already serialize this? Assert: would be useful to print <value> as well.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal when a production path hides a wrong index, truncates a model shape or half-builds a device command: 'Prefer asserting', 'IMO we should assert at this level', 'should we just assert this, or debug_exit()? We can't meaningfully continue on with this right?'. minor for an unbounded spin and for an assert message: 'Just seems a bit dangerous, but probably a next iteration/enhancement effort', 'would be useful to print the head_size as well'. Question form with no severity word for a guard that may be defensive: 'So this is defensive/sanity guarding?', 'should we just assert this? Are there legit scenarios ...?'. He wrote 'nit' on none of the eight member comments. He states reservations on a spin-wait without requesting changes and without approving (PR 2872: one COMMENTED review, closed unmerged 2026-06-03); PR 2766 he approved at cef0fb5b64 'assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments'.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at HEAD (sibling asserts, the file's other wait loops, how the function treats other invalid inputs); callers (the upstream screen, who moves the type, src/ versus t/ callers); other files (the eligibility function in h/tron/models/model.hpp, src/tron/gof.cpp asserts, h/common/assert.hpp macro, the mwaitx helpers in h/system/mwaitx.hpp, src/pos/worker.cpp tx wait); commits (git log -S for an earlier assert or a backed-out wait; gh api for a review commit the worktree lacks); runtime for the completion-path argument (write Insufficient data when hardware queue knowledge is needed).

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: silent fallback where an assert belongs

Setup for this check. When the review commit is already on main, `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself; take BASE as the parent of the PR's first commit: `FIRST=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json commits -q '.commits[0].oid'); BASE=$(git -C WT rev-parse $FIRST^)`. When the worktree lacks the review commit (`git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD` fails, as for PR 2766 cef0fb5b64 and PR 2233 4b7d03f71c), take the diff from `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/HEAD -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.diff"` or `gh pr diff N`, read a file at that commit with `gh api "repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD" --jq .content | base64 -d`, and run the flag-store and `git log -S` greps on the merged head or nearest ancestor. Every diff below uses `-w` so a re-indented line does not count as added (PR 2875 h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1666-1670 asserts show as `+` without -w). A new file needs no special case: its -U0 diff carries every line with `+`.

1. Clamps (shape a): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@|\+.*std::(min|max|clamp)<?[^;]*,\s*(\w+\()?([A-Z_]*(MAX|SIZE|LIMIT)[A-Z_]*|[0-9]+)\)?\);)'`. The +++ and @@ lines give the HEAD file and line of each hit (HEAD line = @@ new start + offset). Drop a chunk or batch bound in a loop (`std::min(remaining, CHUNK)`, `std::min(positions_data.size(), size_t(4))`), a counter floor (`std::max(x - 1, 0)`) and a limit on an external request field (`std::min<uint32_t>(request.logprobs, 20)`).
2. Silent exits (shape b): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E -A2 '^(\+\+\+|@@|\+ *if \(.*(<|>|<=|>=|==|!=|!\w)|\+ *return nullptr;)' | grep -E '^[0-9]+[:-](\+\+\+|@@|\+ *if .*(return|continue|break)|\+ *(return[^;]*;|continue;|break;))'`. This catches the one-line form and the form whose `return;` sits on the next line. Drop: a condition that is only an enable flag, an is_initialized() probe or a getenv/config result (`if (!enabled) return;`, `if (value == nullptr) return false;`); a branch that contains spdlog::error, TRON_ASSERT, TRON_ABORT or debug_exit (read 3 lines at HEAD); a success return in a checker; a null check after weak_ptr::lock(), find() or dynamic_cast; an equality of two values; a planner filter (`if (k < 2) continue;`). Keep a hit only if step 8 finds the callee assert or step 7 finds a tell within five lines. Positive-guard form: also grep `^\+ *if \(\w+ < \w+(\.size\(\))?( &&| \|\|)` for a write wrapped in a range test with no else branch, and read whether that write is the function's only effect.
3. Self-move guards (shape c): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*this != &other'`; then `git -C WT grep -n -E 'std::move\(.*<Type>|vector<<Type>>' HEAD -- h src`. Emit a question only; never a change request.
4. Sentinel branches (shape d): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+ *if \(\w+ == 0\)|^\+ *if \(!\w+\)'`. Keep a hit only if the enclosing function at HEAD calls a device command builder after the branch (`hardware::xfer_blocks`, `write_tx_descriptors`, `DmaQueue`, `descriptor`, a `.fields.` store): `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<start>,<end>p' | grep -n -E 'xfer_blocks|descriptor|\.fields\.|debug_exit|spdlog::error|TRON_ASSERT'`. A spdlog::error inside the branch does not clear the hit when the function keeps building the command (PR 2233 4b7d03f71c src/pos/worker.cpp:986-991 logs and continues). Drop a hit inside `#if 0`/`#endif` (disabled-code-left-in owns it; PR 2135 hwattention.hpp:765) and an if/else on a piece index with no command (PR 4353 model.hpp:2931).
5. Wait loops (shape e): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E -A3 '^\+ *(while ?\(|for ?\(;;\)|do \{)'`; keep a hit whose condition or body (the -A3 lines) reads an atomic or flag (`.load(`, `.wait(`, `in_flight`, `== false`) and whose body is only `ck_pr_stall()`, `_mm_pause()`, `mwaitx::delay_ns(` or `<view>.wait(N)` with no counter, no rdtsc deadline and no debug_exit. Do not put `ready`, `prepared` or `_done` in the loop-line pattern (a range-for over `ready_kv_plan` matches, PR 4353 model.hpp:2840). Who clears the flag: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<flag>\.store\(' HEAD -- src h`; record the thread (TX/RX worker, completion callback, prep worker) and whether it can be stuck. Earlier assert or backed-out wait: `git -C WT log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -S'<flag>' -- <file>`. The file's bounded form: `git -C WT show HEAD:src/pos/worker.cpp | grep -n 'max_checks\|deadline = \|debug_exit'` (HEAD c5d44bd86f: max_checks = 5 at :2009; PR 2766 raised it to 500 but never merged). Helpers: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'wait_for_|delay_ns' HEAD -- h/system/mwaitx.hpp` (wait_for_event :69/:74, wait_for_not_event :84/:89, wait_for_geq :99/:104, delay_ns :116; namespace tron::hardware::mwaitx, file h/system/mwaitx.hpp).
6. Assert messages (shape f): `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E -A2 '^\+.*TRON_(ASSERT|ABORT)\('`. Keep a hit whose condition names a model-shape or hardware-limit parameter (head_size, head_dim, n_kv_heads, n_heads, layer, n_layers, tok_ix, an HBM address or length) and whose message has no `{` placeholder of any form (`{}` and `{:#016x}` both count). Expand a precomputed bool (`addr_valid`) into its operands before deciding; drop an assert on a bool flag, a loop position or a pointer-null test (`TRON_ASSERT(!populated, ...)`, `position < 4`). At most one finding per PR, never on a line present at BASE. `git -C WT grep -n 'define TRON_ASSERT(' HEAD -- h` shows h/common/assert.hpp:69 forwards `...` to fmt, so adding the value costs one argument.
7. Comment tells, to rank the hits: `git -C WT diff -w -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -i -E '^[-+].*//.*(unit tests?|test states?|defensive|just in case|sanity|prevent(s)? reuse|we will expect|for now|today|eventually|extend)'`. A tell on a removed (`-`) line counts when the clamp or guard under it is kept (PR 4007 removed `// NOTE that we will expect n_kvheads <= 8 today...` and kept the clamp); a tell removed together with the check it described does not (PR 2875 token_cache.cpp removes `check_usage` and its 'defensively' comment together).
8. Reachability for shapes a and b. Clamp: `git -C WT grep -n '<LIMIT>' HEAD -- h src`; every TRON_ASSERT line in that output is a sibling assert. The parameter-name grep `git -C WT grep -n -E 'TRON_ASSERT[A-Z_]*\(.*<param>' HEAD -- h src` is a supplement only (the hunk may spell `n_kvheads` where siblings spell `n_kv_heads`: 0 versus 2 hits at 29a39ac33e). Open the screen: `git -C WT grep -n -E '_eligible\(|is_supported\(|can_use' HEAD -- h`, read its body, record STEER (returns bool) or ASSERT. Classify the clamp's function by callers: `git -C WT grep -n '<function>(' HEAD -- h src t`; only t/ callers = test-only, reported at nit. Exit: open the callee the index enters next (`git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -A3 '<callee>(size_t'`) and record its TRON_ASSERT_LT lines; tests that depend on the guard: `git -C WT grep -n '<hook>' HEAD -- t/`.
9. Report one finding per hit with the shape, the reachability fact (screen or callee file:line), the production consequence, and the ask (assert with the value in the message | comment says the state is expected | bound plus diagnosed exit | add the value). Ask whether the guard is defensive before asking for the assert.

On PR 4007 (HEAD 29a39ac33e, BASE 21162f5568 = parent of the PR's first commit bc298be626; h/+src/ diff 52 lines, 4 files): step 1 hits h/pos/hwattention.hpp:466 (k_hwcacheblock prep_xfer), :990 (xfer_k_packed_entry, production: src/pos/hwattention.cpp:26), :1035 (xfer_k_entry, test-only: t/t_hwattention.cpp:418). Steps 2-6 give 0 hits; step 7 hits two removed-line tells (`we will expect n_kvheads <= 8 today`, `which we will extend eventually`) next to kept clamps. Step 8: `git grep HW_MAX_KV_HEADS` 19 hits; h/tron/models/model.hpp:789-795 model_shape_is_hwattn_eligible() returns bool (steer); src/tron/gof.cpp:195-196 and model.hpp:1571-1573 assert with the value. Reproduces 3866435051. The whole-file grep would add :389 and :594 `std::min(positions_data.size(), size_t(4))`, present at BASE and never commented on. At the approved head 3a8544cd35 steps 1-7 give 0 candidates: the asserts at :456-458, :693-695, :1043-1044, :1095-1096, :1144-1145 all carry `{}`.

On PR 4596 (HEAD 1430736b2a, file new): step 2 one-line form yields :145-146 (dropped: getenv), :350 `return nullptr` (token_path_span), :358/:390/:437/:448/:469/:673/:685/:719/:740/:741/:764 (dropped: enable flag, `!any`, `!ok`, is_initialized, is_safe_model_id, `!stats->enabled`), :409 (note_attn_job), :421 (note_join_wait), :429 (note_fpga_pass); the two-line form adds :382-383 (add_visits, the line Wade anchored on). The positive-guard grep adds :371-373 (note_token_path). Step 7 hits :346 'test state that never ran begin_forward', :368 'unit tests drive apply_page_range without a forward', :378 'test states that grow `attn`'. Step 8: row() at :327-329 has TRON_ASSERT_LT(worker, n_workers) and TRON_ASSERT_LT(layer, n_layers), so the compares at :382, :409 and :421 are redundant and their only effect is to hide a wrong index. Reproduces 4125033677; the author converted every guard to TRON_ASSERT in 15f355acb2 (attn_stats.hpp:354-392, :479-501) and deleted note_token_path.

On PR 2233 (review commit 4b7d03f71c, not in the worktree; read with gh api contents): step 4 hits src/pos/worker.cpp:986 `if (shard_stride == 0) { spdlog::error("Shard stride should NOT be ZERO! ...", ...); }` among 7 sentinel branches; the function then stores shard_stride into the K and V weight commands, and treats too-much-context with spdlog::error + debug_exit and the batch size with TRON_ASSERT((workreq->B == 1), ...). Reproduces 2983787051; the merged head af9438799a:955-960 has `TRON_ASSERT((shard_stride != 0), "... shard_pages {}, tok_pages {}, shard_stride {} acmd_len {}", ...)` and :971/:975 store it into kwcmd/vwcmd.fields.hbm_stride.

Silent-corpus probe (precision lens, 15 silent PR diffs): with the narrowed shape (b) and the drop rules above, PR 2875 full.hpp:1001-1004 and token_tree.cpp:22, PR 4353 model.hpp:2856 and self_attention.hpp:1406, PR 2646 util.hpp:278, PR 1722 hwattention.hpp:252/:292/:305 and PR 2135 hwattention.hpp:765 produce 0 findings.
finals.widen_delta: New check; nothing in the thirteen existing checks looks at production guards, clamps, spin loops or assert messages. Checks 3 and 5 look at tests only; check 6 looks at claims. The closest neighbour is check 5's 'fix the fixture' remedy: this check adds the production-side half of codex C20 ('fix an invalid test fixture instead of adding production guards that silently hide bad state'). Widen the SKILL.md description line with 'production guards that hide a bad state where an assert belongs, unbounded waits, assert messages without the value'. Add to 'How Wade words a finding': the three-question form 'should we just assert this? Are there legit scenarios ...? Is this just a common defensive coding pattern ...?' and the two-alternative form 'should we just assert this, or debug_exit()?'. Add to Words used here: TRON_ASSERT (the project's assertion macro, active in every build because h/common/assert.hpp:3-4 undefines NDEBUG; it takes a format string plus arguments and forwards them to fmt at :69), debug_exit (the process-abort-with-diagnostics path in src/pos/driver.cpp), ck_pr_stall / mwaitx (a concurrencykit busy-wait pause / the repository's timed-wait helpers in h/system/mwaitx.hpp, namespace tron::hardware::mwaitx), screen function (a model-shape eligibility check such as model_shape_is_hwattn_eligible() that returns false and steers the model to another path instead of asserting).
