skill_entry.name: Redundant statement, member, branch, specifier or scope (nit)
skill_entry.trigger: Added lines in one of seven closed shapes: (a) a lambda in a std::function slot that only forwards its parameters, in order, to one free function; (b) an `} else {` whose every assignment repeats the variable's initializer above the `if`; (c) `struct X {` with `public:` first; (d) a repeated zero-argument call on one object where a local holds its result; (e) a new struct with an id or count member beside a pointer to a different type that exposes the same value; (f) `size_t n<name> = 0` beside a std::vector `<name>`; (g) a loop header replaced by a bare `{` while end-of-body resets stay; (h) a loop casting each `(T)obj[k]` where obj's element type is T.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. BASE from the PR's baseRefOid, never the live base branch. 2. Grep each shape (references/procedures.md); record file:line at HEAD. 3. (a): find the slot alias via `std::vector<ALIAS> <slot>;` and the callee declaration; compare types after namespace resolution; fire only on an exact match with no capture, conversion, reorder, drop or extra argument. 4. (b): read the whole function. 5. (d): one function body (`@@` headers); note pointer locals (`(*devs)[0]`). 6. (e): added-struct hits only; read the pointee member; grep every writer; a writer leaving the pointer null means ask. 7. (f): std::vector only. 8. (g): read the whole block. 9. (h): resolve typedefs. 10. One nit per shape per PR, at the first hit, ending 'etc'.
skill_entry.question: If this statement, member, branch, specifier or scope were deleted, would any observable state, any type, or any build change, or does the surrounding code or the language already give exactly what it gives?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A lambda that captures, converts, reorders, drops or adds an argument, or calls a member on a looked-up object (429249ead6:798-801 stayed). A count beside std::array or T[N] (3010846319 misread). A member re-read, not a call (tron-1722); a call on another object (tron-4353); repeated `getenv` (duplicate-logic check). A pointer to the enclosing type; a member added to an existing struct; a member with no reader (dead-symbol check). A cv-qualifying, widening or pointer cast. A memset with no removed loop (hot-path check). An explicit `= 0` (review body 4125818552). Redundancies outside the seven shapes (tron-1827, tron-2646 silent). Never block: approvals came 1-11 minutes after the ask; three of eight asks never applied. Withdraw after an author fact (2790097310, 2790148917).
skill_entry.finding_shape: "<'minor nit:' | 'a bit pedantic but' | nothing>: `<thing>` is redundant here... <one reason: members are public by default / `<local>` already holds it / `<ptr>->idx` already has it / already initialized to these values / you're no longer running a loop>. <optional: Would it be clearer to just do `<one-line replacement>`?> <optional: Or is there some <state> where <it is needed>?>" A one-line replacement goes in a ```suggestion block. One comment per shape per PR, anchored at the first hit in file order, ending 'etc' or 'and similarly elsewhere' when the shape repeats.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit only. His own words: 'minor nit:' (3391446464), 'I know this is pedantic... but' (2700506675), 'a bit pedantic but' (2976643305), 'isn't `device_idx` redundant here?' (2913598312), 'it seems like `nshards` is redundant' (3010846319), a bare ```suggestion block with no words (3029340601). The same register appears outside this check: 'kinda pedantic, but' on a default-argument echo (2789826297, tron-2011) and on constexpr placement (2947931435, tron-2176), and 'a bit pedantic' in the APPROVED review body 4125818552 (tron-2438). 'Not blocking' spelled out: 0 corpus hits; the approval arrives minutes later regardless (5 min 19 s on tron-2176, 56 s on tron-2223, 11 min 3 s on tron-2906, each at the commented commit).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk, then the full enclosing function or type at HEAD (shapes b, d, g), then other files: the member declaration that names the slot alias, the alias, the callee declaration and its enclosing namespace lines (shape a); the pointee type and every writer of the id member in h/ and src/ (shape e); the typedef chain of the indexed object (shape h). Also `gh pr view N --json baseRefOid` for BASE. Not the PR body, not commits, not CI, not runtime.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check <n>: redundant statement, member, branch, specifier or scope (nit)

Setup. BASE is the merge base against the PR base branch AS IT WAS at review time. `gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName,baseRefOid,mergeCommit`; BASE=`git -C WT merge-base HEAD <baseRefOid>`. If `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>` returns HEAD itself, the branch already contains the merged PR and that result is wrong (on PR 2176: `git merge-base 8e19ea3e62 origin/hwattention_sync` = 8e19ea3e62; baseRefOid 363edb2910 gives the 20-file, 1176-added-line diff). Save it: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD > pr-u0.diff; git -C WT diff BASE HEAD > pr.diff`. Context lines that `grep -A` prints carry an `N-` prefix (line number, dash); every second-stage filter below allows `^[0-9]+[-:]`.

1. Lambdas pushed into callback slots (shape a): `grep -nE -A1 '\.(push_back|emplace_back)\(' pr-u0.diff | grep -E '^[0-9]+[-:]\+.*\[[^]]*\]\s*\('`. This catches the one-line form `x.push_back([](...) {` and the clang-format split form (`x.push_back(` on one line, `[](...) {` on the next). Do not grep `= [`: it matches helper lambdas (`auto is_special_value = [](float f) {`) and fmt strings (`[{}-{}] (count={})`). For each hit read the lambda at HEAD (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'L,L+4p'`). Keep it only if its body is one call whose argument list equals the lambda parameter list in order; a capture (`[&, i]`), a member call on a looked-up object (`get_device_dma_tracker().await_layer(l)`), a conversion, a dropped or added argument = no finding. Then find the slot's element type from its member declaration (`git -C WT grep -n -E '\b<slot>\b' HEAD -- FILE`, read `std::vector<ALIAS> <slot>;`), the alias (`git -C WT grep -n -A1 'using ALIAS' HEAD -- FILE`) and the callee (`git -C WT grep -n 'CALLEE(' HEAD -- h`). Compare types after namespace resolution: read the `namespace` lines above the callee (`git -C WT show HEAD:h/tron/gof.hpp | grep -nE '^namespace|^struct node_base|^using'`); `node_base*` declared inside `namespace tron::hardware` with `namespace tron { struct node_base; }` above it equals `tron::node_base*`. Parameter names never matter. Exact types and order = finding.
2. Else branch that repeats initializers (shape b): `grep -nE '^\+\s*\} else \{' pr-u0.diff`. Map each hit to HEAD through its `@@` header and read the whole function (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'S,Ep'`). For each `VAR = RHS;` in the else find `TYPE VAR = INIT;` above the if in the same function; finding only when every RHS equals INIT (treat `0` and `nullptr` for a pointer as equal). An else that assigns anything else, or with no assignment, is cleared.
3. Redundant first access specifier (shape c, struct form only): `grep -nE -A1 '^\+\s*struct [A-Za-z_0-9]+[^;]*\{\s*$' pr-u0.diff | grep -E '^[0-9]+[-:]\+\s*public:'`. Confirm no other specifier sits between the brace and the hit. The `class X {` + `private:` mirror is not a shape (0 instances in Wade's 267 texts and 0 added `public:|private:|protected:` lines in the 15 silent diffs).
4. Repeated zero-argument accessor (shape d): list the changed functions from the hunk headers, `grep -oE '^@@.*@@.*' pr-u0.diff | sort -u`. For each function body at HEAD list locals of the form `auto\*? NAME = EXPR;` or `auto const& NAME = *EXPR;` where EXPR is a zero-argument call (`pos_list_devices()`, `obj.size()`); the finding is a later textual repeat of EXPR (same callee, same object) in the same function body. Two calls in two functions are not a finding (gof.cpp:260 on_save_impl and :385 gof_flush_partial on PR 2176). A plain member read after a local (`dev->num_fetchers` after `auto num_fetchers = dev->num_fetchers;`) is not a call. Read whether NAME is a pointer or a reference before writing the suggestion (`(*devs)[0]`, not `devs[0]`). `getenv` belongs to duplicate-logic-use-existing-helper.
5. Id or index member beside a pointer member (shape e): `grep -nE '^(@@|\+\s*struct [A-Za-z_0-9]+\s*\{|\+\s*(uint32_t|uint64_t|int|size_t) [a-z_]*(idx|index|_id)\s*(=[^;]*)?;|\+\s*[A-Za-z_:]+\* [a-z_]+ = )' pr-u0.diff`. Keep an id hit only when it sits between an added `struct NAME {` line and that struct's closing brace (a hunk whose `@@` header names a function or `public:` is a function local or an existing class: discard; on PR 2176 all five `size_t device_idx = device_index_of(dev);` hits are locals). Pointee field: `git -C WT grep -n 'struct POINTEE' HEAD -- h` then read for `idx`; a pointer to the enclosing type itself (tree links) never counts. Writers: `git -C WT grep -n '\bMEMBER\b' HEAD -- h src`; record for each writer whether it also sets the pointer. One writer that leaves the pointer null = ask the 'transient state' question, assert nothing.
6. Count beside a container (shape f): `grep -nE -A1 '^\+\s*std::(vector|array)<' pr-u0.diff | grep -E '^[0-9]+[-:]\+\s*size_t n[a-z_]* = 0;'`. Read the container type: std::vector = finding; std::array<T, N> or T[N] = capacity, the count is the fill level, no finding.
7. Loop header turned into a bare block (shape g): `grep -nE -A2 '^-\s*(for|while) \(' pr.diff | grep -E '^[0-9]+-\+\s*\{\s*$'` (on PR 2223: removed `for (auto dev : *pos_list_devices()) {` at diff line 277, added `{` at 278). Open the block at HEAD from the `{` to its closing brace; list end-of-body statements that only prepare the next iteration (`memset(`, `.clear()`, `= 0;`) and the brace pair plus indentation.
8. Per-element cast of an already-typed object (shape h): `grep -nE '^\+.*\((bf16|float|uint(8|16|32|64)_t)\)\s*[a-z_]+\[[a-z_]+\]' pr-u0.diff` inside a loop; resolve the declared element type of the indexed object through its typedef chain (`git -C WT grep -n 'using OBJ_t' HEAD -- h`); finding only when it equals the cast target exactly. A cast that adds a cv-qualifier (`(volatile bf16) * (cpt + lc)`), changes width or signedness, or casts a pointer is not a redundancy.
9. Report: one comment per shape per PR, anchored at the first hit in file order, nit, question form, with the one-line replacement in a ```suggestion block when it is one line, ending 'etc' or 'and similarly elsewhere'. Withdraw after an author fact. Never block.

On PR 2176 (BASE 363edb2910, commented commit 8e19ea3e62): step 1 returns five lines (diff 1885, 1889 wrapped on_save_k/on_save_v introducers; 1892 one-line on_flush_partial; 1896, 1898 on_await_dma/on_forward_poll) and no fmt strings or helper lambdas. At HEAD h/tron/models/model.hpp:795-802 two lambdas `[](bf16** h, size_t t, size_t nk, size_t l, size_t hs, tron::node_base* n) { tron::hardware::gof_on_save_k(h, t, nk, l, hs, n); }` go into `on_save_k`/`on_save_v`, declared :629-630 as `std::vector<kv_save_observer_t>`; alias :627-628 `std::function<void(bf16**, size_t, size_t, size_t, size_t, tron::node_base*)>`; callees h/tron/gof.hpp:85-90 `gof_on_save_k(bf16** heads, size_t tok_ix, size_t n_kv_heads, size_t layer, size_t head_size, node_base* hint)`, :91 gof_on_save_v, :97 `gof_flush_partial(size_t, size_t, node_base*)` inside `namespace tron::hardware` (:21) with `namespace tron { struct node_base; }` (:17-18); on_flush_partial alias :633-634. Three forwarders match exactly -> one comment anchored at :795 with 'etc'. The :805-806 on_await_dma and on_forward_poll lambdas call a member on `get_device_dma_tracker()` -> no finding; they stayed at the fix commit 429249ead6 model.hpp:798-801 ('Simplify observer registration; document xfer_gof as temporary', which pushes gof_on_save_k, gof_on_save_v, gof_flush_partial directly at :795-797) with no comment. Steps 2-8 on PR 2176: 3 `} else {` hits in the new file h/pos/hwattention_dump.hpp, none redundant; 0 struct+public; 0 same-function accessor repeats; 5 id hits, all function locals, discarded; 0 count-beside-vector; 0 loop-to-block; 0 per-element casts.

Other verified anchors. 2913598312 (tron-2089, dbd7478b7e h/pos/gof.hpp:111-112 `uint32_t device_idx = 0;` beside `PosDevice* dev = nullptr;` inside `struct shard` :109; pointee h/pos/device.hpp:236-237 `struct PosDevice { int idx;`); skill_entry.name: 14. Disabled code left in the tree (`#if 0` blocks and commented-out statements)
skill_entry.trigger: Any one, all mechanical. (a) The diff adds `#if 0` or `#if false` (a preprocessor block no build compiles). (b) A touched h/ or src/ file holds an unchanged `#if 0` block at HEAD within 20 lines of a hunk start (PR 2148 h/pos/hwattention.hpp:507 sits outside both hunks of the file). (c) In h/ or src/ the diff adds a `//` line that is a statement: it starts with `if (`, `for (`, `while (`, `}` or an identifier followed by `(` or ` = `, ends with `;`, `{`, `(` or `,`, is not a log, dump or exit call, and holds no run of four lowercase words. (d) A removed line reappears in the same file with `//` in front and passes the statement test of (c) (PR 1997 `if (pdc + 1 == dev->num_fetchers) {`).
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Run the step 1-3 commands of procedures.md: added disabled lines mapped to HEAD lines, removed lines that reappear commented in the same file, unchanged `#if 0` blocks within 20 lines of a hunk. 2. Per `#if 0` block: read to `#endif`, record line count and kind (debug prints, disabled production logic, disabled test code), and test the first statement inside against `git show BASE:FILE`: present verbatim means live code switched off (PR 2461 src/pos/worker.cpp:769). 3. Per commented statement: find a live call or assignment of the same name in the same function (PR 1920 hwattention.hpp:655 next to the live wait at :649) or a commented declaration in another file (device.hpp:338-339 for device.cpp:90-91). 4. Read the two lines above for a stated reason; a PR-body sentence is not one (PR 2461 body says 'behind `#if 0`', Wade asked anyway). 5. Report once per file: first hit is the finding, later hits are 'same at'.
skill_entry.question: Does any build compile this text, and if not, why is it in the tree instead of deleted, or is it a reference the author means to keep (then a one-line comment should say so)?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A disabled line or block whose two preceding lines say why it is off or where the behavior moved (PR 2008 h/pos/hwattention.hpp:816, :847 under 'performing our wait one layer down inside the xfer function', approved with no text); a line that only says what the code would do is no reason (PR 1920 :654). Commented-out log, dump or exit calls (PR 1920 head: 15 `// spdlog::` lines, `// debug_exit` at :507). Commented statements under t/ (PR 1666 :1371-1374, :1423; PR 1920 t_hwattention.cpp:170). An old signature above a definition (PR 1920 :443-444). `#ifdef NAME` blocks (debug-switch-or-output-left-on). A single commented-out wait, sleep, lock, assert or check live at BASE (silent-behavior-change owns it, 3307473806). A block the author told a human reviewer is kept on purpose (PR 2461 3102946251): never repeat, never block.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (A) commented statement: "`<file>:<line>` is a commented-out <guard | call | assignment> that nothing compiles; the live `<call>` at :<line> already does the work. can this go away? Or are you leaving it as reference for an alternative strategy (then a one-line comment should say so)?" (B) `#if 0` block: "`<file>:<line>` is an `#if 0` block of N lines (<debug prints | a <check | wait> that was live at BASE and is now silent>) that nothing compiles. if this isn't useful, should get rid of it. <same at :<line>, :<line>>"

## Check 14: disabled code left in the tree

BASE for this check: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha` when online. Offline, or when `origin/<base_ref>` is absent from WT (PR 2461: no `origin/wm-bill-hwsync1`): BASE = the second parent of the newest merge on HEAD's first-parent line, `git -C WT log --first-parent --merges -1 --format=%P HEAD | cut -d" " -f2` (PR 2461: b539439a18, same as base.sha). If there is no merge, ask for base.sha. Never use origin/main for a PR against a feature branch (PR 2461: 5f37572171, a huge diff).

1. Added lines that are `#if 0`/`#if false` or commented-out statements, with HEAD file:line. The awk counts every added line, blank ones included (a bare `+` must advance the counter, or every later number in the hunk is low by one per blank line: the earlier awk printed PR 1920 :451 for the block at :458). The greps keep code syntax, drop prose (a run of four lowercase words), drop log, dump and exit calls with any namespace prefix (`//tron::hardware::debug_exit(...)`, PR 2461 worker.cpp:775), and keep only `#if 0` lines under t/:
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3); next} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); n=a[2]-1; next} /^\+/{n++; print f":"n":"substr($0,2)}' \
| grep -E ':[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*if[[:space:]]+(0|false)[[:space:]]*$|:[[:space:]]*//[[:space:]]*(if \(|for \(|while \(|else|\}|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:.>-]*(\(|[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]).*[;{(,]$)' \
| grep -v -E '//[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*::)*(spdlog::|debug_hexdump|debug_bf16dump|debug_exit|dbg_)' \
| grep -v -E '//[^;{(,]*([a-z]+ ){3,}[a-z]+' \
| grep -v -E '^t/[^:]*:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*//' > disabled.txt
```
2. Removed lines that reappear commented in the same file, passing the statement test and the log-call exclusion of step 1 (a removed log, dump or exit call that comes back commented is not a hit; a removed wait, sleep, lock, assert, warn or check that comes back commented goes to silent-behavior-change, not here):
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} /^\+[ \t]*\/\//{l=$0; sub(/^\+[ \t]*\/\/[ \t]*/,"",l); print f"\t"l}' \
| while IFS=$'\t' read -r f l; do git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- "${f#a/}" | grep -E '^-[^-]' | sed -E 's/^-[ \t]*//' | grep -qxF -- "$l" \
  && echo "$l" | grep -qE '^(if \(|for \(|while \(|else|\}|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:.>-]*(\(|[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]))' \
  && echo "$l" | grep -qvE '^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*::)*(spdlog::|debug_hexdump|debug_bf16dump|debug_exit|dbg_)' \
  && echo "REAPPEARS in ${f#a/}: $l"; done
```
3. Unchanged `#if 0` blocks within 20 lines of a hunk start in touched h/ and src/ files, minus the step 1 hits (one command; `prfiles.txt` from the common setup):
```
for f in $(grep -E '^(h|src)/' prfiles.txt); do starts=$(git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- $f | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@ -[0-9,]+ \+([0-9]+).*/\1/' | tr '\n' ' '); git -C WT show HEAD:$f | grep -n -E '^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*if[[:space:]]+(0|false)' | cut -d: -f1 | awk -v s="$starts" -v f=$f 'BEGIN{n=split(s,h," ")} {for(i=1;i<=n;i++) if ($1-h[i]<=20 && h[i]-$1<=20){print f":"$1; break}}'; done | grep -v -x -F -f <(cut -d: -f1,2 disabled.txt)
```
   Expect one or two unchanged debug blocks per worker-style file that Wade would not mention (PR 2148 src/pos/worker.cpp:1251, PR 1920 src/pos/worker.cpp:1154); they go into the per-file sentence after the first hit and never lead when a step 1 hit exists in the same file.
4. Per `#if 0` block: extent, kind, and whether it switches off code that was live at BASE. Take the first line inside the block that is not blank, a brace or a `//` comment; if it exists verbatim at BASE the block disables live code, else the block is new:
```
git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v s=LINE 'NR>=s{print NR": "$0} NR>s && /^[[:space:]]*#endif/{exit}'
first=$(git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v s=LINE 'NR>s && /^[[:space:]]*#endif/{exit} NR>s && !/^[[:space:]]*([{}]|\/\/.*)?[[:space:]]*$/{print; exit}'); git -C WT show BASE:FILE | grep -qxF -- "$first" && echo LIVE-AT-BASE || echo NEW
```
5. Per commented statement: live twin in the same function, and a commented declaration elsewhere (residue pair):
```
git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n 'NAME'                      # live call or assignment of the same name
git -C WT grep -n -E '//[[:space:]]*(size_t|int|bool|auto)?[[:space:]]*NAME' HEAD -- h src
```
6. Stated reason and author reply. The two lines above the block clear it when they say why it is off or where the behavior moved (PR 2008 :814-815); a comment naming the switch the block stands for (`// #ifdef DEBUG_RX_DESC`, PR 2148 worker.cpp:300) is a hypothesis-grade clear, reported in the per-file sentence only. A reply clears a block only when it answers a human reviewer (not a bot) and says the block is kept on purpose; a reply that says the disabled check is no longer valid (PR 2461 3101971874, to cursor[bot]) is a reason to delete, and Wade asked at :769 after it:
```
git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v s=LINE 'NR>=s-2 && NR<s{print NR": "$0}'
gh api --paginate repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/comments --jq '.[] | select(.path=="FILE") | [.id,.user.login,.created_at,.in_reply_to_id,.original_line,(.body|.[0:120])] | @tsv'
```
7. Report once per file: first hit as the finding (shape A for a commented statement, shape B for an `#if 0` block), later hits as "same at :L, :L". A block that switches off a BASE-live check or wait gets the clause "now silent" in shape B and is not repeated by silent-behavior-change.

Wade: 'can probably just remove the commented lines' (2771711406). At the approved head c502e4d61a the lines are gone and :703-704 carry the prose reason ('wait after every transfer for now ... chip hang'). On PR 2461 (BASE b539439a18, HEAD 9d0d649274) step 1 hits h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:468, src/pos/worker.cpp:769 and :797 (worker.cpp:775 `//tron::hardware::debug_exit(...)` is dropped by the exclusion); step 2 prints nothing; step 4 marks :769 LIVE-AT-BASE (`if (workreq->tok_ix < hardware::MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN) {`), :468 and :797 NEW. Wade commented on the first two (3102601258, 3102603313 'same here'). On PR 2148 (BASE e2ce886cca, HEAD 4491ff73db) step 1 hits only src/pos/worker.cpp:301; step 3 adds h/pos/hwattention.hpp:507 (hunk at :520, 4 lines after its `#endif`, -U0 headers `@@ -466 +466,6` and `@@ -514,0 +520,5`) and src/pos/worker.cpp:1251; Wade asked at :507 (2915191812). On PR 1920 (BASE a85c91e3f5 = second parent of the last merge, HEAD 620d1e83ba) step 1 hits hwattention.hpp:458, :655, model.hpp:1355, device.cpp:90-91, t_hwattention_replay.cpp:712; Wade asked at :656 (2737935271) and device.cpp:91 (2737826254). skill_entry.name: 14. Shared state reached from a new thread, guarded by a new lock, or no longer waited for
skill_entry.trigger: Added non-comment lines under h/ or src/ show one of: (a) a new parallel region (parallel_for, parallel_for_limited, std::thread, std::jthread, std::async, worker fanout) whose body reaches a function that ran serially at BASE; (b) a new mutex, lock_guard or static mutex array with no comment naming the guarded state, where the mutated member lives in another file or struct, or a lock held over a loop whose node type lives in another file; (c) one struct hunk adds a std::atomic member and a plain member written by one function; (d) one block reads a racy getter (count_complete_gofs, an atomic load) twice, in a condition and a dependent value; (e) a software readiness predicate (name contains needed, ready, visible, depends) is narrowed or removed where another minibatch or thread writes the storage it guards.
skill_entry.procedure: Apply the do-not-fire list first; take HEAD from the review row. (a) Parallel region: reach the callee through lambdas and template bodies; list the members it writes and their owner; grep the callee for a lock or atomic; combine nested regions to decide whether two executions reach one object. (b) New lock: name the mutated member and its file, the owner's existing mutexes, and the mutex each other mutator takes; separate the mutating part from the waiting part. (c) Atomic/plain mix: list readers and writers per member with their thread. (d) Double read: find the sibling block that caches the value and the base-branch fix. (e) Narrowed predicate: check the removed wait did not move into a callee; compare the consumer's read width with the predicate. Report object, writer thread, reader thread, protection file:line or NONE, precedent; the race is Insufficient data (runtime).
skill_entry.question: Which thread writes this state and which thread reads it at HEAD, and does the lock, atomic or wait that separates them live in the object that owns the state and cover every path that mutates it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Applied before the steps. A mutex whose comment names state declared in the same file, including a lock held over a loop there (tron-1722 hwkv_mutex; PR 2777 placer.cpp, no comment). A member mutex over the owner's own container (tron-2469 qalloc_mutex over device->queues; tron-2875 n->mtx). Atomics added alone with no caller outside their header (tron-2693 kv_saves_). A plain member of a thread_local object (PR 2777 device_placer). A whole-loop lock once the author states the reason (PR 2233). A fanout with one device per iteration and no added lock (tron-2475, tron-3756); a rewrite of an existing region (tron-4077). A wait that moved into a callee, and hardware DMA waits (tron-2008): index-count-or-wait-set-mismatch owns those. Memory-order choices. Observed-race claims. A missing test for a new primitive (4614385493).
skill_entry.finding_shape: Question form (default, his own initiative): "I assume you <lock `<mutex>` for the entire loop | made `<members>` (and only these) atomics> because <someone could update `<structure>` during the gather | `<reader>` runs on a different thread>?" Statement form (only when answering an existing thread): "`<callee>` (<file:line>) is not <locked | waited for>. So concurrent <calls | minibatches> on the *same* `<object>` would <contend on `<member>` with no lock/guard protection | read `<storage>` while `<writer>` writes it>." Placement form (the head already carries a caller-side lock): "IMO it would be better to add a mutex member to `<owner>` and take it inside `<callee>`; the wait only compares per-caller values, so the lock can end after `<mutating call>`." Double read: "see line <L> where the value is cached."
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal, never 'nit'. Of the six rows, three are replies inside a thread another reviewer or a bot opened (3275212298 to axch 3274515787; 3125517302 and 3970590653 to cursor[bot]). On his own initiative he used the question form in two of three rows (2983867856, 3406007619); default to the question form and use the statement form only when answering an existing thread. His own words on the six rows: 'I'm inclined to balk at this a bit', "this is probably 'fine' just because I don't think we're actually parallelizing across the **same device**, right?", 'may be acceptable', 'I would still ultimately defer to @mcherba', and he labels his own reading ('based on my read of the code', 'I _think_'). Adjacent rows outside the six: 'I do think there's merit to this complaint' (2983833171, PR 2233, src/pos/worker.cpp:808, a reply to cursor[bot] on an early release inside prepare_hwattn_cmds) and 'I think this is a legit concern' (3156090573, PR 2565, full.hpp:858, a shard-ordering reply to cursor[bot]). The one blocking row (3970590653, reader no longer waits for a writer) stayed COMMENTED on 2026-09-09 until the fix fe516bb512 landed, then APPROVED on 2026-09-14 at df9b800181; he never used CHANGES_REQUESTED. He defers lock placement in driver code to the file's owner by @-mention and does not block on it.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (every acquirer of the mutex, the sibling block that caches the getter, the comment above the mutex); callers (every other mutator of the member and the mutex each takes, every caller of the parallel region including generated code under ingest/); other files (the callee definition under src/, the owning struct header, the FUSE registration in src/pos/device.cpp, the consumer accessor in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp); commits (base branch log for an earlier fix of the same pattern); the review row's commit id (the inline comment's commit id is re-anchored by GitHub). Runtime evidence is needed to confirm a race and is normally unavailable: write Insufficient data (runtime) for the race and report the protection gap. The dropped-wait branch (e) is worded from the merged code comment at 9653307d68:common.hpp:957-960 and the pasted GPT text on 3970590653; Wade's own text on that thread is only 'I asked GPT to evaluate this... it agrees:', so present that branch as a check Wade acted on, not as his wording.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: shared state reached from a new thread, guarded by a new lock, or no longer waited for

Setup. HEAD = the commit of the review row: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/reviews --jq '.[]|select(.user.login=="Wado-posi")|[.submitted_at,.commit_id]|@tsv'`. Never take the inline comment's commit id: GitHub re-anchors it to a later head when the line survives a push. If `git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD` fails, read files with `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD --jq .content | base64 -d` and the diff with `gh pr diff N --repo positron-ai/tron`; without network write `Insufficient data (no network)`. Save the full text of every file that declares a mutex or atomic the diff adds, and the definition file of every callee inside a new parallel region.

1. Trigger grep over production files, comment lines and the threading primitive excluded:
   `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src ':!h/tron/threading.hpp' | grep -v -E '^\+\s*//' | grep -n -E '^\+.*(parallel_for|std::thread|std::jthread|std::async|std::mutex|lock_guard|unique_lock|scoped_lock|std::atomic|fetch_add)'`
   `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -v -E '^[-+]\s*//' | grep -n -E '^[-+].*(_needed|_ready|ready\(|visible\(|depends)'`
   Map hits to HEAD file:line: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3)} /^@@/{split($3,a,","); n=substr(a[1],2)+0; next} /^-/{next} {if ($0 ~ /^\+.*(parallel_for|std::thread|std::mutex|lock_guard|std::atomic|fetch_add|_needed|_ready)/) print f":"n": "substr($0,2); n++}'`
   Expect 10-30 hits on a loading PR. List t/ and threading.hpp hits as context only. Apply the do-not-fire list to every hit now; a covered hit is listed as context and not run through steps 2-7.
2. Parallel region. When the body is a template or lambda parameter (`body(e)`, `f(ix)`), the region has no callee of its own: `git -C WT grep -n '<region fn>' HEAD` over the WHOLE tree (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs emits generated C++ callers) and take the lambda at each caller as the body. Follow lambdas through at most two levels; beyond that take the entry points named in the PR body ("Changes" bullets) and in existing review threads, and state which levels were not read. Callee definition: `git -C WT grep -n -E '\b<callee>\(' HEAD -- h src`; body: `git -C WT show HEAD:<def file> | sed -n '<s>,<e>p'`; write every member written (`dev->`, `q->`, push, assignment) and its owner; `git -C WT show HEAD:<def file> | sed -n '<s>,<e>p' | grep -n -E 'mutex|lock_guard|atomic'` (empty = unprotected). Combine every enclosing region before deciding whether two executions reach one object: an inner device-disjoint loop (`dev_idx = map.mask[i]`) reaches the same device twice when an outer fanout runs it once per expert. Record the outermost new region and the object key of the innermost call.
3. New lock. Read the comment on the mutex: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<decl-3>,<decl>p'`. If it names a state declared in the same file or struct, stop for this hit. Otherwise the state = the member the locked call mutates (step 2). Acquirers: `git -C WT grep -n '<mutex>' HEAD -- h src`. Other mutators: `git -C WT grep -n '<member>' HEAD -- h src`; walk each up to its callers until a lock_guard or none is found and record the NAME of the mutex (two different mutexes on one member is a finding of its own). Wait split: `git -C WT show HEAD:<def file> | sed -n '<s>,<e>p' | grep -n -E 'wait_for|usleep|delay_ns|while|do \{'`; record (i) what the wait reads and (ii) what it compares against; a wait that writes, pops or resets nothing and compares shared state with values the caller got from its own enqueue (`start_ch`, `end_desc`) can run outside the lock. House convention: `git -C WT show HEAD:<owner header> | grep -n 'std::mutex'`.
4. Lock over a whole loop (node or entry type declared in another file): `git -C WT grep -n '<mutex>' HEAD -- <file>`; per acquirer note whether it mutates the looped structure; `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<lock-3>,<lock+2>p'` for a reason comment; the thread that runs the loop comes from the author's reply or the PR thread.
5. Atomic/plain mix: per new member `git -C WT grep -n '<member>' HEAD -- h src t`; tag each hit with its function and thread (src/pos/worker.cpp = TX worker; `git -C WT grep -n -E '&[A-Za-z_]+::<member>' HEAD -- src` = a pointer handed to tron::fuse::stats, read on the FUSE thread; an object declared `thread_local` has no cross-thread reader and the plain/atomic mix is not reported). The atomic set must equal the set of members with a reader on another thread.
6. Double read: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(count_complete_gofs|dma_complete)\(\)|^\+.*\.load\('`; enclosing block: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /\{$/ {n=NR; s=$0} END{print n": "s}'`; warning comment: `git -C WT grep -n -B2 -A2 '<getter>' HEAD -- h | grep -i -E 'race|async'`; sibling cache: `git -C WT grep -n -E '= [a-z_.]*<getter>\(\);' HEAD -- h src`; earlier fix: `git -C WT log --format='%h %an %ad %s' --date=short -S'<getter>' BASE -- <file>`.
7. Narrowed predicate: first `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- <file> | grep -n '<removed wait name>'`; a `+` line inside a function the hunk now calls means the wait moved, and the check stops for that hit. Then `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- <file> | grep -n -A14 '<predicate>('` and read old and new side by side; consumer read width: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'scaled_v|entire page|whole page|interleaved' HEAD -- h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp`; tests on the predicate and whether they pre-initialize the shared storage (which hides the case): `git -C WT grep -n -l '<predicate>\|poison\|NaN' HEAD -- t/`.
8. Report per hit: object, writing thread, reading thread, protection file:line or NONE, precedent (sibling line, earlier commit, member mutex in the owner). Question form by default; statement form only inside an existing thread; placement form when the reviewed head already carries a caller-side lock (never the unprotected statement then); `Insufficient data (runtime)` for the race itself.

skill_entry.name: 14. A declaration, constant block, include or growing function sits where a reader will not look for it
skill_entry.trigger: Any one fires; all judged at HEAD. (a) A header hunk deletes or moves a line of a namespace-scope constexpr value block that existed at BASE below the file's first struct, class or function body; config headers (h/pos/config.hpp, h/system/config.hpp) are exempt. (b) A hunk adds a prototype, with no `-` twin of the same symbol in the hunk, to a header that exists at BASE, and the defining src/<dir>/<base>.cpp has a same-directory header h/<dir>/<base>.hpp other than the receiving one. (c) An added `#include "<path>"` where h/<path> does not resolve at the PR head and no src/**/<basename>.in generates it. (d) 30 or more added lines inside one function of 400 or more lines at BASE, split over both branches of one if/else. (e) A production header keeps 5 or more dump_/debug_/print_/trace_ definitions and another reviewer asked to keep them.
skill_entry.procedure: 0. A PR that creates the header, a branch merge or a workaround PR drew no placement comment; there (a) and (b) are noted, not reported. 1. Per touched header: first body line, constexpr value lines below it, constexpr lines the hunk deletes; home = top of file or h/pos/config.hpp. 2. Per added prototype: column-0 definition in src/, its same-directory header, the type whose members the body reads; a header without @file takes its topic from its name and first two structs. 3. Per quoted include: resolve at the PR head; list the library's sibling includes; read .clang-format IncludeCategories. 4. Per function with hunks: indentation-matched length at BASE and HEAD; added lines per branch. 5. Count dump_ definitions; look for a sibling *_dump.hpp. 6. Read non-bot threads and the body; a move request by another reviewer or a split the author schedules closes the item. 7. Report nits; never hold approval.
skill_entry.question: If a reader opens the file whose name says it owns this thing (the config header for a constant, the subsystem header for a declaration, the third-party include block for a library header, a helper for a long stanza), do they find it there, or do they have to search the body of a file about something else?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A constexpr block the PR creates or only extends (PR 1722 hwattention.hpp:162-171; PR 2135 added hwkv_tok_per_layer at :458, 0 lines deleted; both approved silently). A constexpr function or template tied to a type above it (PR 2774 mixture_of_experts.hpp:401, :409). One constant directly above its first user (PR 4353 model.hpp:131, used at :147). A block already at the top (hwattention.hpp:30-31) or in config.hpp. A re-spelled prototype with a `-` twin (PR 3756 debug_exit, get_device). A declaration in a header the PR creates (PR 1722 :24 `devices`). Pre-existing quoted includes (four at a62d15a3dc). `<ck_pr.h>` sorted by clang-format. A placement the body explains (PR 1980, 'good enough for now'). A split the author schedules. A move another reviewer requested. Debug helpers removed with nobody asking to keep them. Brace style, whitespace, include order inside a group. t/, .py, .txt, .json. PRs of 50 lines or fewer.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Declaration: Nit: `<symbol>` (<file>:<line>) sits next to `<neighbour>` in <header> and has nothing to do with <header topic>; its definition at <src file>:<line> reads <type> from <candidate header>. Odd place for it? Maybe `<candidate header>`? Constants: kinda pedantic, but can we move these constexpr (<file>:<a>-<b>, below `<first struct>` at :<c>) to the top of the file, or into <config header> with the other <group> constants? Include: a ```suggestion block with `#include <lib/x.h>` plus 'and group it with `#include <lib/y.h>` at :<line>?' Function: `<fn>` is already <N> lines at BASE and this grows the <A> and <B> branches by <n>+<m> lines; pull the two stanzas into helpers (name them; do not claim they are copies). Next iteration would be fine.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit, in his words: 'just a nit', 'kinda pedantic', 'seems like an odd spot ... good enough for now though!', 'Next iteration would be fine though', 'That's something I could take on in a later iteration'. Minor at most for the long-function ask ('I really think we should'). He approved every member PR in the same review round: PR 1980 ten seconds after the comment (19:38:42Z comment, 19:38:52Z approval, both at 56d432ee61); PR 2176 the next day; PR 2980 three days later. He held nothing on these.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at HEAD (line of the first body, include neighbours, dump_ share); other files (the definition in src/, the candidate header, config.hpp, .clang-format); BASE for the function length; PR body for a stated placement reason; other reviewers' and the author's threads on the same hunk.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a declaration, constant block, include or growing function sits where a reader will not look for it

Common setup, in addition to the shared setup: for a merged PR, or whenever `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main` prints HEAD itself, take BASE as the parent of the first PR commit: `first=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json commits -q '.commits[0].oid'); BASE=$(git -C WT rev-parse $first^)`. When reproducing a comment, set HEAD to the commit shown next to the comment, not the final head.

0. PR kind: `gh pr view N --json title,body -q .title`. A PR that creates the header (`git -C WT diff --diff-filter=A --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp'`), a branch merge or a workaround PR drew no placement comment in the corpus (1707, 1722, 1739, 2008, 2135 silent); on such a PR run steps 2 and 3 to note, never to report.
1. Touched headers: `git -C WT diff --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp' > hdrs.txt`. Skip h/pos/config.hpp and h/system/config.hpp.
2. Constants (trigger a), per header F: `git -C WT show HEAD:F > full/F; first=$(grep -n -E '^(struct|class|union|template|inline|static|constexpr|[A-Za-z_][^;]*\))[^;]*\{ *$' full/F | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:(namespace|extern|enum)' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)` (first line that opens a struct, class or function body; a forward declaration `struct X;` does not match). Constant values below it: `grep -n -E '^(static |inline )*constexpr [^=(]*=' full/F | awk -F: -v f=$first '$1>f'`. Fire only when the hunk deletes or moves a pre-existing line of that block: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- F | grep -E '^-.*constexpr'`; no deleted line means no finding (PR 2135 added a line to the mid-file block and deleted none; PR 2176 deleted five). Candidate home: `git -C WT show HEAD:h/pos/config.hpp | grep -n -B2 'inline constexpr'` to find the group the constants belong to.
3. Declarations (trigger b): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp' | grep -E '^(\+\+\+|@@|[-+](extern|inline|struct|class|enum|template|[A-Za-z_:<>]+ [A-Za-z_]+\())'`. Drop a `+` line that has a `-` twin declaring the same symbol in the same hunk (PR 3756 re-spellings). Drop a header absent at BASE (`git -C WT cat-file -e BASE:H`). For each remaining symbol S in header H: `git -C WT grep -l -E "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_:<>*& ]*[ *&:]S\(" HEAD -- src | sed 's/^[^:]*://'` lists the defining files (column-0 definitions only; call sites are indented). For each `src/<dir>/<base>.cpp` check `git -C WT cat-file -e HEAD:h/<dir>/<base>.hpp` (`h/<base>.hpp` when dir is empty). Fire only when that same-directory header exists and is not H. Confirm the candidate: `git -C WT show HEAD:src/<dir>/<base>.cpp | sed -n '<def line>,+30p'` and name the type whose members the body reads. Header topic: `git -C WT show HEAD:H | sed -n 1,20p` for `@file` / `@brief`; when there is none (h/pos/alloc.hpp has none), take the file name and `grep -n -E '^(struct|class|[A-Za-z_].*\() ' full/H | head -2`.
4. Includes (trigger c), resolved at the PR head, never at the worktree HEAD: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -E '^\+#include "' | sed -E 's/.*"([^"]+)".*/\1/' | sort -u | while read p; do git -C WT cat-file -e HEAD:h/$p 2>/dev/null || git -C WT ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD | grep -q "$(basename $p).in$" || echo "third-party quoted: $p"; done`. For each hit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E '^#include [<"]<lib>'` lists the sibling includes and their lines; `git -C WT show HEAD:.clang-format | sed -n '/IncludeCategories/,/IncludeIsMainRegex/p'` (quoted = project group priority 3; `<lib/...>` = third-party priority 2; IncludeBlocks Regroup is what separates a quoted third-party include from its angle-bracket siblings).
5. Function growth (trigger d): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <file> | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@[^@]*@@ ?//' | sort | uniq -c` lists the functions with hunks; a blank or `extern "C" {` context is outside any function and is skipped. Length at BASE and at HEAD, indentation-aware so member functions count: `git -C WT show C:<file> > w.cpp; s=$(grep -n -E '^ *[A-Za-z_][^;]*\b<fn>\(' w.cpp | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); ind=$(sed -n "${s}p" w.cpp | sed -E 's/^( *).*/\1/'); e=$(awk -v s=$s -v ind="$ind" 'NR>s && $0 == ind"}" {print NR; exit}' w.cpp); echo $((e-s+1))`. Branches: `L=$(grep -n '<if line>' w.cpp | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); I=$(sed -n "${L}p" w.cpp | sed -E 's/^( *).*/\1/'); E=$(awk -v L=$L -v I="$I" 'NR>L && $0 == I"} else {" {print NR; exit}' w.cpp); E2=$(awk -v E=$E -v I="$I" 'NR>E && $0 == I"}" {print NR; exit}' w.cpp)`. New-side hunk starts b from `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <file> | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@ -[0-9,]+ \+([0-9]+),?([0-9]*) @@.*/\1 \2/'`: b < E -> first branch, E <= b < E2 -> second branch; sum the added lines per branch.
6. Debug helpers (trigger e), per touched header: `git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep -c -E '^(inline |static )?[A-Za-z_:<>*&]+ (dump_|debug_|print_|trace_)[a-z_]*\('` and `git -C WT ls-tree --name-only HEAD h/<dir>/ | grep -E '_(dump|debug)\.hpp'`.
7. Threads and body: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/comments --paginate | jq -r '.[] | select(.path=="F") | select(.user.login | test("\\[bot\\]") | not) | [.id,.user.login,.in_reply_to_id,.body] | @tsv' | grep -i -E 'move|config\.hpp|belongs|odd place|top of|next (phase|iteration)|later|for now'`. A row by another reviewer that asks for a move closes the item (PR 2176: 2927506780 mcherba 'These probably ought to move to h/pos/config.hpp'). A row by the author on the same hunk that schedules the split or move closes trigger (d) (PR 2980: 3405422090 'planning this as part of the next phase'). Then `grep -n -i -E 'available wherever|for now|next (phase|iteration)' body.md` for a stated reason in the body (PR 1980).
8. Report each hit as a nit with the candidate home named; do not block.

On PR 2980 (BASE f59334dc24 = parent of 514fc3ec5f; comment commits edec446b76 and 247c8a4c22; final head a62d15a3dc): step 3 finds `extern void pos_driver_register_fuse_stats() noexcept;` at edec446b76:h/pos/alloc.hpp:234 under pos_devices_register_fuse_stats (:229, allocator stats; alloc.hpp has no @file comment, struct alloc_info :24, struct allocator :50); column-0 definitions in src/pos/device.cpp:595 and src/pos/fake.cpp:72; src/pos/device.cpp -> h/pos/device.hpp exists and is not alloc.hpp (fire); fake.cpp has no same-directory header; the body reads PosDevice counters at h/pos/device.hpp:404-405; the fix 7a139971bd moved the declaration to h/pos/device.hpp:662-665 at a62d15a3dc. Step 4 at 247c8a4c22 finds exactly `third-party quoted: spdlog/spdlog.h` (src/pos/device.cpp:12) with the sibling `<spdlog/fmt/fmt.h>` at :18, separated by `<pci/pci.h>` at :15; `system/fuse_stats_config.hpp` is cleared by src/system/fuse_stats_config.hpp.in; at a62d15a3dc both are angle-bracket and adjacent at :15-16 and step 4 prints 0 hits. Step 5: hw_prepare is 467 lines at BASE (src/pos/worker.cpp:1131-1597), 601 at edec446b76 (:1141-1741), 591 at a62d15a3dc (:1141-1731); hunks +1237(44), +1287(6), +1322(4) land in `if (!workreq->attn_req) {` (:1232) and +1361(56), +1419(14), +1452(10) in `} else {` (:1326-1462): 54 + 80 added lines; the author's reply 3405422090 defers the split and Wade approved at 10d44f7aba on 2026-06-15. Steps 2 and 6: 0 hits (device.hpp constants :30-40 sit above the first body `struct wqentry {` at :54). Step 7: 24 rows on the three files, 11 by cursor[bot], dropped by the filter.

On PR 2176 (BASE 1794cdf67d, comment commit 9553cd0a11; the inline comment carries commit_id 429249ead6, the child of the approval commit 8e19ea3e62, and its line 449 matches 9553cd0a11): step 2 finds first body `struct hwattn_kv_meta {` at :37 and the hwkv_* block at h/pos/hwattention.hpp:449-452; the hunk @@ -450,98 +448,9 @@ deletes five constexpr lines of the pre-existing block (header -928/+9), so (a) fires; PAGES_PER_WMEM and POS_PER_PAGE at :30-31 are above the first body. The fix 8a6db72438 (hunk @@ -446,11 +446,8 @@) removes 9553cd0a11:h/pos/hwattention.hpp:449-453 and adds the four constants as `inline constexpr` to h/pos/config.hpp:89-92 under the comment at :88 `// HW KV cache layout constants` (lines at 8e19ea3e62). Step 7 finds 2927506780 (mcherba, 2026-03-12) asking for config.hpp, which closes the item before Wade's ask.

Over the 15 silent PRs with diffs (heads from corpus.json): step 2 as narrowed fires on 0 (the first draft fired on 1722, 2135, 2774, 4353); step 3 as narrowed fires on 0 (the basename-only draft fired on 1722 and 3756); step 4 resolved at the PR heads fires on 0 (resolved at the worktree HEAD it falsely fired on 5 project headers of 1707 and 1722); steps 5 and 6 fire on 0.

finals.label: silent-behavior-change-or-unexamined-threshold

skill_entry.name: 14. A behavior change that presents as a refactor, cleanup, one-character edit or debug-value revert
skill_entry.trigger: A hunk in h/ or src/ (never t/) of one of five shapes, with no PR-body sentence or in-hunk comment naming an input on which old and new behave differently: (a) a same-type expression swap on an executable line: an index or lookup (`x.i` to `positions[x]`), a literal used as a comparison, divisor, multiplier, sleep argument or default, a comparison operator, or a negation; (b) a removed `isnan`, `isfinite`, `isinf` or `infinity()` line while the hunk adds a helper call whose result feeds `>` or `<` against a tolerance; (c) a sleep, wait, assert, lock or check turned into a `//` comment; (d) a changed named constant that a reader compares a measured time or count against; (e) a changed comparison that resolves a build or environment default while the comment block above keeps the old meaning.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Pre-filter, never a finding: per hunk join removed and added lines, tokenize, keep pairs with at most 2 removed and 8 added tokens; drop string-literal edits, argument-list changes, type swaps, `#if`/`#define` lines, names the diff declares, one-member typedef wraps, same-value literal-to-constant swaps, inserted statements. 2. Shape (a): read both definitions at HEAD; write the coincidence condition and one differing input; none means no finding. 3. Shape (b): read the helper's NaN and inf returns; evaluate the consuming comparison (`NaN > tol` is false). 4. Shape (c): confirm no identical call is added elsewhere in the diff. 5. Shape (d): quote every reader that logs, errors or exits on a crossing; class it fatal or log-and-continue. 6. Shape (e): read the comment block, the `#define` default and the cited doc. 7. Grep the PR body, then the commit messages, for the old and new spelling.
skill_entry.question: On which input do the removed line and the added line behave differently, and does the PR body say that difference is intended?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A PR-body sentence or in-hunk comment naming the differing input class and calling the old line wrong (PR 2698 `0` to `no_readback_sentinel`, body line 9); a commit message alone never clears (1fd45e6062 named 'multiple branches' four days before Wade asked). A literal or constant change the title or body states (tron-1739 'Set page size to 128'; PR 2766 'larger max_cmd_fifo_depth'; PR 2698 'Debug-value reverts' for maxpolls, whose reader errors and exits), except a lowered limit whose reader logs and continues. A commented-out call whose identical text is added elsewhere in the diff (tron-2008, wait moved into the callees). A bare literal replacing a named value (magic-literal check, 3307459854). Removed special-value lines found verbatim at HEAD (a move). A `#define` flip (debug-switch check). Any hunk in t/.
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<file>:<line>` changes `<old>` to `<new>`. So on <input class> the code now <new behavior> where it used to <old behavior>; the PR body does not say this is intended<; commit <id> says '<quote>'>. was this intentional? If so, please say under which inputs the old line was wrong. Shape (b): don't we still need to handle NaN / inf for the comparison to be trustworthy? Shape (d): the reader at <file:line> logs on a crossing; which values have we seen on this branch, and in main? Siblings of one swap get one sentence pointing at the first finding. No value, remedy or benchmark is proposed.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal when the swap is in a production path: a plain question ('was this intentional?', 'were we grabbing the (potentially) wrong token-id all this time?', 'don't we still need to consider nan / inf values?'). When a bot already flagged it he writes one line with no severity word, either endorsing ('Cursorbot's observation seems valid', 3307473806) or asking the author directly ('was this intentional?', 3463061252, after a cursor[bot] High Severity). For a threshold he labels his own prediction as speculation and addresses the people who know the runtime ('I'm speculating we'll see a LOT more... not saying that's a reason to keep the larger value', 3236579299). Never blocking: he approved PR 1997 nine minutes after the NaN question (00:43:21Z to 00:52:27Z) and PR 2766 with 'Approved, assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments'.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (the definitions of both expressions, the comment block and `#define` above a changed comparison); other files (the helper the added line calls, every reader of a changed constant via git grep, the struct behind a typedef wrap); PR body and commit messages (a body sentence clears, a commit sentence is quoted); runtime (a log line already observed on the branch when the user gives logs; otherwise Insufficient data).

## Check 14: a behavior change that presents as a refactor, cleanup, one-character edit or debug-value revert

Setup for this check: BASE is the PR's recorded base, not origin/main.
`BASE=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefOid -q .baseRefOid)`; for an open PR whose base branch moved, `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`. On PR 2176 (base branch hwattention_sync) merge-base against origin/main gives 83 files instead of the PR's 20.
`git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src > c14.diff`

1. Pre-filter (a candidate list, never a finding). Save as step1.py, run `python3 -I step1.py c14.diff`:
```
import sys,re,difflib
TOK=re.compile(r'\w+|\S')
def hunks(p):
    f=h=None; out=[]
    for l in open(p,errors='replace'):
        l=l.rstrip('\n')
        if l.startswith('+++ '): f=l[6:]; continue
        if l.startswith('--- '): continue
        if l.startswith('@@'):
            if h: out.append(h)
            h={'file':f,'line':int(re.search(r'\+(\d+)',l).group(1)),'old':[],'new':[]}; continue
        if h is None: continue
        if l.startswith('-'): h['old'].append(l[1:].strip())
        elif l.startswith('+'): h['new'].append(l[1:].strip())
    if h: out.append(h)
    return out
cmt=lambda s: s.startswith(('//','*','/*'))
tot=kept=0
for h in hunks(sys.argv[1]):
    if not h['old'] or not h['new'] or h['file'].startswith('t/') or not h['file'].endswith(('.hpp','.cpp','.h','.cc')): continue
    if all(cmt(l) for l in h['old']+h['new']): continue
    tot+=1
    o=TOK.findall(' '.join(h['old'])); n=TOK.findall(' '.join(h['new']))
    rem=add=0
    for t,i1,i2,j1,j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(a=o,b=n,autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
        if t!='equal': rem+=i2-i1; add+=j2-j1
    if 0<rem+add and rem<=2 and add<=8:
        kept+=1; print(f"{h['file']}:{h['line']} rem={rem} add={add} | {' '.join(h['old'])[:100]} -> {' '.join(h['new'])[:100]}")
print(f"pairs={tot} kept={kept}")
```
   Joining the lines of one hunk matters: PR 2176's `size_t tok_ix = enclosing_state.token_positions[...]` is wrapped over two `+` lines, and a line-by-line pairing never sees one expression. Then drop, by reading each kept line once: (i) the change is inside a string literal; (ii) tokens only added to or removed from an argument, parameter or capture list; (iii) a type name swapped in a declaration (`float` to `double`, `uint32_t` to `process_device_id`); (iv) `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#define` lines (debug-switch check); (v) the new name is declared in the diff (rename map, a new accessor `used` to `used()`, a new setter `set_node(...)`); (vi) a strong typedef wrapped or unwrapped (`x` to `x.i`, `T{x}`) whose struct holds one data member: `git -C WT grep -n 'struct <T>' HEAD -- h`, once per type; (vii) a literal replaced by a named constant with the same value at HEAD (magic-literal check); (viii) an inserted statement (added tokens contain `;` or `{`). Name the pair, kept and surviving counts in the report.
2. Shape (b): `grep -n -E '^-.*(isnan|isfinite|isinf|infinity\(\))' c14.diff`; for each hit `git -C WT grep -n -F -- '<removed line>' HEAD -- h src` (a verbatim hit at HEAD is a move; drop). Otherwise list the `+` lines of the same hunk matching `\b(comberr|abserr|relerr|approx_equal|is_close)\s*\(` and the `>` or `<` comparison that consumes the result; read the helper at HEAD and write its return for a NaN on either side and for an inf on one side; evaluate the comparison with that value.
3. Shape (c): `grep -n -E '^\+\s*//\s*(usleep|sleep|nanosleep|wait\w*|mwaitx|TRON_ASSERT|assert|lock|unlock|check\w*)\s*\(' c14.diff` (the `\(` keeps prose comments such as `// mwaitx-waitable views` out); confirm the same text is a `-` line of the hunk; then `grep -c -F '+  <call text>' c14.diff`: a replacement call added elsewhere means the statement moved (do not fire).
4. Shape (d): `grep -E '^[-+]\s*(inline )?(static )?constexpr' c14.diff | sed -E 's/^([-+]).*\b(\w+)\s*=\s*([0-9]+).*/\1 \2 \3/' | awk '{k=$2; if($1=="-") o[k]=$3; else n[k]=$3} END{for(k in o) if(k in n && o[k]!=n[k]) print k, o[k], "->", n[k]}'` (a name with the same value on both sides is a moved constant, not a change). For each name `git -C WT grep -n '<constant>' HEAD -- h src`; quote every reader with `spdlog::|debug_exit|TRON_ASSERT` within 5 lines of the comparison and class it fatal (error then exit) or log-and-continue. A constant no reader compares a measured value against (a ring size, a page size, a max layer count) is not a candidate.
5. Shape (e): `grep -n -E '^[-+].*(DEFAULT_ON|_DEFAULT|_ENABLED|DEFAULT).*(!=|==) *[01]\b' c14.diff`; keep only a `-`/`+` pair of the same line (the draft's `return (true|false);` alternative matched 7 added lines on PR 3016 and 2 on tron-2875 that resolve no default). `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<line-15>,<line>p'` for the comment block and the `#define`; `grep -n '<MACRO>' doc/*.md`.
6. Shape (a) definitions: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<old container>;|<new container>;' HEAD -- h`, `git -C WT grep -n 'struct <type>' HEAD -- h` (read the comment on validity), `git -C WT grep -n '<new container>.push_back' HEAD -- h src` (the fill site); write the coincidence condition and one differing input. No differing input, no finding.
7. Intent: `grep -n -i -E '<old token>|<new token>|intention|deliberate|debug-only|revert' body.md`: a body sentence that names the input class, or lists the value change, clears. `git -C WT log --format='%h %s%n%b' BASE..HEAD | grep -n -i -E '<old token>|<new token>'`: a commit sentence does not clear; quote it in the finding and ask for it in the body or at the line.
8. Observed values (shape d): `grep -rn '<log string>' <run logs>` only when the user gives logs; otherwise write `Insufficient data: no run log` and quote the reader line.
9. One finding per hunk, phrased as a question with both behaviors on the named input; siblings with the same removed and added tokens get one pointer sentence.

finals.label: tests-run-at-head-before-approve
finals.disposition: widen_existing (check 3), merged with the other check-3 widening. Check 3 today asks one question: does a gated assertion execute on the lane that gates the PR. Wade's record shows the wider theme: before he approves a hardware-path or scheduler-path change, he wants evidence that a run exercised the changed path at the reviewed head, in every build configuration the diff touches. When the PR makes a test statement that does not cover the changed path, he asks the author (2915270383: one runtron command named while the hunks sit under `#ifdef FWD_HW_RESULTS`; 4265644124: a test plan of clang-format and whitespace only; 3156090573: a `--users 1` repro under a bot finding about duplicate shards). Twice he ran tests himself and pasted the result: a full ctest summary of 69 tests (4131374395) and a `Running t_... PASS` list of 13 binaries (4422833076). On all four member heads the gating lane `CMake and CTest` (cmake-single-platform.yml) produced no ctest run (verified with gh api): at 8f22c93862 and 9d0d649274 the workflow did not run at all because its `pull_request: branches:` list omitted the base branch (hwattention_sync at 8f22c93862; wm-bill-hwsync1 at 9d0d649274); at e76638c63e, 1d3ff17c9d and 159e09a940 `lint | failure` skipped the `build` job (`needs: lint`), which held the ctest steps. The row named `test` on those heads is the job `test` of test-release-build.yml, gated by the label `Continuous integration`, which none of the four PRs carries; it says nothing about ctest and is not read by this check. The widening keeps the existing trigger as Trigger A and adds Trigger B (insufficient test statement at HEAD). The heading is shared with the item test-silently-skips-or-cannot-fail, which also widens check 3 under Trigger A; this item owns Trigger B only.

skill_entry.name: 3. A check on the changed path must execute, and a run must be named, at the reviewed head
skill_entry.trigger: Trigger A (unchanged): a runtime assertion on stored bytes or indices sits below a runtime exit on a hardware or environment probe. Trigger B, all three: (1) the diff changes non-comment, non-formatting lines on a hardware-facing path (h/pos/, src/pos/, h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp, h/tron/scheduler/), a production constant (timeout, sentinel), or a region under a defined macro whose `#else` or `#ifndef` twin reads an identifier the hunk assigns; (2) the job that runs ctest has no success row at HEAD; (3) the PR text (body, commits, comments) makes a test statement that does not cover the changed path: static checks only, one named run beside such a gated hunk, or a repro whose flags exclude the runtime scenario a High-severity bot finding names.
skill_entry.procedure: Trigger A: steps 1-8 unchanged. Trigger B: merged PR: BASE from `.base.sha`. Read the check runs at HEAD; find the job whose step runs `ctest` or `bin/slice run`; ignore the row named `test` (test-release-build.yml, label-gated). State the cause: `needs: lint` after a lint failure, or a `pull_request: branches:` filter omitting the base. Map each hunk to its preprocessor region by script; grep the twin for the identifiers the hunk assigns. List tests by link line in t/CMakeLists.txt (`pos` library, `LABELS fpga`, `DISABLED TRUE`). Collect test statements from body, commits and comments; match each to a configuration. Keep bot findings at HEAD that name a runtime scenario. With a labelled host run and paste the summary; otherwise `Insufficient data`.
skill_entry.question: Which run, named by binary or command, by build configuration and by commit, executed the changed path at this head, and where on the PR does it say so? If a changed hunk sits under `#ifdef X` and the twin region reads the state the hunk writes, did a build with X in the opposite state compile and run too?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A PR with no test statement in body, commits or comments (Wade approved 2135, 2008 and 1827 in silence: same author and base as 2148, lane never ran). Comment-only, test-only, documentation-only and one-line PRs. A ctest job that succeeded at HEAD when no gated twin reads the hunk's state. Formatting-only hunks (`git diff -w` empty). Regions under a commented-out or never-defined macro (`// #define MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG`). Static bot findings (sizeof, bound, duplicate constant): verify-automated-findings owns them. `(Disabled)` rows in a ctest summary. `#if 0` blocks the author still needs. A WIP body on a feature-branch base. A run cited at an older id: check 8 owns it. Never block: the strongest form is a conditional approval or a question.
skill_entry.finding_shape: 'do these changes for <feature> work when `<MACRO>` is UNdefined as well? Did you sanity test that?' or 'Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs (<binaries from the link line>) against these changes before merging.' or, under a bot finding that names a runtime scenario, 'I think this is a legit concern... did you run any <multi-user | repeated-iteration> tests to see if you encounter this issue?' With a labelled host, state the result instead: 'all the UTs pass out of this branch as well:' followed by the pasted summary (`100% tests passed, N tests failed out of M`, the Label Time Summary and the `(Disabled)` rows).
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal, as a question or as a condition on an approval, never a block (0 CHANGES_REQUESTED in 334 reviews): "Approved, but please run ..." (4265644124; review state COMMENTED at 1d3ff17c9d, the prose says Approved; the APPROVED state is 4339065826 at 159e09a940 ten days later with an empty body), "Did you sanity test that?" (2915270383), "I think this is a legit concern" (3156090573). When he has the machine he states the result instead of asking: "all the UTs pass out of this branch as well" (4131374395, a 69-test ctest summary) and "The following set of UTs ran/passed against these changes" (4422833076, 13 binaries).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the changed region and its macro), full file (the `#else` or `#ifndef` twin and the identifiers it reads), other files (t/CMakeLists.txt link lines and labels; the other files that test the macro), PR body plus commit messages plus comments (test statements, runtron repro flags), CI (check runs at HEAD; the job whose step runs ctest or bin/slice run; the workflow `on:` block and `needs:` lines), bot findings at HEAD with a runtime scenario, runtime (the run itself; needs a host with the hardware label and a build of HEAD).

## Check 3 (widened): a check on the changed path must execute, and a run must be named, at the reviewed head

Steps 1-8 unchanged (Trigger A, gated assertion). Trigger B (insufficient test statement at HEAD) adds:

BASE on a merged PR: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq '"\(.base.sha) \(.merge_commit_sha)"'`; cross-check with `git -C WT merge-base HEAD <merge_commit_sha>^1`. Do not use `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` on a merged PR: it returns HEAD (PR 2148: `git merge-base 8f22c93862 origin/hwattention_sync` = 8f22c93862; `.base.sha` = e2ce886cca). If BASE or HEAD is not in WT, `gh pr diff N --repo positron-ai/tron` gives the same diff (749 lines for PR 2148).

9. Check runs at HEAD: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/HEAD/check-runs --paginate --jq '.check_runs[] | "\(.name) | \(.conclusion) | \(.app.slug)"'`. Find the job that runs the tests by its step, never by a row name: `git -C WT show HEAD:.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml | grep -n -E '^  [a-zA-Z_-]+:$|^    name:|needs:|^    if:|ctest|slice run'` and read the job name above the `ctest` or `bin/slice run` line. At the 2025-12 to 2026-06 heads that job is `build` (row `build`; `ctest -LE fpga` and `ctest -L fpga` at cmake-single-platform.yml:265/:271 at 8f22c93862, :391/:399 at 159e09a940). State the cause of a missing test-job row as one of: (a) the lane never ran because `on: pull_request: branches:` omits the PR base (`sed -n '/^on:/,/^[a-z]/p'`; 8f22c93862 has `branches: [ "main" ]`, PR 2148 base hwattention_sync; 9d0d649274 has `["main", "hwattention_sync"]`, PR 2461 base wm-bill-hwsync1); (b) the lane ran but `lint | failure` skipped the test job through `needs: lint` (cmake-single-platform.yml:123 at 8f22c93862, :173 at 159e09a940; PRs 2565 and 2698).
10a. Preprocessor map per changed file: `git -C WT show HEAD:<f> | grep -n -E '^#(ifdef|ifndef|if|else|elif|endif)([ \t]|$)'` (no trailing space in the pattern: bare `#else` and `#endif` must match; the pattern with a trailing space hides the `#else` at self_attention.hpp:724).
10b. Enclosing region of each hunk, by script: hunk starts `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <f> | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@ -[0-9,]+ \+([0-9]+).*/\1/'`; for each start L: `git -C WT show HEAD:<f> | awk -v L=$L 'NR>L{exit} /^#(ifdef|ifndef|if)[ \t]/{d++;n[d]=$0;s[d]=NR;next} /^#else/{n[d]=n[d] " [else@" NR "]";next} /^#endif/{d--;next} END{for(i=1;i<=d;i++) printf " > %s@%d", n[i], s[i]; print (d?"":" top level")}'`.
10c. For each macro X that encloses a hunk: the macro counts only when it is defined by an uncommented `#define X` in the file or by a CMake, preset or `-D` line (`git -C WT grep -n -E 'define X|-DX' HEAD -- CMakeLists.txt CMakePresets.json nix h src`); `// #define X` is not a configuration. The region counts only when X has an `#else` or `#ifndef X` twin in the file and the twin reads an identifier the hunk assigns: identifiers `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <f> | grep '^+' | grep -o -E '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\[[^]]*\])? *(=|\.wait|\.data)' | sort -u`; twin read `git -C WT show HEAD:<f> | sed -n '<else>,<endif>p' | grep -n -E '<ident1>|<ident2>'`. Record how many other files test X (`git -C WT grep -l '<X>' HEAD -- h src`). An in-file `#define` means every run named on the PR used the defined state unless a sentence says otherwise.
11. Tests that can reach the touched code, from the link line: `git -C WT show HEAD:t/CMakeLists.txt | grep add_catch_test | grep -E 'LIBRARIES[^)]*\b(pos|full_scheduler)\b'` (binaries that link the real hardware library; 22 at 8f22c93862); `grep -E 'LABELS fpga'` (need a card; 21); `grep 'DISABLED TRUE'` (never run; 6). One runtron command is one configuration and, with `--users 1` or `--iterations 1`, one user or one iteration only. No test statement at all: do not fire.

skill_entry.name: 3A. A test must run, reach its assertion and observe the defect on the lane that gates the PR (3B, from the item tests-run-at-head-before-approve, covers a run the author did not do; do not interleave the two triggers)
skill_entry.trigger: Any of five, in t/. (a) Probe exit: a formula assertion on stored bytes below a return or SKIP gated by a hardware or environment probe (`available()`, getenv, FPGA). (b) Unconditional exit: an added `return;` or `SKIP(` whose owner line is TEST_CASE, TEST_CASE_METHOD or SECTION, with REQUIRE/CHECK below. (c) Selection gate: a tag gains a leading `.` or `[!mayfail]`, or add_catch_test leaves t/CMakeLists.txt, unnamed in body or commits. (d) Fake boundary: a new assertion observes counts, sizes or sampled bytes while the call hands addresses, fetchers, offsets or lengths to a fake with unnamed parameters or a bare `return {...}`. (e) Stale artifact: an added line names a fixed path the test or a helper writes and the HEAD file reads back, with no remove or unique name.
skill_entry.procedure: BASE = merge-base(HEAD, PR base.sha). (a) steps 1-8 unchanged. (b) map added `return;` or `SKIP(` to HEAD; find the owner line; proceed only for TEST_CASE, TEST_CASE_METHOD or SECTION; count REQUIRE/CHECK lines to the unit end; date with `git log -G`. (c) pair the `-`/`+` TEST_CASE lines; a dot-only change is a hidden tag; grep the file for pre-existing `[.`, body and subjects for the test name or 'disable'. (d) name the production call, follow it to the fake entry point; drop assertions whose `-` twin differs only by the rename map; write the break each discarded argument hides; list index classes. (e) pair each added fixed name with a later read; grep for cleanup; locate the writer helper. State five facts.
skill_entry.question: If the production code were wrong in the way this test claims to guard, which assertion fails on the lane that gates the PR, on a runner without the hardware, on a second run? In Wade's words: 'did you intend to leave this return / disable this test?', and for a fake: which incorrect bases, fetchers, offsets or lengths 'would still pass'?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A gated assertion whose contract a non-gated independent assertion covers (name it). A hidden tag present at BASE, a bench or stress tag, or one whose comment states the reason (t_weight_load_reuse.cpp:328-330 at c5d44bd86f). A binary with LABELS fpga, min_slices_N or DISABLED TRUE (selection; list it), and an opt-in getenv mode inside it (PR 2475). A fake that records the arguments a test reads (fake.cpp:376-396 at 7f80aa17da). A conditional exit whose comment names the covering test. A `return;` owned by `if constexpr`, a loop or a helper (PR 4353 t_llama_unit.cpp:2661). `#if 0` and commented-out assertions belong to disabled-code-left-in. A writer line present at BASE (PRs 1985, 3756). Test-only PRs 1978, 1985, 2475, 2939 and RESOURCE_LOCK-only 2844 passed silently. Never ask the author to run the suite as the remedy, never claim to have run it.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (a) 'This is the only check of <contract> against a formula that does not go through <helper>, but it sits after the <probe> early return at :<line>, so it does not execute on <lane>. Move it above the early return, or into <closest non-gated test>.' (b)/(c) one lowercase question: 'did you intend to leave this `return`?' / 'did you intend to disable this test?' (add '<N> REQUIREs at :<lines> no longer run' when the hunk hides them). (d) 'Coverage gap: `<fake fn>` (`<file:lines>`) discards <arguments>; these tests inspect <what>, so incorrect <bases, fetchers, offsets, lengths> would still pass. Please extend <existing suite> to observe <boundary> with <nonzero index, partial window, page boundary>; the current assertions do not establish that contract.' (e) 'does this test clean up any existing artifacts it previously generated, each time it runs?'
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: No 'nit' on any member. (b), (c), (e): a bare lowercase question with no severity word; he approved PR 1920 33 minutes after the artifact question (18:34:57Z question, 19:08:11Z approval, no reply) and PR 2011 54 seconds after the restoring commit d4795f37a5 (20:38:08Z commit, 20:39:02Z approval), so the question form is non-blocking. (d): bold 'Coverage gap:' headline, closed by 'the current packing assertions do not establish that contract' and, on the sibling comment 3960538961, 'I have not observed a lost-GOF or premature-completion failure in the implementation' (a gap, not a defect). (a): declarative fact plus 'Move it ...', no severity word; the author moved the case.

BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $BASE_SHA)

skill_entry.name: 9. Passages a later reader cannot use: PR-body sections, code comments and Notes
skill_entry.trigger: Part A (unchanged): the PR body has a Status, Verification, Tests or Results section; the body procedure runs only inside those sections. Part B, on the diff under h/, src/ or t/, any one: (B1) an added comment line carries a review label (class R: 'PR <n> review|round|comment', 'review round', 'round <n>', 'comment W<n>', 'R<n>-M<n>', 'as discussed with') in any of the three trees, or a tracker id (class T: Story or STORY-<n>, ticket <n>, JIRA, issue #<n>) under h/ or src/; (B2) an added '// Note [name]' line, at any indentation, followed by the tilde line; (B3) a comment of one to three lines directly above a general-purpose statement (TRACE_EVENT, log call, TRON_ASSERT, counter) that says 'See Note [<a Note this PR adds>]' or names a Note or identifier the PR introduces.
skill_entry.procedure: BASE = merge-base(base.sha from gh api, HEAD); require 0 merges in BASE..HEAD. B1: grep added comment lines, map to HEAD lines, count comments per file (adjacent lines are one comment). Delete the reference: fact still stated = offer that sentence (suggestion block if one line); only history left = ask for what the code guarantees. Class-T hits under t/ are 'also in' lines after an h/ or src/ hit. B2: count comment lines; grep cites outside the file; grep below the tilde line for narrative markers (NaN, crash, wrong, bug, the fix, used to, no longer, the latter put); grep the body for the marker line's parenthesis text. Markers plus body overlap = history whatever the cite count: ask for about five lines at the cited declaration. No marker = keep. B3: git grep every statement token at BASE; all present = justification; ask once per PR to drop the comment and keep the statement. Final head: zero hits, zero cites of a removed Note.
skill_entry.question: Body: if the reviewer could only open GitHub, would deleting this clause change any decision about the head? Code: if a reader in two years had only the code, no GitHub and no tracker, would deleting this comment line, or this whole Note, lose a fact the code must honor, or only the story of who asked for it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A story id or review label in the PR title or a commit subject (PR 2906 '(Story 2814)', PR 4596 '(review round 4, W2)'). A 'See Note [X]' cite of a mechanism Note (13 cites of Note [GOF staging eviction], 2 of Note [Attention path stats]). A long mechanism Note or comment (79-line Note [Attention path stats]; the 12-line inflight_guard comment gof.hpp:105-116 at ffc2d6156a drew only the 'public:' nit). A tracker id in a test file alone (tron-2475 t/t_clearhbm.cpp:47, :83, :150 STORY-397/396 approved silently; the four t/ 'Story 2814' lines of PR 2906 unmarked). A second B3 comment in one PR (src/tron/gof.cpp:89-92 survived to 678f559d5d). A comment longer than three lines above an assert (tron-2875 full.hpp:1656-1661). A TODO with a tracker id. 'ticket 5' as a sequencing token. Prose under doc/. A bare 'see PR #n' pointer: Insufficient data.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Body: unchanged. B1: 'probably don't want to reference "PR <n> review round <k> comment W<x>" like this... seems there are more (<N> comments in <file>). Scrub please.' One-liner: a suggestion block, 'don't mention Story numbers in comments', 'Story <n> frees X' becomes 'X is freed'. B2: 'I'm not sure this (basically) bug-fix is worthy of its own noisy Note. It's not like we are defining some fancy algorithm we need to document; a short comment at <declaration> saying <invariant> is enough.' B3: 'we don't really need this comment IMO... and this <TRACE_EVENT label> really isn't related to Note [<name>] directly. It's a useful event no matter the context.'
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: minor, never blocking: 'probably don't want to', 'we don't really need this comment IMO', 'I'm not sure this ... is worthy', 'Scrub please', 'minor nit'. One comment per file area plus 'seems there are more'; a suggestion block when the fix is one line; one B3 ask per PR. All five members were changed by the author before approval; he approved PR 4596 at the scrubbed head 441e81178b, PR 2906 at ffc2d6156a and PR 4007 at 3a8544cd35.

6. Reference grep over added comment lines, two classes (awk has no `\b`; keep the pattern free of it; append reviewer logins to PATR if the PR text names them):
```
PATR='(PR ?#?[0-9]{3,5}[ ,]+(review|round|comment)|review round|round [0-9]|comment [WR][0-9]|R[0-9]+-M[0-9]+|as discussed with)'
PATT='([Ss][Tt][Oo][Rr][Yy][ -]?#?[0-9]+|[Tt]icket[ -]?#?[A-Z]*-?[0-9]+|JIRA|issue #[0-9]+)'
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -E '^\+\+\+|^@@|^\+' | awk -v pr="$PATR" -v pt="$PATT" '/^\+\+\+/{f=substr($0,7)} /^@@/{split($0,a," "); split(a[3],b,","); n=substr(b[1],2)+0; next} /^\+/{ if ($0 ~ /^\+[ \t]*(\/\/|\*|\/\*)/) { if ($0 ~ pr) print "R " f":"n": "substr($0,2); else if ($0 ~ pt) print "T " f":"n": "substr($0,2) } n++}' | tee c9-hits.txt
awk '{print $1, $2}' c9-hits.txt | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c     # hit LINES per class and file
```
