skill_entry.name: 14. A new path, state, counter or option must be visible to the operator through the tools the team already uses
skill_entry.trigger: (a) Debug dump: new data members in a type whose HEAD print helper (debug_string, dump, to_string, operator<<) the diff leaves untouched. (b) Trace coverage: a new src/ file in a directory where no file contains TRACE_EVENT, plus an added function that loops over a container inside a lock scope or is named drain_*, expand_* or *_oom, with no trace macro added. (c) Exit-time counter: build-gated counters printed once from a static destructor while fuse_stats.hpp exists. (d) Launcher wiring: a new cxxopts row coupled by its parse to an option that a perfetto/ or bin/ launcher sets itself. (e) Sample output: a new perfetto::Category, TRACE_COUNTER, track or rendered report with no image, excerpt or capture location in the body.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Debug dump: list added members (and enum class lines). At HEAD bound the enclosing type, its helper and the helper body; grep each member; zero hits is a gap. 2. Trace: count TRACE_EVENT per sibling of the new src/ file; list added functions holding both a loop and a lock, or named drain_, expand_ or oom; drop register_, init_, setup_ functions; grep for the category header (context only). 3. Counter: a file with a gate hit (not TRON_FUSE_STATS_ENABLED) and a report hit; compare with fuse_stats.hpp on enable time, live read, interval. 4. Launcher: read the launcher exec line and usage for the coupled option. 5. Sample: grep the body for an image, code block or capture path.
skill_entry.question: Can an operator who runs the normal tools (the debug dump, a Perfetto trace, the FUSE stats tree, the launcher script) see, measure or switch on what this PR adds, today, without rebuilding or reading the source?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Counters already registered in FUSE (PR 2980: Wade asked only about the atomics and the dump). A steady-state per-operation path: Wade closed his own PR 2713 question with "No action needed, just inquiring." before the author's 20 ns per operation reply. A new environment variable (tron-4353, 3879, 4596: no launcher ask). A merge or sync step of an existing branch (tron-1707, 1722, 1739 passed with a new untraced src/pos file). A one-time registration or init loop. A FUSE leaf, debug_string helper, dbg_* log line or test-output change as the subject of a sample ask (PR 2980, tron-1707, tron-1985 silent). A test-only knob or CMake test row. Never raise above a question: PR 4267 and 2713 were approved with it open.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Debug dump: "add these to the `<helper>` utility for printing?" Trace: "wouldn't it be useful to have some TRACE_EVENTs across <paths>? there is no `<subsystem>` category in perfetto.hpp either. No action needed, just asking." Counter: "I'm ok approving as-is, but did you look at using FUSE for this? collection could still be opt-in via env-var, then the counters could be read live and over chosen intervals." Launcher: "<script> is how people launch <binary> with <coupled flag>. So that script needs to take `<new flag>` and forward it (like it does other options today)." Sample: "do you have a couple screenshots of these new <captures> you could share?"

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a new path, state, counter or option must be visible through the tools the team already uses

Setup additions for this check (the common setup's BASE formula fails on a merged PR, because the reviewed commit is then an ancestor of origin/main and `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself):

```
# BASE for a merged PR: the parent of the PR's first commit
BASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/commits --jq '.[0].parents[0].sha')
git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main && echo merged   # records why the common formula was not used
# HEAD for an inline comment: the commit of the review that posted it (not the comment's own commit_id, which GitHub re-stamps)
gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/comments/<id> --jq '.commit_id[0:10] + " " + .original_commit_id[0:10] + " line=" + (.original_line|tostring)'
gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/reviews --jq '.[] | .submitted_at + " " + .commit_id[0:10] + " " + .state'
# HEAD for an issue comment: the last push before the comment time
gh api --paginate repos/positron-ai/tron/issues/N/timeline --jq '.[] | select(.event=="head_ref_force_pushed") | .created_at + " " + .commit_id[0:10]'
gh api 'repos/positron-ai/tron/compare/<last force-push sha>...<next review commit>' --jq '.commits[] | .sha[0:10] + " " + .commit.committer.date'   # regular pushes after the force push
# If git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD fails (pre-rebase commit), read files from GitHub and say so in the finding
gh api "repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD" --jq .content | base64 -d | grep -n -F -- '<flag>'
```

1. Debug dump. Added members: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp' | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@)|^\+\s+[^/(]+\s[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*(\s*=[^;]*|\{[^}]*\})?;'` (an added line with a type, a lowercase name, an optional initializer and a semicolon, no parenthesis); kind enums: `... | grep -n -E '^\+\s+enum (class )?'`. Take the type name from the `@@ ... struct <T> {` context. Bound the type and find its helper: `F=$(mktemp); git -C WT show HEAD:<file> > $F; S=$(grep -n -E "^(struct|class) <T>\b" $F | cut -d: -f1); E=$(awk -v s=$S 'NR>s && /^};/ {print NR; exit}' $F); sed -n "${S},${E}p" $F | grep -n -E 'std::string (debug_string|to_string|dump)\(|operator<<\('` (add S-1 to the printed line). Body end: `awk -v l=<helper line> 'NR>l && /^  }$/ {print NR; exit}' $F`. Then `sed -n '<helper>,<end>p' $F > body.txt; for m in <members>; do echo $m $(grep -c $m body.txt); done`. If the helper is only declared in the header, grep src/ for `<T>::debug_string(` and bound the body there. Zero hits for a state member = gap.
2. Trace coverage. New src files: `git -C WT diff --diff-filter=A --name-only BASE HEAD -- src`. For each new file's directory: `for f in $(git -C WT ls-tree --name-only HEAD <dir>); do echo "$f $(git -C WT show HEAD:$f | grep -c TRACE_EVENT)"; done`; continue only when every sibling is 0. Added functions holding both a loop and a lock: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- src h | awk '/^\+.*\)( const| noexcept)* \{$/ {fn=$0} /^\+.*for \(/ {loop[fn]=1} /^\+.*(lock_guard|unique_lock|scoped_lock)/ {lock[fn]=1} END {for (f in loop) if (lock[f]) print f}'`; also `grep -n -E '^\+.*(drain_|expand_|_oom)'`. Drop functions named register_*, init_* or setup_*, or called once from main or from a *_register_* path; state the caller of each hit. Added trace macros: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- src h | grep -c -E '^\+.*(TRACE_EVENT|TRACE_COUNTER|TRON_CHECKPOINT)'`. Category context: `git -C WT grep -l 'perfetto::Category(' HEAD -- h` (h/tron/perfetto.hpp before f3cc5baded of 2026-01-13, h/common/perfetto.hpp after) and list its names; if neither exists write Insufficient data. A missing category is context for the question, never a trigger.
3. Exit-time counter. Gate list: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -P '^\+.*(option\(TRON_|#ifdef TRON_(?!FUSE|PERFETTO)|#if TRON_)'`. Report list: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(fprintf\(stderr|spdlog::(info|warn)\(.*count|report_at_exit|~[a-z_]+\(\) \{)'`. A file with hits in both lists is a candidate; a gate hit alone is not. For a candidate: `git -C WT show HEAD:README.stats.md | sed -n 1,40p`; `git -C WT show HEAD:h/system/fuse_stats.hpp | grep -n -E 'make_file|set_read_callback'`; `git -C WT show HEAD:h/system/fuse_tronstats.hpp | grep -n register_tronstats_metric_descriptor`; env-var precedent: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'getenv\("(TRON|RZ)_' HEAD -- h src | head`. Record the three axes (enable time, live read, interval). If README.stats.md or fuse_stats.hpp is absent at HEAD, write Insufficient data.
4. Launcher wiring. New option rows: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- src/runtron.cpp src/rinzler.cpp | grep -n -E '^\+\s*\("[a-z-]+",'`. Coupling: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- src/runtron.cpp src/rinzler.cpp | grep -n -E 'args.count\("|requires --|overrides'`; record the coupled option. Launchers: `git -C WT grep -n -E '"\$RUNTRON"|gen/runtron|bin/runtron' HEAD -- perfetto bin ci`; for each, `grep -n -F -- '--<coupled>'` on its exec line and usage (`sed -n '/^usage()/,/^}/p'`). If the launcher sets the coupled option and `git -C WT grep -n -F -- '--<new flag>' HEAD -- perfetto bin ci` is empty, that is the gap. Compile-time knobs: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+#define [A-Z_]+ [01]$'` are not launcher-reachable by construction; send one to step 3 only when it gates a counter or a report. A getenv addition never counts here. Do not demand a usage line for an option that stands alone (perfetto/tronperf names 4 of the 47 runtron options at main 2026-10-06).
5. Sample output. Only when the diff adds a `perfetto::Category(`, `TRACE_COUNTER`, a new track or annotation name, or a report format whose look a reader cannot predict from the code. Then `grep -n -E '!\[|\.png|\.pftrace|```|/scratch/|/var/tmp/|/home/' body.md`; an image, a decoded excerpt, a repository path or a named capture location (even a machine-local path, as on PR 3490) counts as a sample and closes the ask. Check 9 still reports a machine-local path as unusable to a GitHub reader; the two checks do not conflict. A FUSE leaf or a one-integer counter never needs a sample.
6. One question per gap, in the finding shape. Say it is not a condition of approval.

skill_entry.name: 8. Result rows, body sentences and the branch state match the reviewed head
skill_entry.trigger: Any one: (a) the body reports a measurement of the PR's code (test counts, token identity, perf A/B, objdump, lint, build) under a Verification, Status, Tests or Results heading; (b) a non-merge commit by the PR author inside BASE..HEAD has a committer date after the body's last edit (createdAt when the body was never edited), or its subject contains 'review round', 'review feedback', 'Apply suggestions from code review' or 'Integrate review'; (c) `gh pr view N --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` answers CONFLICTING or DIRTY at the head being approved; (d) the body says a file is ported, copied, extracted, cherry-picked or originally authored from a named branch or PR; (e) a push arrives while an inline thread the reviewer himself opened holds an unresolved suggestion block.
skill_entry.procedure: Resolve BASEREF, BASEOID and HEAD first; BASE = merge-base HEAD BASEOID, never origin/main. Result rows: hex ids containing a letter in those sections; cat-file, is-ancestor against HEAD, gh commits (404 or 422 = twin); per ancestor list the PR files changed since; verdict per row. Body: LAST = the last body edit before the review being written; list the author's non-merge commits after LAST; for each body sentence whose symbol, key or count one of those commits touched (git log -S), grep the identifier the commit subject names at HEAD and count TEST_CASE in the named test file. Branch: gh mergeable live; merge-tree conflict markers for a posted review. Ported file: diff the PR copy against the source head dated at the review; a symbol only in the PR copy that a source commit removed is the finding. Suggestion: grep the thread's original line text at HEAD.
skill_entry.question: Does the description, including every result id and every mechanism sentence the review-round commits touched, describe this head; does this head merge into its target branch as it stands; does a ported file match its source branch head; and is every suggestion thread the reviewer opened applied at this push?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Ids in a commit or review-outcome table; the target-branch baseline id; reference bands from outside the PR. A row with no id when no commit postdates the body's last edit (PR 2475). A body edited after the last code commit, an empty body, or a sentence no post-edit commit touched (a never-true claim is check 6). BEHIND, or a target tip that is not an ancestor of HEAD, with a clean merge-tree (19 of 36 silent tron PRs). A ported copy that lacks source symbols: first-step merge (PR 1707), extraction (PR 2844), cherry-pick plus own changes (PR 2875); a difference the body states as held back (PR 2676, POS_PER_PAGE); 'ported' inside 'reported'. Commit count (PR 4596 approved at 26). Follow-ups the author agreed to. A bot's resolved suggestion thread. Whether the rebase or refresh happened afterwards.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Result row: 'PR description, <section>: the <kind> rows cite <id>, <event>; <files> changed since then. Please <re-run at <HEAD> | delete them, the rows at <HEAD> replace them | mark them pre-merge and say which files did not change>.' Stale body at approval (absorbs the result rows; not blocking): 'I think your PR description is stale at this point: it says <clause>, but at <HEAD> <symbol or count> is <value> (<commit>). Please refresh it; also you currently have a merge conflict.' Ported file: 'this is an old version. <path> still declares <symbols> that <source> dropped in <commit>. ## Check 8: result rows, body sentences and the branch state match the reviewed head

Setup for this check (replaces `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $HEAD origin/main)` for every check):
```
read BASEREF BASEOID HEADOID < <(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName,baseRefOid,headRefOid -q '[.baseRefName,.baseRefOid,.headRefOid]|@tsv')
HEAD=<the reviewed head; $HEADOID for a live review>
BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $HEAD $BASEOID)
```
After a merge, `merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself (PR 4596: 441e81178b, 0 commits, 0 files); baseRefOid is the target-branch commit GitHub compared against and stays correct (66c7bb8db1, 26 non-merge commits, 11 files). PR 2233 targeted hwattention_sync; never hard-code origin/main.

1. Live state: `gh pr view N --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus,state,mergedAt`.
2. Section ranges: headings whose text contains Verification, Status, Tests or Results, ending at the next heading of the same or higher level.
3. Ids: `grep -oE '\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b' body.md | grep -E '[a-f]' | sort -u`, restricted to measurement rows in those sections; drop hits inside fenced code blocks and JSON samples (PR 4596 live body: 23 of 32 raw hits are decimal counter values). A row without an id takes the nearest "Binary:" or "at <id>" line of its section; a section with no id at all and no commit newer than the body's last edit (step 7) describes HEAD and is accepted (PR 2475).
4. Per id: `git -C WT cat-file -t ID`; `git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor ID $HEAD`; `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/ID --jq .sha` (404 or 422 = GitHub cannot show it). Not resolving or not an ancestor = twin -> finding, unless the body itself states the difference ("ebadce2adb as f7da0e64ab, which differs by one comment line": accepted). A twin's dates give the event: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/ID --jq '.commit.author.date, .commit.committer.date'` equal to HEAD's author date = amend or rebase of the same commit. Invent no further history.
5. Per ancestor id: `git -C WT rev-list --count --first-parent ID..$HEAD`; `git -C WT rev-list --parents ID..$HEAD | awk 'NF>2'` (a two-parent commit = merge of the target branch); `for f in $(cat prfiles.txt); do git -C WT diff --quiet ID $HEAD -- $f || echo $f; done`.
6. Row verdict: id == HEAD -> fine; id behind with no label -> finding; a label with the unchanged PR files, the re-run date or a stated difference -> accepted. A present-tense phrase ("ran at the head X", "now", "current") next to a non-HEAD id -> finding. Ask per kind: unit tests, token identity, lint, build -> re-run at HEAD, or delete when rows at HEAD already stand, or label; perf A/B and objdump -> add the id and a label, never a re-run. At approval, when step 8 reports at least one stale sentence, the result rows go into the one stale-body sentence; post no separate re-run ask (PR 4596: the 2026-09-25 Verification rows cite ebadce2adb, 0274131d23, 7f8a4aa4d8, d85edc0e28, 16 to 19 commits behind 441e81178b with 10 of 11 PR files changed, and Wade asked for no re-run).
7. Body edit times: `gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"positron-ai",name:"tron"){pullRequest(number:N){createdAt lastEditedAt userContentEdits(first:50){nodes{editedAt editor{login} diff}}}}}' > edits.json`. Each `diff` field is the full body text after that edit, not a patch. Live review: LAST = lastEditedAt (createdAt when userContentEdits is empty) and body.md = the live text. Review already posted: LAST = the newest editedAt before the review time, and body.md = that edit's `diff` (PR 4596: the 2026-09-25T22:31:45Z text, 13078 chars; the live text is the 2026-10-01 refresh and holds nothing stale). Commits: `git -C WT log --no-merges --author='<PR author>' --format='%h %cI %s' --since=LAST $BASE..$HEAD` (ISO time with Z works; PR 4596: 16 commits, 12 subjects contain "review round"). An empty body, a body with no mechanism sentence, or zero commits -> skip steps 8a and 8b.
8a. Mechanism sentences: `grep -nE '[0-9]+ (cases|tests|assertions)|keyed by|per (pool |attention )?(worker|layer|forward)|owns|T[1-9] =' body.md | grep -v '^[0-9]*:[ ]*[\[{"]'` (PR 4596 2026-09-25 body: 7 sentence lines, 0 JSON lines). Keep only sentences whose symbol, key or count a step-7 commit touched: `git -C WT log --format=%h -S'<identifier>' --since=LAST $BASE..$HEAD` non-empty, or the commit changes the named test file; the rest is check 6 territory. For a kept sentence take the identifier from the commit subject, not the body phrase: `git -C WT grep -n '<identifier>' $HEAD -- h src t` (at 441e81178b `attention worker` has 17 comment hits and decides nothing; `pool_worker` has 2 hits, attn_stats.hpp:336 and :431, from bff317e0d3 'rows keyed by pool worker', review round 4, W5). 8b. Sample keys: `grep -o '"[a-z_0-9]*":' body.md | tr -d '":' | sort -u`; strip a `ready_` or `pending_` prefix and a `_w0` suffix to get the stem; `git -C WT grep -c -F '<stem>' $HEAD -- <renderer>`. Only a stem with 0 hits is a finding: the renderer escapes keys inside fmt::format strings (`\"key\"`) and composes the visit counters from prefix and stem (PR 4596: a literal grep of the full key reads 13 of 39 keys as absent although all exist at run time). A sample value the review itself flags as from a stale configuration (`"join_wait_cycles":0` from the untimed poll, inline 4125033634) is a stale-sample finding regardless of the grep.
9. Branch state. Live: step 1; CONFLICTING or DIRTY = "merge conflict"; UNKNOWN = re-query once after 10 s. A review already posted, or any merged PR: gh answers UNKNOWN for good; use the read-only `git -C WT merge-tree $BASE $HEAD $BASEOID > mt.txt; grep -c '<<<<<<<' mt.txt` (unanchored: the old merge-tree prints `+<<<<<<< .our`); the `changed in both` header above the first marker names the file (PR 4596 at 441e81178b vs 9b60b69dce: 1 block, h/tron/models/model.hpp, resolved by the two-parent merge 8c95514924 four hours after the approval). Report as one clause of the review body, never as a block.
10. Ported files: `grep -nEiw 'ported|copied|extracted|cherry-pick|cherry-picked|originally authored' body.md; grep -nEi 'from `?[A-Za-z_/-]+`? branch' body.md` (bare `ported` matched 'reported' on PRs 4256 and 4353). Without a named source branch or PR, write Insufficient data and stop (PR 1722 names none). Per file, source head at the review: `git -C WT log -1 --before='<review time>' --format='%h %cI %s' origin/S -- <path>` (PR 2676: a02939c11a 2026-05-05, not today's b4e9be991a 2026-05-14; drop --before for a live review). PR copy: `git -C WT show <id>:<path>` when the id resolves, else `gh api "repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=<id>" --jq .content | base64 -d` (36cf204564 is not in the worktree, GitHub serves it, 184 lines). Symbols only in the PR copy: `diff <(git -C WT show <source>:<path>) <prcopy> | grep '^>' | grep -oE '\b[a-z_]+\(' | tr -d '(' | sort -u`; per symbol `git -C WT log -1 --before='<review time>' --format="$s %h %cI %s" -S"$s" origin/S -- <path>`; report only symbols whose last source commit removed them (PR 2676: gof_configure, gof_configured, gof_layer_uses_hw, gof_max_layers, gof_reset, gof_hw_params, removed by a02939c11a). A symbol the PR copy lacks is never a finding (PRs 1707, 2844, 2875). Drop differences the body states as held back.

Open suggestion threads at a new push: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/comments --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.body | test("```suggestion")) | [.id, .user.login, .path, .original_commit_id[0:10], .original_line, .commit_id[0:10], .line, (.body | split("\n")[1])] | @tsv'`; keep threads the reviewer opened and `gh api graphql` reviewThreads.isResolved false. finals.label: test-exists-and-reaches-changed-path

skill_entry.name: 14. A changed path needs a test that enters it from the production side
skill_entry.trigger: Any one of four. (a) New primitive: a new header under h/ declares a type with mutable state sized by a constant (an advancing index or count plus an array or ring), a Note or doc comment states an ordering, capacity, full, empty or exactly-once invariant, and `git grep -l -w <name> HEAD -- t/` is empty. (b) Orchestration bypass: a changed or added function F in h/ or src/ sits on the call chain from a production caller down to a function the diff added; F and its callers up to three levels have no t/ hit; every t/ hit on the chain is a callee below F; F's own added or removed lines contain a branch or loop. (c) Formula mirror: a hunk in h/ or src/ changes the right-hand side of an assignment to a dotted or arrow field, and a t/ file the diff does not touch assigns the same field. (d) Accessor swap: a test hunk replaces a resource acquisition with a different named member or function, and no comment, commit message or body sentence names the new accessor.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Build the changed-function list from added definition lines plus the function enclosing each hunk (never from the `@@` text). List new headers with `--diff-filter=A`. 2. New type: grep t/ for its name; read its Note and list the invariants; check whether its size is a constexpr baked into its owner. 3. For each changed F with no t/ hit: walk callers up three levels; follow changed callees down to the first with a t/ hit; take the enclosing TEST_CASE of each hit and read it: does it call F, F's caller, or the callees by hand? List F's branches and the test that reaches each. Read the comment above F for the contract and grep t/ for the fields its barrier uses. 4. For each changed field formula, grep t/ for assignments of that field outside the diff; substitute the test's local definitions and compare. 5. For each accessor swap, read both accessors' definitions and grep body and commit messages for the new name. 6. Write a coverage statement; say what wrong behavior would still pass; keep an observed bug in a separate sentence.
skill_entry.question: Which test enters the changed code through its production entry point, and which assertion fails if that code is wrong?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A PR that changes h/ or src/ with no t/ file when it is not a new primitive, an orchestration change or a hardware-path change (20 of 48 silent PRs; negative_space 'Missing tests alone do not draw a comment'). A new type or function family added inside an existing header (tron-2693 counters, tron-2646 helpers drew nothing). A PR whose title or body says it merges, lifts or ports code from a named branch (tron-1707, 1722, 1739, 2646): the primitive only moves. Doc-only, test-only, one-line and mechanical-rename PRs (every removed/added pair differs only by the rename map). A test calling a callee directly when the diff changed only that callee. A formula hit the author shows equivalent after substituting the test's definitions (PR 1997: Wade approved 14 minutes after mcherba's last reply, without answering). An element-access respelling (`(*p)[0]` to `p->front()`). A swap a sentence explains. He asks to 'extend an existing CI suite' or for 'a unit-test', never a new file for moved code; he does not ask for a run here; he does not re-raise a bot's finding.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Orchestration: 'Coverage gap: the changed <F> is bypassed by the focused tests. The added tests call `<callee>` directly; the existing test named "<name>" invokes <steps> by hand. Please extend an existing CI suite with cases through <production entry>: <cases from F's branches>. Assert <contract>. These are missing safety-contract checks; I have not observed a <failure> in the implementation.' If the test reaches F only through a fake that ignores the arguments production emits, report under check 3. New primitive: 'Are you going to build a unit-test for `<primitive>`? Seems it should warrant one... verifying <invariant>, <invariant>, etc'. Formula: 'this should be updated in the <test files> as well'. Accessor swap: 'is this indeed the same <resource>?'
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal. A bold 'Coverage gap:' headline appears in the two PR 4128 comments (3960538961, 3960538177); the six dense PR 4128 inline comments carry no attribution header, and whether they were assistant-written is Insufficient data (wade-corpus.md:46), so cite the headline as the form of the posted finding, not as his phrasing. His own words elsewhere: 'Seems it should warrant one' (4614385493, a conversation comment); 'this should be updated ... as well... else I can do it after you merge this I guess' (2771720147); a bare question 'is this indeed the same queue?' (2737853978). Never 'nit', never blocking: he approved PR 1997 after the author's explanation and PR 2903 after the test file landed.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: full file (every TEST_CASE that hits a callee, read at HEAD), other files (t/ files the diff does not touch; the production definition of a swapped accessor), callers (production callers of the changed function, up to three levels), PR body and commit messages (for a sentence that covers a test edit). Not CI, not runtime.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a changed path needs a test that enters it from the production side

Common setup for this check. HEAD = the commit of the review record (corpus reviews[].commit; 97de6ee02c for PR 4128 review 5144955010), never the inline comment's commit field (GitHub moves it to the later head). BASE: if `git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main` succeeds (merged PR; merge-base would return HEAD itself), use `gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefOid -q .baseRefOid`, and when that id is not in WT use the merge commit's first parent `git -C WT merge-base HEAD <mergeCommit>^1`; otherwise `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main)`.

1. New primitives. `git -C WT diff --diff-filter=A --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*'`. Skip the step when the PR title or body says it merges, lifts or ports code from a named branch. For each new header: `git -C WT show HEAD:<hdr> | grep -n -E '^ *(class|struct) [A-Za-z_]+|Note \[|\b(must|exactly once|wrap|full|empty)\b'`. A type is a candidate only when it has an advancing index or count and an array or ring sized by a constant, and at least one invariant line hit. For each candidate name: `git -C WT grep -l -w <name> HEAD -- t/`; no hit = finding. List the invariants the `Note [...]` states (ordering, wrap-around, full, empty, concurrent writers); those are the cases to ask for. Baked size: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<name>[^;]*\{[a-z_]+_size\}' HEAD -- h/` and the constant's value in h/pos/config.hpp; if baked, note that a test cannot build a small instance (the remedy wording, a constructor argument with that default, is owned by the constant-name check, id 3350173837).

2. Orchestration. Changed functions, two commands, take the union. (a) Added or rewritten definitions: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | grep -E '^\+[ \t]*(template *<[^>]*> *)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:<>,*& ]* +)?[~A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:]*\([^;]*\)[ \t]*(const)?[ \t]*(noexcept)?[ \t]*\{[ \t]*$' | grep -v -E '^\+[ \t]*(if|for|while|switch|return|else|TRON_|REQUIRE|CHECK|static_assert|catch)\b'`. (b) The function enclosing each hunk: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | awk '/^\+\+\+ b\//{f=substr($0,7)} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[+,]/); print f, a[2]}'`, then per (file, line) `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /^[ \t]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:<>,*& ]* +)?[~A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:]*\([^;]*(\)[ \t]*(const)?[ \t]*(noexcept)?[ \t]*\{[ \t]*$|,$)/ && !/^[ \t]*(if|for|while|switch|return|else|TRON_|REQUIRE|CHECK|static_assert|catch|TRACE)/ {name=$0} END{print name}'`. Drop lambdas and wrapped assertion lines by eye. Do not use the stock `@@` text: for an indented member function it prints `public:` or the enclosing struct, and an added function never appears in it.
   Per function F: `git -C WT grep -n -w F HEAD -- t/` and `git -C WT grep -n -w F HEAD -- h/ src/`. For a member name shorter than six characters, or a common verb (clear, complete, populate, reset, size), or more than 30 bare hits, grep with the access spelling instead: `git -C WT grep -n -E '(<class>::|<receiver>->|<receiver>\.)F\(' HEAD -- t/`. Record the hit count next to each name.
   Body of F: `s=$(git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E '\bF\(' | grep -E '\{ *$|noexcept *\{|\) *\{' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); e=$(git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v S=$s 'NR>=S{n+=gsub(/\{/,"{"); n-=gsub(/\}/,"}"); if(NR>S && n==0){print NR; exit}}'); git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n "${s},${e}p" | grep -o -E '\b(<changed names joined by |>)\(' | sort | uniq -c`.
   Chain: start from each production caller outside F's file; follow changed callees down until a changed function with a t/ hit appears. The outermost changed function on the chain with zero t/ hits is F; the t/-hit callee at the chain end is the "called directly" function of the finding. Caller walk: `git -C WT grep -n -w F HEAD -- h/ src/`, then each caller's callers, up to three levels; stop at the first function with a t/ hit and record it with its TEST_CASE. Branch test: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <file> | sed -n '<F hunks>' | grep -E '^[-+].*\b(if|for|while|switch)\b|\?|\.(size|empty)\(\)'`. Fire only when no caller level reaches t/ and the branch test hits; argument plumbing and one forwarding call are not a branch.
   Enclosing TEST_CASE per callee hit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<test> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /TEST_CASE\(/ {name=$0; n=NR} END{print n": "name}'`. An empty name means the hit is in a helper above the first TEST_CASE: take the helper's name with the function pattern of 2(b) and `git -C WT grep -n -w <helper> HEAD -- <test file>` for the TEST_CASEs that call it. Read each TEST_CASE: does it call F, F's production caller, or the callees by hand? List F's branches (single versus batch, reservation collision, fanout, mixed shards and layers) and the test that reaches each, or none.
   Contract: read the comment block above F (`sed -n "$((s-8)),$((s-1))p"`) and the Note it cites; list the fields F's barrier reads or writes (`grep -o -E '[a-z_]+_\.'` over F's body); `git -C WT grep -n -E '<field1>|<field2>' HEAD -- t/`. Zero hits = no assertion observes the contract.
   Author's fix at a later head FINAL: `git -C WT log --no-merges --format='%h %s' HEAD..FINAL -- t/` and `git -C WT grep -n -w -E '<F names>' FINAL -- t/`; never `git diff --stat HEAD FINAL -- t/` when a merge of main sits between (46 files on PR 4128).

3. Formula mirror. `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | grep -n -E '^[-+][^/]*\b[A-Za-z_]+(\.|->)[A-Za-z_.]+ *= *[^;=]*[%*/+-]' | grep -v -E '= *[^;]*->'`; drop a line whose target is declared on the same line. The target field is the last dotted or arrow name before ` =`; a local variable is out of scope (a test cannot mirror a local). `git -C WT grep -n -E '(\.|->)<field> *=' HEAD -- t/`. For each hit in a file not in prfiles.txt: `git -C WT show HEAD:<test> | grep -n '<local var> ='` for every variable in the test's formula, substitute, and compare with the production form. Resolve the production operand to what it counts: `git -C WT show HEAD:<src> | grep -n '<operand> ='`. Report hits that are not equivalent and hits the PR touches that still carry the old form.

4. Accessor swap. `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 't/*' | grep -n -B2 -A2 -E '^-.*(::acquire\(|pos_allocate|std::make_shared<)|^\+.*= *(dev|device)->[a-z_]+;|^[-+].*= *[A-Za-z_]+->[a-z_]+_q\b'`. A removed statement may span two lines (`DmaQueue* read_q =` then `DmaQueue::acquire(...)`): pair by the variable name on the removed `=` line with the added line that assigns the same name. Discard an added line with no removed partner (construction, not a swap), an added line whose right-hand side is a field read in arithmetic or a method chain (`dev->num_fetchers`, `dev->load_weight_q->write_next_descriptor(`), and a pair that differs only by element-access spelling (`(*p)[0]` to `p->front()`, `v.at(i)` to `v[i]`). For each kept pair: `git -C WT grep -n '<new accessor>' HEAD -- h/ src/` (definition, init site) and read the old accessor's body; decide whether both name one object. `grep -n -i '<accessor>' body.md`; `git -C WT log --format=%B BASE..HEAD | grep -n -i '<accessor>'`.

5. Report per candidate; separate the coverage statement from any observed bug and say what wrong behavior would still pass.

On PR 4128 (step 2 only; reviewed at 97de6ee02c, BASE 130ad3a652, final head 7f80aa17da): the stock `@@` list names none of the five functions; command 2(a) lists fire_gof_rodeo_batch and gof_rodeo_impl_batch, command 2(b) lists help_drain_gof (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2988) and wait_for_coop_gof (:3015). t/ hits: help_drain_gof 0, wait_for_coop_gof 0, fire_gof_rodeo_batch 0, gof_rodeo_impl_batch 0, dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers 0, xfer_gofs 2. help_drain_gof calls one changed function (fire_gof_rodeo_batch :3005) plus the unchanged gof_coop_queue_.try_dequeue, so a two-callee count does not select it; the chain does: self_attention.hpp:793 and :908 -> help_drain_gof -> fire_gof_rodeo_batch (:3039, `tasks.size() == 1` branch) -> gof_rodeo_impl_batch (:3063) -> dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers (src/tron/gof.cpp:455) -> shard::xfer_gofs, hit at t/t_phase1_integration.cpp:910 (TEST_CASE :853) and :1002 (TEST_CASE :969); xfer_gof at :1055 inside TEST_CASE "gof rodeo populates and xfers to shard" (:1017), populate by hand at :1047. Branch test on help_drain_gof: the `while (task_count < task_budget ...)` loop and `if (!gof_coop_queue_.try_dequeue(tasks[0])) return;`. Contract: comment above wait_for_coop_gof (:3010-3014, "every fire_gof_rodeo is done before the scheduler rebuilds gof_jobs"); fields gof_coop_outstanding_ and gof_coop_queue_, 0 t/ hits. Wade's comment 3960538961 sits at :3005. At 7f80aa17da: t/t_llama_unit.cpp:1020 TEST_CASE "production GOF drain handles fanout layers and reservation gaps", :1023 gof_indices{2, 3, 4}, :1099 enqueue on state.gof_coop_queue_, :1102 state.wait_for_coop_gof(), :1104 outstanding == 0, :1113-1118 dma_done per shard and GOF; wait_for_coop_gof then has 1 t/ hit, the other four still 0. 442ed0dd1a (on three comments) does not resolve in WT; 97de6ee02c resolves but is on no ref and is not an ancestor of 7f80aa17da (rebased; its subject reappears as fd9fa17f9d); 7f80aa17da is the tip of origin/mrc_dma_coalesce_02; PR 4128 is open.
On PR 2903 (step 1; 64ea13a671, BASE 09d6fce432 from baseRefOid because merge-base returns HEAD itself): new h/pos/minfifo.hpp and src/pos/minfifo.cpp; `Note [minfifo design]` at minfifo.hpp:8, `class minfifo` at :32; :16 three-state sequence number, :40 enqueue returns false when full, :44 dequeue returns nullptr when empty; `git grep -l -w minfifo 64ea13a671 -- t/` empty; size baked at b8739108f7:h/pos/device.hpp:265 `tron::minfifo inwork_queue{inwork_ring_size}` with inwork_ring_size = 2048 at h/pos/config.hpp:86; the PosDevice constructor at b8739108f7 has no ring-size argument (remedy not adopted, approved anyway). finals.widen_delta: Checks 1 to 5 start from a test that exists and reaches the changed code; they judge the rows, the gates, the duplicates and the names. Check 14 runs one step earlier: it asks whether any test enters the changed code at all, and whether it enters through the production caller rather than a callee or hand-written steps. It adds four mechanical triggers (new stateful primitive with an invariant sentence and no t/ file, orchestration bypass on a call chain, formula mirror of a dotted field in untouched tests, unexplained accessor swap to a different named object in a test hunk) and one call-graph procedure (changed function -> t/ hits -> caller walk up three levels -> chain down to the first t/-hit callee -> enclosing TEST_CASE -> F, caller or by-hand). The changed-function list comes from added definition lines plus the function enclosing each hunk, never from the `@@` text. Two wording rules go to 'How Wade words a finding': a coverage finding says what wrong behavior would still pass, and keeps any observed bug in a separate sentence ('I have not observed a ... failure in the implementation'); the ask is 'extend an existing CI suite', not a new file. The 'Coverage gap:' headline is cited as the form of the posted PR 4128 finding, not as Wade's own phrasing (attribution Insufficient data). The baked-size remedy (constructor argument with the constant as default) is a one-line pointer here; its id 3350173837 stays with the constant-name check. The fake-boundary note (3960538177) stays with check 3; this check only cross-references it. The common setup gains two rules: HEAD is the review record's commit, and BASE for a merged PR comes from baseRefOid or the merge commit's first parent.

skill_entry.name: 10. Hunk-to-claim trace (unrelated, unexplained or merge-dropped changes)
skill_entry.trigger: Always; cost one `git log`, one `git diff --name-status`, one `git show` per non-merge commit. Four sub-triggers. (a) FILE: a D or R row whose stem appears whole-word in no body sentence or commit subject (`.gitkeep` counts; an A row is at most a body gap). (b) CONSUMER COMMENT: a removed comment line naming a reader outside the compiler (DO NOT RENAME, packaging, parsed by, read by, regex, grep, CMake, script, depends on). (c) MERGE CONTENT: a merge or sync PR with added lines in no source branch, or a merge commit dropping a pure-removal hunk the branch never removed. (d) BUILD FLAG: a CMake hunk adding target_compile_options, target_compile_definitions or `-m<feature>`. Other-author commits, 'merge', 'sync' raise scan order only.
skill_entry.procedure: 1 BASE: open PR `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>`; merged PR `git merge-base M^1 <review commit>`. 2 Identifiers: backticked names under Changes, What changes or Summary hitting pr.diff, plus column-0 declarations of created .cpp/.hpp files; sweep PRs skip hunk scanning. 3 Hunk candidate: half its removed lines at BASE, one substantive, no identifier added; a body 'drop' sentence clears a pure removal. 4 FILE: whole-word stem grep of body and subjects. 5 CONSUMER COMMENT: candidate on its own text; name adding commit, removing commit (`git log -m -S`), consumers outside h/ src/ at BASE, origin/main. 6 MERGE: first-parent sources at review date; per merge, pure-removal hunks of `diff -U0 M^2 M`. 7 FLAG: sibling targets, intrinsic includers. 8 Revert test.
skill_entry.question: If this hunk, file row, removed comment or flag alone were reverted, would any body sentence stop being true, any PR symbol stop compiling or stop being tested, and can the author say where it came from (which commit, which source branch, which failed build)?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A removed/added pair differing only by the rename map. Removed lines absent from BASE. A comment-only removal naming no outside reader, or one the PR's rewrite replaces (a new comment above the same code line). A pure removal a body sentence says is dropped. A file row the body or a subject names by stem. A sweep that is the PR's subject (PR 3756). Debug helpers in a hardware-attention author's own area. A build flag a sibling target already carries when the body says the target uses the feature. Formatting and include order; duplicate includes or a literal replacing a constant after a merge belong to dead-symbol and magic-literal. A merge commit as such. Never block (PR 2659).
skill_entry.finding_shape: Code hunk: "<file>:<lines> (commit <id>, '<subject>') changes <N> lines that exist at BASE and that <feature> does not touch: <what>. Reverting it alone keeps the body true. Not part of <title>; please split it out." File row, consumer comment, merge content or flag, as a question: "<file>:<BASE lines> (commit <id>, '<subject>') <deletes <path> | removes the comment '<quote>' above `<identifier>`, which survives at HEAD | adds `<qualifier or flag>` to <N> lines> that no body sentence or commit subject mentions. <Consumer at <file:line> of <rev>, or the adding commit says '<subject>' | Neither <source A> nor <source B> has these lines, so where is this coming from? | <sibling> already carries these flags; which translation unit failed?> Was this intentional?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: A question, never an order: "was this intentional?" (3197414598), "why did this comment get removed? It's still relevant AFAIK" (3973917755), "So where is this coming from?" (2629374536). He approves in the same review when the rest is fine: PR 2659 approved at 20:50:41Z, 26 s after the question, before the restore; PR 1807 approved one minute after the flag question with no change asked ("Hmph."). The merge-artifact wording "please clean this up... perhaps a merge artifact?" (2915281512, duplicate includes, owned by dead-symbol-no-consumer-or-definition) shows the same register. Only PR 4557 got "please split them out", for a 35-line kernel hunk inside a feature PR. Default severity: minor; normal when the removed line protects a build or packaging consumer; informational for a build flag.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk, PR body (bot summary blocks stripped; edit history checked against the review time), commit subjects and commit parents (`git log -m -S`, `git diff -U0 M^2 M`), other files (consumers outside h/ and src/: CMakeLists.txt, cmake/, packaging/, bin/, scripts) at BASE and at origin/main, the source branches of a merge or sync PR at the review date (first-parent tips), and sibling CMake targets. Full file only for the comment block above the changed lines and for the next code line below a dropped comment. No runtime; a build-flag provenance question is asked, not answered.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 10: hunk-to-claim trace (unrelated, unexplained or merge-dropped changes)

Setup for this check (overrides the common BASE line):

```
BR=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName)
# open PR:
BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$BR)
# merged PR (HEAD = the review commit, an ancestor of the base branch, so merge-base HEAD origin/$BR is HEAD itself and the diff is empty):
M=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .merge_commit_sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $M^1 HEAD)
```
Verified: PR 2659 (base hwattention_sync) BASE=8248ebbe72, `git diff --name-status BASE eb0627f006` = 2 rows (against origin/main: 178 rows); PR 1716 BASE=37cfc477fb, 2 files +48/-19 (first parent of the oldest PR commit, 7f993bc2db, gives 50 files because it includes main's merged changes); PR 1807 BASE=e61f0b0ab7 (= d03129dad0~2).
Body: strip `<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->` ... `<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->` from body.md. Body date: `gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"positron-ai",name:"tron"){pullRequest(number:N){userContentEdits(first:20){nodes{editedAt editor{login}}}}}}'`; an edit later than the review means a clearance sentence may not have been visible to the reviewer (PR 3738: 17 edits, last 2026-09-09T23:15:23Z, review 23:25Z).
Author map: `gh api users/<login> --jq .name` before binning (PR 3738: login BillBaumann = 'Bill Baumann', 7 commits; 29 commits by 'Chander Luderman Miller', login chander-positron).

1. Identifier set: backticked names and Note titles under the first heading whose text contains "What changes", "Changes" or "Summary" (the whole stripped body when none exists), minus names with 0 hits in pr.diff (PR 3738: `t_mwaitx`, a flaky test cited in the test plan) and minus command-line flags (`--tracer-core`) that no C++ line carries verbatim. A body name that exists at BASE stays in the set (PR 3756: `process_device_id`). From each created .cpp/.hpp file add `git show HEAD:FILE | grep -E '^(struct|class|static|constexpr|inline|using|TEST_CASE)'` (t/t_fpga_tracer.cpp: 34 TEST_CASEs, 56 column-0 lines); a created .md file adds none. When the body has no backticked code name, or every one is a test target or commit id (PR 4353: `t_llama_unit`, `t_ranged_mask`, `282955f1`), take the function, member and parameter names the diff declares in `+` lines. Write the list with its `grep -c` count over pr.diff.
2. Bin commits from log.txt (SIDE / MAIN-FEATURE as in SKILL.md). Sweep PR: the title or body says "throughout", "everywhere", "all call sites", "rename" or "use X ... throughout" and one identifier appears in at least half of the diff files (PR 3756: process_device_id in 29 of 36 files); then skip step 3 and run only steps 4-7. Steps 4-7 run over the BASE..HEAD diff, not per commit: a line a merge commit dropped is in no non-merge commit (PR 3738: 26 non-merge commits, 624 hunks, none carries the DO NOT RENAME removal). Scan every non-merge commit, SIDE first: `git show <sha> -- FILE` per file.
3. Candidate hunk test: at least half of its `-` lines in `git show BASE:FILE` verbatim, at least one not blank, brace-only or comment-only, no identifier in the `+` lines. Inheritance within the same function or TEST_CASE. A hunk with no `+` lines is a candidate only when none of its removed lines names an identifier that a body sentence says is dropped, removed or replaced (PR 2875 "Drop `mark_used`/`mark_unused`/`check_usage`" clears full.hpp:419, :512 and token_cache.cpp:162).
4. FILE rows: `git -C WT diff --name-status BASE..HEAD | grep -E '^(A|D|R)'`. For each path P: STEM=$(basename P | sed 's/\..*//'); grep body.md and log.txt with `grep -i -w -c -F "$STEM"`, again with `_` and `-` in STEM replaced by a space, and `grep -i -c -F "$(dirname P)/"` for the directory with its trailing slash. A one-letter directory (t/, h/) never clears; a substring hit never clears ('doc' inside 'documented'). Zero hits on every form: a D or R row is a candidate; an A row is a body gap at most, and never a candidate when another hunk of pr.diff uses a name the file declares (PR 2774 h/common/fixed_string.hpp: `fixed_string`, `expert_labels` used in feed_forward.hpp). Name the commit: `git -C WT log --diff-filter=AD --format='%h %s' BASE..HEAD -- P`. Verified: 73 A/D/R rows in the 38 silent tron PRs give 0 candidates (basename-only grep gave 3: PR 1722 hwattention.hpp/.cpp, body "Added hwattention files."; PR 2774 fixed_string.hpp); PR 3738: `t_fpga_tracer` 1 whole-word body hit clears t/t_fpga_tracer.cpp, "fpga tracing" 3 subject hits clear doc/fpga-tracing.md.
5. CONSUMER COMMENT lines: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE..HEAD | grep -n -E '^-\s*(//|\*|#)' | grep -i -E 'DO NOT RENAME|DO NOT REMOVE|packag|parsed by|read by|regex|grep|cmake|script|depend'`. Every hit is a candidate on the strength of its own text; the greps below corroborate and are reported either way. (a) Adding commit: `git -C WT log --format='%h %ci %s' -S'<comment text>' origin/main -- FILE | tail -1`. (b) Consumer: take the identifiers on the lines below the comment at BASE, cut each to its stem before the last underscore (`min_bitfile`; CMake builds the full name from a variable, so the full identifier never matches), and run `git -C WT grep -n '<stem>' <rev> -- ':!h' ':!src'` at BASE and at origin/main. (c) Removing commit: `git -C WT log -m --format='%h %p %s' -S'<comment text>' HEAD -- FILE` (`-m` is required; a merge commit's conflict resolution does not show without it). Digest check: the regex hits 3 of 67 digests; 3738 is the true positive; 3093 ("default OFF" rewritten to "default ON") and 4191 ("I depend on `tok`" rewritten) are cleared by step 8 because the PR's own rewrite replaces the line.
6. MERGE CONTENT. (a) Added lines: runs only when the PR title or body says it merges or syncs a named branch (PR 1716 "Second step of AoF merge") or the base_ref is a sync branch. Sources = the branches at the review date: `git rev-list -1 --first-parent --before=<comment timestamp> origin/<branch>` (`--first-parent` is required: without it the origin/main lookup for PR 1716 returns the PR's own commit 2d7f3a62ec, which carries the 19 `volatile` members, and the check would not fire). For every added line of `git diff -U0 BASE..HEAD` run `git -C WT grep -q -F -- '<line>' <src> -- FILE` in each source; lines absent from every source are candidates, grouped by file. A feature PR whose history only contains merge-of-main commits does not run 6a: every added line of such a PR is absent from main by construction (PR 3738: all 62 hunks would fire). (b) Dropped lines: for each merge commit M in `git log --merges --format=%h BASE..HEAD`, run `git -C WT diff -U0 M^2 M` and keep only hunks with `-` lines and no `+` line (a rewritten statement is not a drop). Keep a hunk only when at least one removed non-blank line is present at M^1 or absent at `git merge-base M^1 M^2` (the branch side did not remove it on purpose) and `git -C WT grep -F '<line>' M -- h src t CMakeLists.txt cmake` finds the line nowhere at M (a line found elsewhere was moved). Clear a surviving hunk when HEAD carries a new comment above the same code line, or when the dropped line names a symbol absent at HEAD (it could not compile). Each remaining hunk is a candidate; name M and quote the lines. Do not run `git diff M^2 M` over whole files: it lists the PR's own edits (PR 3738: 128-177 removed lines per merge, 10 merges, 32,990 diff lines). Verified: b815ae9ad4 (PR 3738) keeps 2 pure-removal hunks in h/pos/config.hpp, `@@ -104,3` (DO NOT RENAME block, candidate) and `@@ -69,2` (`static_assert(fpga_use_period % tracer_period == 0`, cleared: `tracer_period` has 0 hits in config.hpp at 819d4c96b8); the 15 merge commits of silent PRs 4353, 1739, 1707 and 1722 keep 0.
7. BUILD FLAG: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -- '*CMakeLists.txt' '*.cmake' | grep -n -E '^\+.*(target_compile_options|target_compile_definitions|add_compile_definitions|(^|[:;" ])-m[a-z0-9]+)'` (the file restriction and the token boundary are required: over whole diffs `-m[a-z0-9]+` hits 6 prose lines of PR 2475 t/t_clearhbm.cpp, 'direct-mode'). Sibling targets: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'mavx512|mavx2|mfma|TRON_AVX512_ENABLED' HEAD -- '*CMakeLists.txt'`. Translation units that need the flag: `git -C WT grep -l -E 'immintrin|_mm512|_mm256|simd.hpp' HEAD -- h/<lib> src/<lib>`. Report the question, not a split.
8. Clearance: rename-map identity; a GitHub review thread id; a body sentence or commit subject describing the added content, the file row or the removal ("Restore the bitfile packaging warning" clears its own hunk). A sentence naming only the file or callee does not clear; a contradicting sentence is quoted. For a consumer comment, clear only when a consumer existed at the adding commit and no longer exists at HEAD; a consumer absent at BASE but named by the adding commit's subject does not clear (PR 3738: the CMake reader entered main five days after the review); a commit message that names the identifiers below the comment but not the comment (b815ae9ad4 "Restore the upstream bitfile version constants so the merged tree builds") does not clear.
9. Test hunks: callee untouched by the PR -> unrelated; callee rewritten -> regression guard, body gap at most.
10. Revert test (all kinds): reverting the item alone keeps every body sentence true, every identifier compiling, and every assertion passing at HEAD also passing at BASE. If the hunk is the sole test of a PR symbol's forwarded behavior, report a body gap and let the author choose.
11. One finding per hunk, file row, removed comment block or flag line.

On PR 4557: ec795fbce8 (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:152-181, 35 of 36 removed lines at BASE, 0 identifiers, body:52 "The tile loads are unchanged" contradicts) -> unrelated, split out. 39a6899446 carries t/t_heap_v2.cpp:1209-1223 (CHECK is_aligned, contract alloc_align at BASE memory.hpp:146); it is the only test of the new operator new[]'s alignment forwarding -> body gap, author's choice. 959d1ae229 partner-zero rows: callee append_v_row rewritten by the PR -> regression guard, not unrelated.

skill_entry.name: Avoidable per-call work on a per-token, per-layer or spin path
skill_entry.trigger: Both halves. Pattern: an added non-comment line under h/ or src/ (not t/, not src/pos/fake.cpp), outside a constructor, destructor, clear() or function-local `static` initializer, matches: `std::vector`, `.reserve(`, `std::map`, `make_shared`, `make_unique` or `new ` in a function body; `std::memset` or `std::fill` over a whole allocation; `std::sort`; a callback (`*_fn(`) in the innermost of nested loops; a `TRON_ASSERT` whose condition calls a function; a call above an `if` chain in a wait, poll or spin routine; a free (`release_buffer`, `free_`, `evict`, `deallocate`) conditioned only on a counter reaching zero. Path: the function, or one caller up, sits in a spin, layer or token-job loop, `poll_completions`, a wait routine, or is the batched sibling of a singleton (`xfer_gof` -> `xfer_gofs`).
skill_entry.procedure: 1. List pattern hits in added h/ and src/ lines with enclosing functions. 2. Grep callers one level up; classify by loop: spin, per-layer, per-token, completion poll, wait routine, once per forward, startup. Keep the first five, and a once-per-forward function whose BASE lines allocated nothing. 3. Count calls from loop bounds and constants, with a unit; layer count from the named model; no time conversion. 4. Open the singleton sibling or replaced BASE lines; record how they avoided the work. 5. Per pattern: container before the empty check; bytes the loops overwrite; emittable order; callback copies or returns a pointer; branch skipping the value; same assert on every entry path; rebuild then resubmit. 6. Report count, sibling fact, remedy.
skill_entry.question: Does this function, on a path the forward runs per token, per layer, per spin iteration or per DMA completion, do work on every call that the sibling or the replaced lines at BASE did not do (allocate, zero, sort, re-gather, re-assert, rebuild), and does the common case need it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Code run once per request or shard backfill, at startup, in a constructor, clear() or teardown. Test code under t/ and src/pos/fake.cpp. A comment line, a `std::function` member declaration, a trace event or counter (3350412400; the author dropped the comment lines, kept the event). A `static const` initializer reported as per-call work: state the real cost (one init plus a guard check). A container sized by dequeued work after the empty check, the feature's own output buffer, or a sort of queued elements (gof_rodeo_impl_batch at 442ed0dd1a: duplication comment 3907214892, never cost). A free whose risk is a live DMA (buffer-lifetime check). Reported TPS or TTFT numbers, benchmark method, kernel arithmetic. Never demand a measurement; label a slowdown a hypothesis.
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<fn>` (<file:line>) runs <count with unit> per <prefill of N tokens (M layers, model X) | decode token per worker | spin iteration> and <allocates | zeroes <bytes> | sorts | calls `<callback>` <k>x | re-asserts `<cond>`> on every call, where <sibling | the replaced code at BASE> (<file:line>) <uses a fixed array | zeroes only padding | is sorted by construction | gathers once per (pos, head) | asserts once | try_dequeues with zero allocation>. So <consequence with the count>. <seems like we should <remedy>? | this is maybe a nit... but should we check the `<cheap case>` first?>
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit for one misplaced computation in a wait routine ('this is maybe a nit... but it seems like we should check for the `else if (0 == wait_cycles)` case first?', 3350064944; the author accepted at 3350409050; Bill replied that ns_to_cycles could be made cheap, 3351684377, and landed that in PR #2915, commit 2ed902167b, merged 2026-06-05 as 1f68af6047; the branch order at b8739108f7:113/:118 never changed). normal, as a statement with the computed count and the sibling named, for allocation before the empty check, whole-buffer zeroing the loops overwrite, a sort the emission order makes unnecessary, or a repeated gather on a prefill or decode path ('xfer_gofs does some avoidable per-call work on the prefill critical path', 3907183627; 'Two decode-path costs in the drain helpers', 3907185740; the author changed all of them at head 7f80aa17da). minor and not blocking for an eviction or rebuild pattern, as a conversation comment posted with the APPROVED review ('I'm always concerned with performance ... Maybe it won't materialize', 4674512577). Since 2026-03 (first 3002297607 on PR 2233, 2026-03-27) he sometimes has an AI assistant word the concern and pastes it; on PR 4128 the pasted form is conversation comment 5498556672, posted five minutes before the inline comments, and the author's fix commit f0467262cb cites that comment by URL; treat a pasted block as attributed material.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: HEAD is the review commit, confirmed by the comment's cited line numbers, not the API commit field (GitHub moves it to the PR head when the line still applies). If HEAD is not in the worktree (a force-pushed merge commit such as 442ed0dd1a), read it through `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/compare/BASE...HEAD` and `contents/<file>?ref=HEAD`. Full file at HEAD (the function and its if/else chain); callers one level up in h/ and src/ (the loop class); other files: the singleton sibling, the removed lines at BASE, the constants in h/pos/config.hpp, h/tron/gof.hpp and h/libpos.hpp, the callback definitions in h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp, h/common/assert.hpp for TRON_ASSERT; the PR body only for the free/rebuild pattern (the workload the body says it optimizes) and for the model name that gives the layer count. No CI and no runtime needed; a trace is optional and never demanded.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: avoidable per-call work on a per-token, per-layer or spin path

Setup. HEAD is the commit of the review, confirmed by the comment's cited line numbers, not the commit field the API shows (GitHub moves `commit_id` to the PR head while the line still applies: 3907183627 shows 7f80aa17da but its lines :37, :256, :278, :333 are 442ed0dd1a lines; `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/comments/<id> --jq '{commit_id,original_commit_id,original_line}'` gives the review commit). BASE = `git -C WT merge-base HEAD $(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha)`; for a merged PR, `merge-base HEAD origin/main` is HEAD itself and the diff is empty (PR 2903: 64ea13a671 vs origin/main gives 0 files; vs base.sha 09d6fce432 the merge-base is 947d045a14, 25 files). If `git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD` fails (a force-pushed merge commit), take the diff from `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/compare/BASE...HEAD` (one `patch` per file, 3 context lines, map hits through the `@@` headers) and each file from `gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw' repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<file>?ref=HEAD`; `gh pr diff N` is the current head only.

1. Pattern hits in production code, comments and hunk headers excluded from the hit list: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@|\+)' | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+\s*(//|\*)' | grep -E '^[0-9]+:(\+\+\+|@@|\+.*(std::vector|\.reserve\(|std::map|std::memset|std::fill|std::sort|make_shared|make_unique|[^a-z_]new |std::function|_fn\(|TRON_ASSERT[A-Z_]*\([^,]*[a-z_0-9]\(|release_buffer|free_|evict|deallocate))'`. A `@@` line is context for mapping, never a hit; count only `+` lines; drop hits in src/pos/fake.cpp and `std::function` member declarations. Enclosing function of a hit at <file>:<L> (the default awk is mawk 1.3.4, which has no interval expressions, so no `{2,4}` inside awk): for a .cpp file `RX='^[a-zA-Z_][^;]*\([^;]*$'`, for a header `RX='^ {2,4}[a-zA-Z_][^;=]*\([^;]*$'`; then `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E "$RX" | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\s*(return|if|for|while|else|switch|TRON_|TRACE_|static_assert|using|namespace|template|//|#|auto |constexpr)' | awk -F: -v L=<L> '$1<=L{l=$0} END{print l}'`. A result whose line is a data member means "not in a function": treat it as the constructor. Verified at 7f80aa17da: gof.cpp:490 -> dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers :438; model.hpp:3001 -> help_drain_gof :2988; model.hpp:3085 -> gof_rodeo_impl_batch :3063.

1b. Pattern (e), a computation above a branch in a wait, poll or spin routine (no step-1 alternative matches it): `git -C WT diff -U1 BASE HEAD -- 'h/*' 'src/*' | grep -n -A1 -E '^\+\s*(static const |const )?[a-zA-Z_0-9:<>]+ [a-z_0-9]+ = .*[a-z_0-9]\(.*\).*;\s*$' | grep -B1 -E '^[0-9]+-\+?\s*(if|else if) \(' | grep -v '^--$'` lists added assignment-with-call lines directly above an `if`; keep those whose enclosing function matches `wait|poll|spin|monitor|for_event|indefinitely`. On PR 2903 (`gh pr diff 2903`) this gives one hit, mwaitx.cpp:112 `static const uint64_t mwaitx_min_cycles = ns_to_cycles(300) + 300;` above `if (wait_cycles > mwaitx_min_cycles)`; on the PR 4128 head diff it gives 0 hits in h/ and src/. A `static const` line costs one init plus a guard check per call; say so.

2. Callers and loop class: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<fn>\(' HEAD -- h src | grep -v -E '^\S+:\s*//'`. For each caller line open 15 lines above it and classify: spin (`while (.*load(std::memory_order_acquire)`), per-layer (`for (.*layer`), per-token (`for (.*job|token`), completion poll (`poll_completions`), wait routine (`monitor_and_wait|for_event_cycles|indefinitely`), once per forward (`run_forward`, `assemble_attention_plan`, `compute_forward_args`), startup (`driver.cpp` init, `scan(`, `pos_list_devices`, a constructor). Keep functions with at least one caller in the first five classes. Keep a once-per-forward function only when the lines it replaced at BASE (`git -C WT show BASE:<file>`) did the same work on the same queue with zero allocation (wait_for_coop_gof: BASE 9a905763ac model.hpp:2978-2987 `gof_coop_task task; while (gof_coop_queue_.try_dequeue(task))`, listed by Wade inside 3907185740). Drop a hit whose enclosing function is a constructor, a destructor, clear(), a function-local `static` initializer, or whose only production callers are startup or t/; record each drop with the caller line. A batched sibling has no loop class of its own: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<stem>s?\(|<stem>_batch\(' HEAD -- h src`; state the count premise explicitly ("one call per coalescence window per layer when every window batches fully; xfer_gofs's own TRON_ASSERT at gof.cpp:229-231 bounds a batch to one window").

3. Count: `git -C WT grep -n -E '(hwkv_coalesce_tokens|gof_tokens|hwkv_tok_per_page|HWCACHEBLOCK_BYTES|FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE|HW_MAX_KV_HEADS|HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE|HWBLOCK_POSITIONS|VBLOCK_ROWS_PER_FETCHER|VBLOCK_CELL_STRIDE_BF16|POS_DATA_SIZE)\s*=' HEAD -- h`. The layer count is a model parameter, not a header constant: take it from the model the PR body or config/test-benchmarks.json names and write "36 layers (model X)"; with no model named, give the count per layer and say so. Write calls per forward = (tokens / window tokens) x layers, allocations per spin iteration x workers x layers, gather calls per GOF = FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE x gof_tokens x n_kv_heads, bytes per window = coalesce_gofs x (HWCACHEBLOCK_BYTES + FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE x pchannel_stride x POS_DATA_SIZE), each with its unit. No time conversion.

4. Sibling: `git -C WT show BASE:<file> | sed -n '<start>,<end>p'` for the replaced lines, or the singleton function at HEAD; grep its storage: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E 'std::array|[a-z_]+\[[0-9A-Z_]+\];|std::fill|std::sort|<callback>\('`. If neither a singleton sibling nor the replaced BASE lines avoid the work, and the enclosing function or its caller already built the same container kind per call at BASE, there is no finding under patterns (a)-(d) and (f); write the fact and stop (silent PR 4353 split_sections_by_query: finish_sw_plan already took std::vector parameters at BASE). Patterns (e) and (g) need no sibling.

5. Per pattern. (a) container before the empty check: does `reserve(` or the constructor precede the first `try_dequeue` / `empty()`? Is the size bounded by a constexpr (`std::max(`, `coalesce_gofs`)? Fire only when the container precedes the empty check or the singleton sibling keeps the same data in a fixed array. (b) zeroing: count the loop ranges below against the allocation size in the common geometry. (c) sort: list the emission order of the push_back loops and the comparator keys; fire only when the keys are known at push time and the loops could emit in comparator order; a sort of elements received from a queue or a tree walk is not a finding. (d) nested callback: `grep -n -E '<callback>\('` inside the function; note which loop index its arguments use; compute calls per element versus the sibling; then open the definition `git -C WT grep -n -E '<callback>\s*=' HEAD -- h src` (page_info lambdas live in h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp): a body that copies into a buffer (`get_v(..., dest)` into a captured `v_buf`, full.hpp:2506-2513 at 442ed0dd1a) is a gather and counts per call; a body that returns a pointer (`k(...).data`) is not, and the repeated call is at most a nit; record the `#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE` variant read. (e) computation before a branch: print the `if` / `else if` chain after the added line; name the branch that does not use the value; `git -C WT grep -n -E '<fn>\([^,]+, 0,' HEAD -- h src` for callers that take it; mark `static const` initializers. finals.label: state-ownership-and-key-granularity

skill_entry.name: 14. One site owns a published record, every call into a gated subsystem sits under its gate, a cumulative row key names the same thread in every forward
skill_entry.trigger: Any one, in h/tron hunks. (a) A published record (a struct folded, printed or exported as one unit: stats row, counter record, FUSE leaf) gets fields from two layers, each writer filling fields the other never writes, or a begin/end pair in one function plus a time stamp around its call. (b) A direct call into a subsystem whose *_configure or *_reset sits under a guard the new site does not share, or a callback loop replaced by a direct call. (c) A cumulative table (never resized per forward) sized by one count (num_workers()) and indexed by a variable offset by a per-forward value (n_attn_workers). (d) A class or budget decided by one predicate over a whole forward.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Writers: keep atomic writes to a record member; drop locals and fold readers. Grep qualified members at HEAD; table member, writer, file, layer. 2. Callers: finding when a production caller reaches one writer and not the other, or one writer reads state only the other sets; a writer inside the other's caller on every path clears it. 3. Gates: the guard above the configure call and above every call into the namespace; unconfigured behaviour; exclude the diff's own switch. 4. Tables: size versus index, exposed versus fillable rows, fold bounds, leaf names. 5. Predicates: pre-review body validation tool, compute_forward_args for mixed forwards, per-element key at the counting site, README bucket definition. 6. One finding per record, subsystem, table, predicate.
skill_entry.question: Who owns this record, and does every caller, every model shape and every forward with a different worker split fill it the same way, so that a reader of the leaves sees one thread per row, one class per forward and no half records?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A record owned through a scoped object (forward_scope). A single-site counter with a reset (PR 2980 drew only an atomics question, 3406007619). A value one function moves between instances of one structure under a Note or TRON_ASSERT (subtree_pins tron-2875, kv_section tron-4353, both silent). A table resized every forward (ready_kv_plan). A function the body declares inert naming the follow-up PR (tron-2693). A call site already under the shared gate helper. A row key documented stable per thread (pool worker index). A per-forward class stated deliberate with the README naming the limitation (ae8a6d38d9). A clear partner with zero callers: dead-symbol check (3029165954). A gate or key spelled two ways: duplicate-logic check (3029194687, 4147010638). Tests driving inner hooks: 4125033677. Missing tests, formatting, wording.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Two layers write `<record>`: <fields> come from `<site A>` while <fields> come from `<site B>`. Any other caller of `<inner call>` (another scheduler, a test harness, a draft path) gives `<field> == 0` next to nonzero `<field>`. Consider owning <X> inside `<one function>`, or wrap <begin/end/stamp> in one scoped helper, so a single site owns the record. Key or class form: Design question on <row sizing | the forward classification>. Rows are sized by `<count A>` but indexed by `<index B>`, so <consequences as bullets>. Was keying by <B> deliberate? Keying by <A> would <benefit>. Alternatively, record `<n>` per forward so readers can interpret the rows. Gate form: endorse the finding, name the mechanism keeping every call under the guard.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal. The two-writer case is a statement that ends in 'Consider ...' with two options; his review summary called it one of 'A few correctness and semantics issues inline'. The key and class cases open with 'Design question on ...' and end in a question with two alternatives plus a documentation fallback ('If per-forward is intended, can the README spell out ...'). The gate case is an endorsement of a bot: 'good point... we should be consistent'. 'Nit:' never inside this check (the row-key-computed-two-ways nit 4147010638 belongs to the duplicate-logic check). Never blocking.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk, full file (the record struct and its hooks), callers (git grep at HEAD for the inner and outer call), other files (the scheduler's compute_forward_args, the configure site, the Note on worker placement), PR body (the version that precedes the review: the sample run's n_workers and active_workers, the validation tool), runtime behaviour (how one forward gathers users is readable from h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp compute_forward_args; mark Insufficient data only for a scheduler outside full.hpp).

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: one owner per published record, one gate per subsystem, one stable key per cumulative row

Setup note: for a merged PR `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself (PR 4596: 1430736b2a). Use `BASE=$(for c in $(git -C WT rev-list --first-parent origin/main); do git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor $c HEAD && echo $c && break; done)` and confirm BASE against the baseline id the PR body names. Layers: h/tron/scheduler = scheduler, h/tron/models = model, src/tron/kernels = kernel.

1. Writers (a): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@|\+.*(fetch_add|inc_relaxed|max_relaxed|\.store\(|\|= ))' | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+.*(out|s|json) \+='`. Keep the `@@` headers to map each hit to its HEAD line (new-side hunk start plus offset). Keep only hits whose left side is a member access of a record struct (`x.member`, `x->member`, a bare member inside the struct's own member function); drop locals, string builds and fold readers (`out +=`, `visits[pass][p] += load_relaxed(...)`, `results[i].store(`). For each kept record take the struct name and its instance, then grep qualified, never a bare member name another struct or a scheduler variable also uses: `git -C WT grep -n -E '(INSTANCE|ARRAY\[[^]]*\])\.(M1|M2|M3)' HEAD -- h src`. Enclosing function: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=LINE 'NR<=L && /^  [a-z][a-z_0-9<>:& ]* [a-z_0-9]+\(/ && !/^  (if|for|while|switch|return)\b/ {f=$0; n=NR} END{print n": "f}'`. Table: member, writer function, file, layer. Two layers, or an inner function in one layer with the time stamp taken in another, make the record a candidate; step 2 decides whether it is a finding.

2. Callers: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'state\.forward\(|\.run_forward\(|begin_forward\(|end_forward\(|note_forward_wall\(' HEAD -- h src t` (replace with the PR's hooks and the function that calls them). The candidate is a finding only when a production caller reaches one writer and not the other, or when one writer reads state only the other sets: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n 'current_class'`. A second writer that runs inside the first writer's caller on every production path clears the candidate (split_sections_by_query inside finish_sw_plan, model.hpp:2785 at a9a9cf30a4ac). Test callers are excluded (4125033677). One production caller at HEAD is not a clearance: name the future callers (another scheduler, a test harness, a draft path).

3. Gates (b): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(if constexpr|getenv\(|_enabled\(\)|_configured\(\)|_configure\()'`. Exclude the switch of the diff's own feature (an env_enabled() or getenv of the variable the PR introduces); a gate counts only when a configure or reset call of a subsystem the diff calls into sits under it. Guard above the configure call: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=LINE 'NR<L && /if constexpr|if \(/ {g=$0; n=NR} END{print n": "g}'`. Every call into the subsystem: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'tron::hardware::gof_[a-z_]+\(' HEAD -- h src`, same awk per hit. Unconfigured behaviour: `git -C WT show HEAD:src/tron/gof.cpp | grep -n -E '/ gof_n_layers|% gof_n_layers|gof_n_layers = 0'` and `git -C WT grep -n 'gof_max_layers()' HEAD -- h src`.

4. Row keys (c): size expressions `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(attn\.size\(\)|num_workers\(\)|std::vector<[a-z_]+>\(N_)'`. Confirm the table is cumulative: `git -C WT grep -n -E '\.resize\(n_attn_workers\)' HEAD -- h` marks per-forward tables, which are out of scope. Index expressions: `git -C WT grep -n -E '(note_attn_job|note_join_wait|add_visits|token_path_span|[^a-z_]row)\(' HEAD -- h`.
