skill_entry.name: 6. Claim wider than the code: guarantees, timed paths, element counts and defaults
skill_entry.trigger: Four sentence kinds in body, commit message, Note, README, doc/ or file header; expand plurals, 'and', 'or', 'both', 'either', 'every' to one subject per row. (a) Type guarantee: a rejected input ('bare pointer') plus a compile-time mechanism word. (b) Measured path: an added timer or counter in h/ or src/ (rdtsc, inc_relaxed, fetch_add, *_cycles, note_*) whose sentence has a whole-word path word ('ends when', 'whichever', 'in both', 'either', 'every'; 'or the', 'and the' only beside the identifier). (c) Element count: an added production [0] or .front() read of a growable container, or a bare !empty() assert, plus a doc, Note or header cardinality sentence. (d) Stated default: the diff changes a default or its sentence; another literal states it.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. One row per subject: property, path or mechanism, text location. 2. (a): resolve each parameter type through every `using`; grade levels 1-3 (explicit constructor; no pointer constructor; distinct class) with the deciding line; read tests for opposite probes. 3. (b): map identifier to label; list every start, stop and increment site at HEAD; per named path find its selector and wait, the enclosing function of each stamp and the branch guarding its call; write start, stop or 'untimed'; tie a 0 in the review-time sample to the untimed path via the sibling counter. 4. (c): growers and call sites versus the cardinality sentence. 5. (d): every literal bound to the setting; the compile_definitions line. 6. One finding per subject.
skill_entry.question: For every subject the sentence covers (each type, each path, each element count, each build path), which line of the code reaches what the sentence says, and does the sentence say where it stops?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A limitation named in the sentence's own row or comment block, or in the body ('inert until #N wires it in'); 'typed' alone; `explicit` as such. A `#define S 0` fallback when CMake defines S only on the ON path (PR 3093): ask, accept the answer. Text narrowed instead of code widened closes a (b) finding. A plural handled by a loop; one accumulator bracketing every named part. .back(), a stack top, a fixed array index, a string receiver, test files. A cap on a setting; a re-spelled getenv, fallback unchanged. Owned elsewhere: CI-subject default (7); duplicate constant (13); [0] on a multi-device set (index-count); env var without comment; wrong identifier in the body (stale-body); misnamed flag (comment-contradicts, 5106398334).
skill_entry.finding_shape: (a): "`<alias>` (<file:line>) is an alias of the generic `<template>`, and <test:line> asserts it is constructible from `<pointer type>`. So any wrapped pointer or same-shaped view passes `<kernel>`; '<claim>' holds for <distinct-type subjects> only. Please say so in the description." (b), (c): "`<identifier>` is only <timed | read> at <file:line>, on the <path>. The <other path> at <file:line> is <never timed | reads `chunks[0]`>. So <`<metric>` reads 0 on <configuration>; the sample's 0 comes from that config | spec and function disagree>; '<claim>' holds for <subject> only. Either <time the poll | assert size() == 1>, or narrow the text." (d), a question: "would it make sense to flip <literal> to <value> at the same time, to make things consistent?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Normal, as a statement, for a timer or guarantee claim: a fact, 'So <consequence>', then two remedies ('Either time the SW poll too ..., or narrow the docs'); the timer finding (4125033634) was the first of the five inline comments of his PR 4596 review 5342222359 (lowest id; review body: 'A few correctness and semantics issues inline, plus two design questions') and carried no severity word. 'Fine as a first step, but please say so in the description' for a staged type guarantee. A question for a spec-versus-code gap ('So is the spec wrong? Or are these functions insufficient?'). Minor, question form, for a default literal ('would it make sense to flip this to 1 at the same time, to make things consistent?'), approved regardless of the answer. Never blocking, never CHANGES_REQUESTED.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at HEAD (the timer's other paths and the enclosing function of each stamp, the unchanged `#ifndef` lines 40 lines below the hunk); other files (README*.md, doc/*.md, CMakeLists.txt, the Note's header, view.hpp for aliases); PR body at review time (GraphQL userContentEdits) including its sample output; callers (the functions that grow a container and their call sites; the increment site of the sibling path counter); the tests' constructibility probes. Not CI, not runtime.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 6: claim wider than the code (guarantees, timed paths, element counts, defaults)

Setup for a merged PR (applies to every kind): HEAD = the commit the review names (the `### inline <id> at <time>` header of the digest, or the review's commit field). `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself for a merged PR and gives an empty diff, so take BASE = `git -C WT merge-base HEAD M^1` where M = `git -C WT log --merges --first-parent --format=%H --grep='#N' origin/main | head -1`. On PR 4596: M = c1331f3fb2, M^1 = 9b60b69dce, BASE = 66c7bb8db1 (diff 1891 lines, 10 files).

Step 1 (kind (a)), replace the grep with a prose-only one: `grep -n -i -E 'compile error|cannot be (passed|handed)|reject|enforce|no (bare|raw|public) pointer|STATIC_REQUIRE|static_assert|typed view so that|neither takes' body.md log.txt; grep -n -E '^\+\s*(//|\*)' pr.diff | grep -i -E '<same pattern>'; git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- doc 'README*.md' | grep -n -i -E '<same pattern>'`. A `static_assert` code line and a register JSON `desc` string ('enforced at the bottom of each Systolic Column', PRs 2180/3631) are the enforcing declaration or hardware prose, not a claim. Steps 2-7 stay as written.

Append after the existing "On PR 4557" line:

8. Measured-path claims. Timers and counters the diff adds, code only: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -n -E '^\+.*(rdtsc\(\)|inc_relaxed\(|fetch_add\(|_cycles\b|note_[a-z_]+\()'`; a doc/*.md or script line is never an added timer (PR 2203 doc line 'usage_time = rdtsc()'). Map each identifier X to its label L first: `grep -n -o -E 'T[0-9] = .*' body.md` and `git -C WT show HEAD:h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp | grep -n -o -E 'T[0-9] = [^.]*'` (gives `T5 = join_wait_cycles`). Then per X: `grep -n -E "X|\bL\b" body.md`; and sentence-level over the repository, because a doc sentence wraps and a Note names a timer by its label: `for f in README.stats.md h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp <files of the diff>; do git -C WT show HEAD:$f | tr '\n' ' ' | grep -o -E "[^.]*(X|\bL\b)[^.]*\."; done`. Keep the sentences that match the whole-word filter `grep -w -i -E 'ends when|whichever|in both|either|every'`; keep 'or the' and 'and the' only when the same sentence names X or L. (`-w` keeps 'neither' out: PR 2693 comment '0 = neither K nor V saved' matched the old filter through the substring 'either' and matches `-w` 0 times; README.stats.md:261 still matches through 'ends when'.) One subject row per path named. Clear a sentence whose X is one accumulator with one start and one stop that bracket every named part (`X -= rdtsc()` before the first part, `X += ...` after the last, no `return` or `continue` between): body.md:19 (T2 'both passes and the join', attn_elapsed :820 to :852 around run_joins :843) clears this way.
9. For each named path find the selector and the wait in the file at HEAD: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E 'const bool (join_hw|uses_hw)|if \((!)?(join_hw|uses_hw)|hw_plan\.empty|continue;  // poll|while \(!'` (drop parameter and signature lines; the plain `uses_hw|stats_enabled` grep gives 40 hits in a 2078-line file, 30 of them signatures). Then the stamps of X: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E 'X|t_wait|t_poll|rdtsc'`. For each start or stop stamp name its enclosing function (`awk 'NR<=<stamp line> && /^    [a-z_:<>]+ [a-z_]+\(/ {l=NR": "$0} END{print l}'`) and the line that calls that function; the branch guarding the call (`if (join_hw)` for stream_hw_joins) is the path the stamp belongs to. Write per path: start line, stop line, or "untimed" (no stamp between the selector and the `note_*` call).
10. Sample output at review time: `gh api graphql -f query='query{repository(owner:"positron-ai",name:"tron"){pullRequest(number:N){userContentEdits(first:30){nodes{editedAt diff}}}}}'`; take the review timestamp from the digest and read the `diff` field of the latest edit before it (the field holds the full body, not a unified diff). Then `grep -n -E '"X":0' body.md README*.md`. For each hit read the whole sample block and the prose line that introduces it; the configuration comes from a path counter in the same block (`fpga_k_tokens`, `fpga_queries`: `git -C WT grep -n 'note_fpga_pass(' HEAD -- h src` gives its increment site and the branch it sits in; 0 there means that path never ran, so the selector of that path was false), `n_workers` in the summary block, and the run shape in the prose. A 0 for X with the other path's counter also 0 is the consequence sentence. A zero is a finding candidate, never evidence of no work.
11. Element-count claims, production files only: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*(\[0\]|\.front\(\))'`. Drop a hit whose receiver is a string (`std::string`, `string_view`, `const char*`: attn_stats.hpp `id.front() == '.'`), whose container has no grower in h/ or src/ (fixed array `bf16* x[N]`, `std::array`, `listeners[2]`), or whose removed twin differs only by whitespace (PR 2135 `attn[0].finish`). `.back()` reads, a stack top and an append-or-extend branch (PR 4353 `worker_plan.back()` after push_back, PR 2545 `shard_stack.back()`) do not trigger. For each container C use the full member expression (`pool.chunks`, never a bare word under 6 characters): `git -C WT grep -n -i -E 'one or more|multiple|several|a list of|exactly one|at most one' HEAD -- doc 'README*.md' h src | grep -i 'C'`; growers: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'C\.(push_back|emplace_back|insert|resize)\(' HEAD -- h src`; call sites of the growing function F: `git -C WT grep -n -E '\bF\(' HEAD -- h src t`. The cardinality sentence must name C itself, not its element type.
12. Default claims. skill_entry.name: 14. A bot finding is traced to the deciding line before it is endorsed, refuted or forwarded
skill_entry.trigger: The PR has an inline comment by cursor[bot] (Cursor Bugbot; REST login `cursor[bot]`, GraphQL author login `cursor`; the body carries `BUGBOT_BUG_ID` and a `**<Low|Medium|High> Severity**` line) whose thread is neither resolved nor outdated at the reviewed head, carries no author reply, and sits on a C++ line under h/, src/ or t/ that the diff adds or changes. Or the reviewer ran an agent review (Claude, GPT) of the whole diff. Graphite (`graphite-app[bot]`) and Codex (`chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`) comments are out of scope: none of Wade's 14 bot replies answers one, and every such comment in the corpus is on a PR he approved in silence (2774, 3756, 4353, asim-330).
skill_entry.procedure:
1. Fetch the review threads (GraphQL reviewThreads: isResolved, isOutdated, first author) and the REST bodies. Per live finding write (symbol, claimed state, claimed consequence) and the severity word.
2. Bin: SENTINEL (a declared default such as `-1` reaches a callee), UNREACHABLE (a branch or default argument can no longer be taken), UNUSED, DUPLICATE-CONSTANT, CONCURRENCY.
3. SENTINEL: at the hunk line name the object the value is read from and its constructor. Grep the resolving initializer and every production constructor call. REFUTED when each call passes the resolved copy; quote the initializer.
4. UNREACHABLE: table the gate's input states; read the PR title and body. INTENDED when they name the behavior and the opt-in branch still enables.
5. UNUSED, DUPLICATE-CONSTANT, CONCURRENCY: run the owning check (dead symbol, re-derivation, shared state). A quoted invariant refutes; a stated race confirms; neither is UNKNOWN.
6. Verdict per finding with the deciding file:line.
skill_entry.question: Read at HEAD, which line decides the bot's claim (the initializer the value passes through, a caller that passes the parameter, or the PR title or body sentence that names the behavior as the goal), does it agree with the bot, and did you quote it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A thread with any author reply (2879602159 'It gets used, just not where this tool seems to be able to find it' and 2926693092 'Notified the FPGA team about this.' closed them for Wade with no line quoted; raise a real item under the owning check, as he did in 2941308844); a resolved or outdated thread; a claim on a line the diff does not add or change (3776964572 fake.cpp:169 exists at BASE; 3149408014 ranged_mask.cpp:20 is context); a claim decided by a number (divisor, bound, overflow: 2879962155, 3149408014, and 3156982388 left unanswered on his own loud PR 2565); a duplicate-constant or name claim (2879962438); a finding on a script, README, JSON or register-map file (1727, 2180, 4353; all 14 replies are on C++ files); the flagged behavior when the title or body names it as the purpose (3659990818); a dead parameter the bot adds in passing (`default_enabled`); forwarded agent items marked optional (C41: never a blocker). Never re-grade severity, recompute numbers or post CHANGES_REQUESTED.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Refute: "this is a false positive... `<member>` is initialized like this: <quoted initializer, file:line>, so when <input> is not given it inherits <resolved value>". Confirm: "I think this is a legit concern... did you run <test> to see if you hit <symptom>?" or "I do think there's merit to this complaint. <mechanism in your own words, file:line>". Intended: "that's the point of this PR... '<state>' leaves it <value>, and `<opt-in>` still turns it on. Looks fine to me.". Unknown (only with a named run or unit case): "was this intentional?". Forward: "I did ask claude to do a review as well. Below are the items it came up with. I do think there's some merit to a few of them, but could be a follow-up if you prefer."
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: None for a refutation or an intended-behavior answer: he approved PR 3488 22 s after 3659990818 (review 4790383475, 18:45:25Z and 18:45:47Z). A confirmed claim is 'a legit concern' (3156090573), stated as a question naming the test that would show it, or 'merit to this complaint' (2983833171), stated as the mechanism in his own words; neither is a block. Forwarded agent items are 'some merit... could be a follow-up if you prefer. I'll approve as-is' (4800935083). A cleanup is 'please clean this up' (2915281512). He never writes CHANGES_REQUESTED, never re-grades the bot's severity word, and leaves findings he cannot decide from the code unanswered (3075799778 on 2426, 3156982388 on 2565).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk + other files (the initializer and every caller at HEAD) + PR title and body + the review-thread state (resolved, outdated, author reply); runtime only as a question to the author (a multi-user run) when the code alone cannot decide.

3. SENTINEL: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<line-5>,<line+2>p'` names the expression; `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n '<object>\b'` finds the member declaration and the constructor that receives it. INTENDED when the title or a body sentence names the behavior and the opt-in branch still returns the enabling value. A parameter the change leaves dead is a cleanup note, not a finding.
5. UNUSED: run check "dead symbol" (`git -C WT grep -n '<symbol>(' HEAD -- h src t ingest`; header: `git -C WT grep -n -E '#include.*<file>' HEAD -- h src t`), record each caller file:line and the argument in the claimed position, and grep the enclosing function family too so that 'only caller' claims name every hit. CONCURRENCY: run the shared-state check; `git -C WT grep -n -i -E '<container>.*(lock|mutex|append-only|only grows|never removed|single writer)' HEAD -- h src`. A quoted invariant: REFUTED. A TODO or Note that names the hazard: CONFIRMED. Neither: UNKNOWN.

skill_entry.name: 14. A workaround for an unexplained defect needs a tracked exit
skill_entry.trigger: Any one, in the diff's added lines under h/, src/ or t/, in this PR's own commit messages, or in the PR body: (a) a comment or commit message calls a behavior a workaround (workaround, work-around, hack) and says the cause is unknown (unidentified, unexplained, not understood, 'root cause is an open question', 'See TODO' with no id after it); (b) a TEST_CASE or SECTION that the diff adds, or adds assertions to, whose header comment (the comment lines between the unit's opening line and its first statement) says the unit guards or protects a workaround, a hang avoidance, or an ordering 'required for production hardware'; (c) a commit of this PR declares a helper obsolete for a named hardware or firmware version ('No longer necessary with 1.5.7.0', 'fixed in bitfile X') while another helper for the same defect (zero, clear, scrub, NaN) survives in t/ or in the files the diff touches.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. BASE is the merge-base against the PR's base branch (gh pr view N --json baseRefName), not origin/main. 2. Grep the added lines (h/ src/ t/ only), this PR's commit messages and the body for workaround and unknown-cause words. An unknown-cause hit counts only with a workaround word within 15 lines of it or in the same commit message; a .md or doc/ hit never counts. 3. Classify each hit: UNEXPLAINED (cause unknown), NAMED-DEFECT (defect named), PROVISIONAL ('for now' about a size, default or ordering, no defect), REMOVAL. 4. Per UNEXPLAINED hit: search the 31-line window, the oldest commit that added the phrase, and the body for a tracker id; a body id closes the hit only inside a workaround paragraph. 5. Per triggered test unit: the header must state permanent contract plus a consumer, or a TODO plus the condition that replaces the test; an id in the TODO is optional. 6. Per obsolescence commit: list surviving sibling helpers, their TRON_*_WORKAROUND gate and whether a build file defines the macro.
skill_entry.question: Is this workaround temporary or permanent? If temporary, which story tracks the root cause, and where does the test say what replaces it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: NAMED-DEFECT workarounds: a defect name alone passes in silence (tron-2008 'as a workaround for DMA/NOC issue' with no owner and no exit, tron-2135 'Until we get a fixed bitfile', both approved with no text; tron-2302 'temporary workaround ... present in the latest bitfile' drew only a comments ask, 3036997452). A removed workaround (tron-2011). A bare TODO without an id: origin/main h/ src/ t/ carries 133 TODO/FIXME/XXX lines and only 4 carry a tracker id. An id-less TODO that states the replacement condition (origin/main:t/t_heap_v2.cpp:244). A pre-existing unit at HEAD that cites a workaround and the diff does not add or widen (t/t_hwattention.cpp 'transfer_k_and_v' at the heads of PRs 2475, 2875, 3756, 4353, all silent). A workaround commit that belongs to another PR on the same side branch. A tracker id inside an explanatory Note (3350285744 asks to remove it). Gate polarity against the commit message (comment-contradicts-adjacent-code owns it). He never asks for the root cause before merge ('No harm it leaving it').
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<function>` (<file>:<line>) is described as a workaround for a bug nobody has identified, and `<TEST_CASE name>` (<test>:<line>) pins that behavior. do we have a ticket/story tracking this for follow up? If it is temporary, say so in the test with a TODO and the condition that replaces it; if it is permanent, name the consumer and drop the word workaround. Obsolescence variant: with <version> that fixed <defect>, `<helper>` (<file>:<line>) should not be needed anymore; no harm leaving it, but is it gated so it can be dropped?
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: A plain question with no severity word for the missing tracker ('do we have a ticket/story tracking this for follow up?', 'so are we enshrining this work-around forever?'); the author changed the test the same day (3227468540 at 14:58Z, e4c4f49452 at 18:18Z). A self-note for the obsolete helper ('No harm it leaving it, but I have a to-do to circle back'), nit level; the author still gated it (958e77d919, reply 'fixed in commit 958e77d91' the next morning). Never blocking; he approved both PRs (ab8a7f758b 2026-05-18, 8e19ea3e62 2026-03-18).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the workaround comment), other files (the guarding test under t/ for a production comment under src/), commits (the commit that added the workaround and any commit of this PR that declares a sibling helper obsolete for a version; the version-fixed-defect claim is read from that commit message, no hardware knowledge is needed), PR body (tracker ids, read per paragraph), build files (whether any defines a TRON_*_WORKAROUND macro); no CI or runtime evidence needed.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a workaround for an unexplained defect needs a tracked exit

Setup for this check: the PR's base branch, not origin/main. `BASEREF=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$BASEREF)`. On PR 2713 origin/main gives 426 commits and 42 step-1 hits; origin/hwattention_sync gives 20 commits and 10 hits. `gh pr view N --json body -q .body > body.md`.

1. Hits, three sources.
   a. Added code lines, already as HEAD file:line: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3)} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); n=a[2]; next} /^\+/{print f":"n": "$0; n++}' | grep -i -E 'work-?around|\bhack\b|unidentified|unexplained|not understood|root cause|open question'`. Do not add `for now` or `until the` to this grep; they matched only ordinary comments (t/t_heap_v2.cpp:502, t/t_token_tree_refcount.cpp:87, tron-1722 x5, PR 4596 x3). Limiting to h src t removes the design-spec 'Open questions' headings under doc/.
   b. This PR's commit messages, each hit prefixed with its commit id: `git -C WT log --format='COMMIT %h %s%n%b' --no-merges BASE..HEAD | awk '/^COMMIT /{c=$2} /work-?around|unexplained|root cause|open question|no longer (necessary|needed) (with|in|on|since) |fixed in (bitfile|firmware|release|v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)/ {print c": "$0}'`. Keep only commits of this PR when the side branch carries other PRs: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/commits/<sha>/pulls --jq '.[].number'` must list N.
   c. Body: `grep -n -i -E 'work-?around|pending (a |the )?(fix|bitfile|firmware)|until (we|a|the) .*(bitfile|firmware|fix)|bitfile [0-9]' body.md`; record the paragraph of each hit.
2. Classify each hit. Mechanical rule first: a hit on an unknown-cause word (unidentified, unexplained, not understood, root cause, open question) counts only when a workaround word (work-?around, hack) appears within 15 lines of it in the same file at HEAD (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L-15)),$((L+15))p" | grep -i -E 'work-?around|\bhack\b'`) or in the same commit message. Classes: UNEXPLAINED = the text says the cause is unknown. NAMED-DEFECT = the text names the defect (a component or bus such as DMA/NOC, a bitfile or firmware version, an issue id, a hardware state such as post-power-cycle); an owner or exit condition is welcome but not required. PROVISIONAL = a 'for now', 'temporarily' or 'until' about a size, default, ordering or test scope with no defect named; never continues. REMOVAL = a removed line or a commit that drops a workaround. Only UNEXPLAINED continues at step 3; REMOVAL and obsolescence commits continue at step 5.
3. Tracker search per UNEXPLAINED hit at HEAD line L of FILE. Window: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L-15)),$((L+15))p" | grep -n -E 'STORY-[0-9]+|[A-Za-z_]+#[0-9]+|#[0-9]{3,}|notion\.so/|/issues/[0-9]+'`. Adding commit: `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' -S'<distinct phrase of the comment>' BASE..HEAD`; when a fixup reworded the comment several commits return, take the oldest (last line) and read it with `git -C WT log -1 --format=%B <sha> | grep -n -E '<id pattern>'`. Body: the same id grep over body.md, but an id closes the hit only when it sits in a paragraph that step 1c matched; an id elsewhere names another item (on PR 2713 body.md:1 'STORY-425' is the fragmentation story, step 1c matched 0 paragraphs, so the heap_v2.cpp:293 hit stays). No id anywhere = finding (a question).
4. Guarding tests, diff test files only (never all of t/ at HEAD; the whole-tree form returned 7 pre-existing hits in 4 untouched files on PR 2713 and fires on four silent PRs): `git -C WT grep -n -i -E 'work-?around|silently flipped|\bhang\b|required for production' HEAD -- $(git -C WT diff --name-only BASE HEAD -- 't/*')`. Enclosing unit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<test> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR<=L && /TEST_CASE\(|SECTION\(|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\(/ {n=NR; name=$0} END{print n": "name}'`. A unit counts only when the diff adds it or adds assertions to it, or when its body calls the helper that a step-2 UNEXPLAINED hit describes; a comment above a helper function is not a unit header. Header range: `git -C WT show HEAD:<test> | awk -v S=<unit start> 'NR>=S {print NR": "$0} NR>S && /REQUIRE|CHECK/ {exit}'`. Required: either a 'permanent contract' sentence with a named consumer (then check 1 owns the row), or `TODO` plus the condition that replaces the test (`grep -c -E 'TODO'` and read the sentence). An id inside the TODO is optional; the id must exist where the reviewer can read it (body paragraph, review reply, commit message). A header with neither sentence = finding.
5. Obsolescence, per step-1b commit that says a version fixed a defect. Sibling list from what the commit removed: `git -C WT show <sha> | grep -o -E '^-[^/]*\b[a-z_]*(clear|zero|scrub|nan)[a-z_]*\b' | sort -u`, plus the defect word from its message (NaN, hang, DMA); then `git -C WT grep -n -i -E '<those stems>|clear_|zero_|zeroi[sz]e|scrub' HEAD -- h src t`. Gates: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'TRON_[A-Z_]*WORKAROUND' HEAD -- h src t CMakeLists.txt t/CMakeLists.txt nix flake.nix CMakePresets.json GNUmakefile`. For each survivor record whether a gate wraps it and whether any build file defines the macro. Do not grade the directive against the commit message here; a message that says 'compiles out by default' over an `#ifndef` is a comment-contradicts-adjacent-code finding.
6. Report one question per step-3 miss, one per step-4 unit, one nit per step-5 survivor ('no harm leaving it, but is it gated so it can be dropped?') with its gate and definition site.

Where the precision and executability lenses disagreed on the kind (b) discriminator, the executability form (the production producer evaluated on the fixture's own values) is used, because it is a computation an agent can run; the precision form (a real model's value) needs model knowledge the diff does not give.

skill_entry.name: 1. Value-pinning rows need a consumer; fixture placeholders need a don't-care comment; opaque expected literals need a provenance
skill_entry.trigger: Any one of three. (a) Conversion row: a test hunk adds a runtime assertion whose expected literal or table entry differs from the bits the same test wrote or read back earlier by a conversion, rounding (ties included), flush, saturation or class change (NaN to inf, denormal to zero). A pure widening is no difference; compile-time rows are check 2. (b) Fixture placeholder: the hunk adds a line assigning a round literal (1.0f, 0, 4) with no comment to a field of a model-parameter or configuration struct that is then passed by pointer or reference to the function under test. (c) Opaque literal: the hunk adds an equality assertion whose expected side is 32 or more hex characters, or a table of four or more entries no test expression derives, with no provenance comment and no repository document containing it.
skill_entry.procedure: (a) Keep round trips, read-backs, kept partners and rows whose discarded bits are zero. For each other row name the storing accessor, search h/ and src/ for a reader, format or AGENTS.md line that depends on the exact bits (a policy or history comment is none), and compute the second policy (the generic converter, or the function a comment says 'would' differ) on the row's input. (b) Follow the struct to the first production call; in the hardware implementation, not the stub, record the field as read on the exercised path, read in an unreached branch, or never read. Evaluate the production producer on the fixture's own values: never read and unequal is a placeholder. Count repeats in every touched test file. (c) Read upward to the first blank line or def/TEST_CASE for a comment naming a generator, date, revision or copied-from file:line; grep documents for the literal; grep AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, if present, for a register mandate.
skill_entry.question: Name what depends on this exact value: for a conversion row, the production reader, format or repository rule that breaks if it changes; for a fixture literal, the exercised line that reads the field; for an opaque literal, the command, date and source revision that produced it, and the register row that lists it. If nothing does, say so next to the value or drop the row.
skill_entry.do_not_fire:
- pair-invariant rows when the test or its accessor cites the Note naming the dependent path; otherwise ask for the citation.
- regression rows for a failure seen on main or in the product; rows pinning a documented wire, file or hardware format.
- a fixture literal equal to the production producer evaluated on the fixture's own values (`params.gqa = 4` with `n_heads = n_kv_heads * 4` equals src/tron/gof.cpp:65 `n_heads / n_kv_heads`; the callee reads gqa no more than pre_attn_scalar).
- a fixture literal the exercised callee reads (a wrong stimulus is a correctness finding), or one already commented as a placeholder.
- a literal that exists at BASE on a re-spelled call (API migration); positional aggregate or constructor arguments.
- an opaque literal whose constant or docstring names an authority, generator or revision; a commit id quoted as a citation; a digest used as a lookup key for a golden artifact (`reference_logits`); digests in generated .json files.
- never recompute a value or dispute a tolerance.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (a) "This row makes '<input> stores as <output>' a tested contract. <AGENTS.md:line '<rule>' | no reader in h/ or src/ depends on <policy>; the only statement is the test comment '<quote>'>. Suggest dropping <rows> and keeping <the round trip and the partner-zero checks>." (b) a suggestion block on the first assignment: "<field> = <literal>; // not correct, but it's a don't-care for this usage below" then "and similarly elsewhere this is done" with the repeat lines; hits in other files of the same PR go on a second line of the same finding. (c) a question: "is this 'magic' <digest|table> captured or documented anywhere? Where did it come from? Are these supposed to be listed in <register doc> (referenced from AGENTS.md:<line>)?"; with no register, ask for a comment naming the command, date and revision.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Kind (a): normal, a declarative statement with the repository rule named and a 'Suggest dropping ... and keeping ...' ask; no severity word. Kind (b): no severity word; the whole comment is a ```suggestion block with the comment text plus the sentence 'and similarly elsewhere this is done'; the author replied 'fixed in commit 8a6db7243'. Kind (c): normal, a question in three parts ('captured/documented anywhere? Where did it come from? Are these supposed to be listed in ...'); the author replied 'Good catch: it was not registered.' None of the three blocks the PR; he approved PR 2176 (3969129694 at 8e19ea3e62), asim 244 (5240537644 at 63c5b8a12c) and PR 4557 (5431977719 at c5d44bd86f) after the fixes.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the row, the assignment, the assertion); full test files the diff touches (repeat count of a fixture block across files; the comment block above an assertion up to the first blank line); other files (the hardware implementation of the callee, not the stub; the production producer of the field; the generic converter); repository policy files at HEAD when they exist (AGENTS.md test-policy line, NaN rule, register mandate; CLAUDE.md) and the register document itself (docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md in asim). A test file at the review commit, fetched with gh api contents when the PR diff shows only the merged head. Not callers, PR body, commits, CI or runtime. Boundary: a round literal in a t/ fixture belongs here (kind b); a bare literal on an added h/ or src/ line belongs to the magic-literal check.

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 1: value-pinning rows need a consumer; fixture placeholders a don't-care comment; opaque literals a provenance

BASE for this check (and the common setup): a merged PR whose base branch is not main gives an empty diff under `merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` (it returns HEAD) and a 30-file diff under `origin/main` (PR 2176: 25 step-9 hits instead of 4). Use the PR's recorded base: `BASE_SHA=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/<repo>/pulls/N --jq .base.sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $BASE_SHA)` (PR 2176 at HEAD 635de61895: base sha 363edb2910, BASE 1794cdf67d, 19 files).

Steps 1-8 unchanged (conversion rows, kind (a)). Steps 9-14 are new.

9. Fixture placeholders, kind (b). Print HEAD lines directly: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 't/*' 'tests/*' | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3); next} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); n=a[2]; next} /^\+/{ if ($0 ~ /^\+[ \t]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\.|->)[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*[ \t]*=[ \t]*(1\.0f?|0\.0f?|[0-9]+)[ \t]*;[ \t]*$/) print f":"n": "$0; n++; next}'`. It lists added assignments of a round literal to a struct field with no trailing comment. Record the struct variable (`params`) and the field (`pre_attn_scalar`). A literal that exists at BASE on the same statement (an API re-spelling such as `push(0, ...)` to `push(process_device_id{0}, ...)`) and a positional aggregate or constructor argument are not hits.
10. Callee: `grep -n -E '&<var>\b|<var>\)' full/<file>` from the assignment downward to the first production call that takes the struct (PR 2176: `xfer_blocking(..., &params, ...)`). `git -C WT grep -n '<callee>' HEAD -- h src` returns every implementation, including a stub (src/pos/fake.cpp, empty bodies). Open the implementation the test binary links on hardware (the file under src/pos/ that is not fake.cpp): `git -C WT show HEAD:<callee file> | grep -n -E '<param>->|\.<field>'`. Record per field: READ on the exercised path (stop, not a placeholder), READ in an unreached branch, or NEVER READ. Record the stub separately as "stub, reads nothing"; a field the hardware implementation reads is READ.
11. Real producer: `git -C WT grep -n '<field>' HEAD -- h src`; pick by reading the line that computes the production value. Evaluate it with the fixture's own values. For gqa: src/tron/gof.cpp:65 `gof_params.gqa = n_heads / n_kv_heads` with the fixture's `n_heads = n_kv_heads * 4` gives 4, equal to the literal: not a placeholder. For pre_attn_scalar: h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:396 `1.0f / sqrtf(head_size)` (635de61895; :395 at 429249ead6) with head_size 128 gives 0.088, so 1.0f is a placeholder. A literal is a placeholder when the exercised callee NEVER READs it and it differs from the producer evaluated on the fixture's shape.
12. Repeats: `grep -n '<field> = <literal>' full/*` over every test file the diff touches, plus every step-9 hit in another file. The finding is one suggestion block on the first line plus "and similarly elsewhere this is done" listing the repeats in the commented file; hits in other files of the same PR go on a second line of the same finding, never as separate findings. A pre-existing line that step 9 did not list (not added by the PR) is mentioned at most as pre-existing.
13. Opaque literals, kind (c): assertions `grep -n -E '^\+.*(\b(REQUIRE|CHECK)[A-Z_]*\(|\bassert\b)[^/]*\b[0-9a-f]{32,}\b' pr.diff` (word-bounded, so CHECKPOINT does not match); frozen tables `grep -n -E '^\+.*(\b(REQUIRE|CHECK)[A-Z_]*\(|\bassert\b).*\[(\s*0x[0-9a-f]+\s*,){3,}' pr.diff`; a literal bound to a name first `grep -n -E '^\+\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\s*=\s*"[0-9a-f]{32,}"' pr.diff` (digits allowed in the name; on asim 244 this finds RTL_REVISION, EXP_TABLE_SHA256 and FROZEN_D128_CHECKPOINT_DIGEST), then follow the name into an assertion. Use grep -E, not awk, for `{32,}` (mawk ignores the interval). Map to file:line at HEAD. `gh pr diff N` shows only the merged head: to run at the commit next to a comment, fetch each touched test file with `gh api 'repos/<org>/<repo>/contents/<path>?ref=<commit>' --jq .content | base64 -d > full/<path>` and grep it; a hit is a finding only if the line is also an added line of the PR diff. A table is a hit only on the expected side of an equality assertion; GENERATE rows, stimulus fractions and tolerance arguments are never an expected side.
14. Provenance: read upward from the assertion to the first blank line or the enclosing `def`/TEST_CASE line, whichever comes first (`sed -n '<start>,<line>p' full/<file>`), and keep only a comment that names a generator, a date, a source revision, or the production file:line the table is copied from (`g_dequant` in t/t_clearhbm.cpp at tron-2475 cites h/tron/hardware/quantization.hpp:99 and is not a finding). A comment stating what the value must stay equal to is not a provenance. `git -C WT grep -n '<first 12 hex characters>' HEAD -- docs doc '*.md' '*.json'`. Register mandate: `git -C WT show HEAD:AGENTS.md | grep -n -i -E 'regist|anchored|evidence|provenance|frozen'`, same for CLAUDE.md; if the file does not exist at HEAD (`git show` fails, as at 635de61895), record "no register mandated" and continue. Register present and literal absent -> the finding asks for the origin and the register row, citing the AGENTS.md line that names the register. Register absent -> the finding asks for a comment with the generating command, the date and the revision. A literal whose definition carries an authority or revision line (EXP_TABLE_SHA256 under "Authority: executable RTL <sha>") is not a finding; a digest that selects a golden artifact for a tolerance comparison (`reference_logits`, t/testutil.hpp:33, `check_golden_logits`) is a lookup key, not an expected value.

skill_entry.name: 4. Same experiment run twice, or run in a new place
skill_entry.trigger: Three forms; any one fires. Form A: the PR adds or widens two test units (TEST_CASE, SECTION, GENERATE arm, template instantiation) that make the same production call with the same constants, token or size set and source type, and reach the same leaf branches of a function the diff changed; two arms of one GENERATE that differ only in token count are not two units. Form B: two new units in one test file assert the return of one production function with named constants; unit A asserts only that return, unit B REQUIREs the same (arguments, expected) pairs, directly or on a local the call initializes, then asserts an effect of the result; a branchless one-line helper fires. Form C: a new t/*.cpp with an add_catch_test or add_executable_test line and a config/test-benchmarks.json row (the per-test cost table that CI step `bin/slice bench --check` reads), whose called production function a TEST_CASE in an existing binary already reaches, directly or through a constructor or destructor.
skill_entry.procedure: BASE = merge-base of HEAD and the PR base sha (`gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha`); merge-base with origin/main returns HEAD or a PR commit once the PR is merged. Form A: name each unit's production call, follow it to the leaf branches the diff changed, map every input to its arm, simulate write order, record (branch, slot, reference, precision, read path) per unit, compare pairwise. Form B: grep every added test line for `<fn>(`, not only assertion lines; group by unit; open the body and count branches; list A's pairs, B's REQUIREs and B's assertions after it uses the result. Form C: name the function the new TEST_CASE calls (inside a lambda counts), its production callers, the existing test files that call it or construct a caller (search `type<` and every `using alias = type<`), and both registration lines' DEFINES, LIBRARIES, LABELS, RESOURCE_LOCK, MODEL_REQUIREMENTS; date PR-body cost passages with userContentEdits.
skill_entry.question: Is there a deliberate code break that fails unit A but passes unit B; and, for a new test binary, which existing binary already executes the function under test, so that the case and its define belong there?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Units with different source value types, token sets or production calls; a pre-existing unit changed only in API spelling; units under different build or hardware gates (check 3). Form B: a helper with a branch B's inputs do not reach (run Form A); a fork-based negative case that asserts the function aborts. Form C: a new binary needing a library, resource lock or MODEL_REQUIREMENTS entry the existing target lacks (state the property); a t/CMakeLists.txt-only edit of existing registrations (tron-2844, RESOURCE_LOCK on the hugepages tests, approved with no text); a new primitive with no existing test of its callers. Never ask for a missing test on its own, never recompute an expected value; test-only fixes by the hardware-attention authors are approved in silence.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Form A: "`<unit A>` and `<unit B>` (line <N>) run the same <inputs> through <call>, reaching <branches>. <B> already checks <what, against which reference, through which read path>; this one adds <nothing | the (branch, slot) pair B overwrites before reading>. The test policy rules out duplicate coverage that protects no distinct behavior: <drop this one | extend B by <edit> and drop this one>." Form B: "Nit: this case duplicates <unit B> (line <N>), which already checks the same mapping (`REQUIRE(<expr>)` for <input 1>, `REQUIRE(<expr>)` for <input 2>) and also checks the outcome that matters: <effect>. This one adds only the arithmetic of a one-line function, so it could be dropped." Form C: "Do we really need a whole new UT module for this test? `<existing binary>` already has <cases> that <construct and destroy X> (which executes `<function>`). Could we just enable <define> on that existing UT and incorporate this test there?"

Form B: "Nit:" and "so it could be dropped"; the author dropped the case the same day (reply 4148253103, 2026-09-30T19:00Z). Form C: a question, no severity word ("Do we really need a whole new UT module for this test?"); he approved at 4b98dc134a 9.6 hours later (2026-09-10T00:57Z) once the test moved. ## Check 4: same experiment run twice, or run in a new place

Preamble (BASE). `PRBASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $PRBASE)`. The common-setup line `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` is wrong once main contains the head: on PR 4596 at 0f784c44ff it returns 0f784c44ff (empty diff), on PR 4265 at 7a7699b338 it returns e2f22c7a09, the PR's own fix commit (the production hunk drops out). Correct values: 66c7bb8db1 for 4596, a80b102c18 for 4265 (4 files, 57 insertions). Without network, take the PR's merge commit from `git -C WT log --first-parent --format='%h %p %s' origin/main | grep '#N'` and use `git merge-base <its first parent> HEAD` (PR 4596: merge c1331f3fb2, first parent 9b60b69dce, BASE 66c7bb8db1).

Form A (two units, one call):

1. `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -- 't/*' | grep -n '^+.*\(TEST_CASE\|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE\|SECTION(\|GENERATE(\)'` lists added or widened units. `git -C WT log --format='%h %s%n%b' BASE..HEAD -- t/` marks commits answering several gap items at once; their units are the first pair to check. Two arms of one GENERATE are two units only when they differ in something other than the token or size set (silent tron-1739: 10 tokens on 1 page against 256 tokens on 2 pages, t/t_llama_unit.cpp:207-214, no fire).
2. For each unit name the production call under test (the first production call after the unit's own writes). `git -C WT grep -n '<call>' HEAD -- t/` lists pre-existing units on the same call; one changed only in API spelling stays out.
3. Follow the call to the leaf function with branches the diff changed. Map every input (each GENERATE value, each token index) to the arm it reaches.
4. Simulate the write order of each unit: a slot counts as observed only if no later write in the same unit replaces it before an assertion reads it.
5. Record per unit the set of (branch, slot, reference, precision, read path) its assertions observe.
6. Compare pairwise. Subset: drop the smaller. Partial: name the (branch, slot) only A observes, give B that observation with one concrete edit, drop A.
7. Compare the comment above each unit with the table: "exercises N cases" holds only if the assertions observe all N.

On PR 4557 (HEAD 96a6220ab6, BASE e5fa372c19): units t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3298 (poison GENERATE) and :3650/:3664 (bit-exact section), both `dst_book.append(src_book)` (:3357, :3685), both from commit 707159b9ef. copy_token arms: even<-even andnot h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp:359-364, even<-odd srli :378-384. Poison: dst 2 -> last copy 6<-4 (andnot), dst 3 -> 6<-3 (srli); observed slot 7 via scaled_v at :3385. Bit-exact: page of 64, last copies 63<-61 / 63<-60 overwrite every odd partner before the loop at :3687-3696 reads it; observes copied lanes against source_bits. Verdict: partial overlap; concrete edit = leave the last odd slot of the bit-exact page poisoned, require zero bits after the append, then drop the GENERATE. Outcome at c5d44bd86f: the poison section (:3275) is back to `dst_tokens = ODD_START_DST_TOKENS_3` (:3279), the bit-exact GENERATE stays (:3639).

Form B (helper arithmetic subsumed by an outcome case):

8. (a) `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE..HEAD -- 't/*.cpp' | grep -n -E '^\+.*[A-Za-z_]+(->|\.)[a-z_]+\(' | sed -E 's/.*(->|\.)([a-z_]+)\(.*/\2/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` counts every production method called on an added test line, assertion or assignment (an assertion-only grep misses unit B, which asserts on a local). (b) Drop container and accessor names (find, empty, size, load, at, begin, end) and keep the functions the PR adds or changes in h/ or src/: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -- h src | grep -E '^\+.*\b<fn>\('`. (c) Map each kept function to units over the full file, not only assertion lines: `git show HEAD:<file> | awk '/^TEST_CASE\(/{name=$0} /<fn>\(/{u[name]++} END{for(k in u) print u[k], k}'`. Drop a unit whose only calls sit inside a fork or signal lambda (the negative case). Take every function with hits in two or more remaining units.

finals.label: test-name-tag-output-conventions

skill_entry.name: 5. A test's name, tag list and result print agree with its assertions and with the file's convention
skill_entry.trigger: Any one. (A) Name: the diff adds, removes or rewrites an assertion, a comment or the stimulus inside a TEST_CASE or SECTION, or a comment inside the unit flips a verb (preserve/zero, keep/drop, accept/reject) while the name keeps the old verb. Re-spelling an expression inside an existing call or assertion, or moving a comment with its words unchanged, does not trigger. (B) Tag: the diff adds a test unit whose name and tag string are not both present at BASE in that file, every pre-existing unit of the file shares one tag count, and the new unit's tag count differs or one of its tags is not spelled from its name. (C) Print: the diff adds an unguarded counter print followed within three lines by a REQUIRE or CHECK of that counter against zero, in a file where at least one sibling summary print of that counter kind exists and every such print is guarded.
skill_entry.procedure: Iterate per unit, never per hunk. (A) Extract the verb and object from the name; read the setup; for each assertion that observes the object write 'fails when <state>'; the name must describe the passing state and agree with the verbs of the unit's own comments; grep the name in the file header comment and the PR body for rename sites. A new unit with no assertion stops with a one-line note. (B) Tabulate (macro, name, tags) for the whole file at HEAD, split multi-tag strings, mark the new units; convention = the tag count every pre-existing unit shares, with tags spelled from the name; candidate = a new unit that breaks it. (C) List the new unit's counter prints and the sibling summary prints with the line above each; drop per-element prints. Report A, B and C as separate nits.
skill_entry.question: Test label: reading the unit's name, tag string or result print next to the setup, the REQUIRE lines and the sibling units of the same file, does the label describe the state in which the assertions pass, and does it follow the pattern the siblings already use?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: (A) a topic label without a verb; a name wrong on main in a unit the diff touches only by re-spellings (note once); an assertion the name does not mention. (B) a pre-existing unit's tag (`[direct_rw_one]`, `[attention_command_Output_validation]`); a plain TEST_CASE among TEST_CASE_METHOD siblings whose single tag is spelled from its name (`[dma_xfer_state]`); a hidden `[.name]`; a moved unit; a new file; a file whose pre-existing units share no tag count or use shared topic tags (t_llama_unit.cpp `[kv_data]`). (C) a print with no REQUIRE on that counter (the per-fetcher print, PR 1666); a file whose sibling prints are unconditional (t_hwattention_replay.cpp); a print inside a helper that returns a bool; the log level; indentation. A hidden-tag flip is check 3; a label outside a Catch2 tag string is the identifier-name check; a comment against code lines is the comment-versus-code check.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (A) "Nit: the section is still named '<name>', but it now asserts that <opposite state> (REQUIRE at :<line>; the comment at :<line> says '<new verb>')." (B) a suggestion block with the tag spelled from the name, then: "maybe? Or... is/was the intention to start grouping a subset of these tests under the `[<tag>]` category (which makes sense too)? It's just that this is the only test using that atm..." (C) a suggestion block `if (<count>) <print>;` then: "... in the other tests, this is only printed if there were actually mismatches found. Should be consistent?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit for A (he writes "Nit:"); B is a suggestion block followed by "maybe?" with no severity word, read here as a nit; C is a suggestion block ending in a question ("Should be consistent?"), minor. Never blocking: the authors changed the code within two hours (PR 1666: 5e0bc3f788 at 18:05Z after the 17:20Z comment; PR 2078: f0134b976b at 17:48Z after 16:01Z) or the same local day (PR 4557: c5d44bd86f 2026-10-05 21:52 -0700 after the 20:18Z comment).

finals.procedure_commands:
## Check 5: a test's name, tag list and result print agree with its assertions and with the file's convention

Setup note. If `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD itself (a merged PR reviewed at a historical head) or the PR's base_ref is not main, take BASE from `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/commits --jq '.[0].parents[0].sha'`. On PR 2078: BASE = be689b7251, HEAD = 9d64b4a8bf (merge-base against origin/hwattention_sync returns HEAD; against origin/main returns b0df78db3c, which is wrong). When a comment's commit differs from the review's commit, anchor at `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/comments/<id> -q '.original_commit_id,.original_line'`.

1. Hunks: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -U0 -- 't/*.cpp' 't/*.hpp' | grep -n '^+++\|^@@\|^[-+]'`. Drop a hunk that only re-spells an expression inside an existing call or assertion (an argument, an index such as `queues[0]` to `queues[process_device_id{0}]`, a type wrapper) or moves a comment without changing its words: it adds no assertion and changes no statement about the code under test. New units: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -U0 -- 't/*.cpp' | grep -o -E '^\+ *(TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEST_CASE|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\(.*'`, then the HEAD line of each with `grep -n -F '<name>' full/<file>`. Moved-unit test: `git -C WT show BASE:<file> | grep -c -F '"<name>"'`; a unit whose name and tag string both exist at BASE is moved, not new. A hunk is only a container: run the rest per unit (every new unit, plus every pre-existing unit whose body a kept hunk changes).
2. Enclosing unit of a changed line L in a pre-existing unit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v L=<L> '/^(TEST_CASE|TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\(/ {t=NR; name=$0; s=0} /^  SECTION\(/ {s=NR; sn=$0} /^  }$/ {if (s) s=0} NR==L {print (s? s": "sn : t": "name); exit}'` (a SECTION at two-space indent closes at the next `  }` at that indent). A line above the first TEST_CASE stops here.
3. (A) Extract the name's verb and object. A new unit with no REQUIRE or CHECK stops here with the note "no assertion, name not judged by this check".
4. Read the setup lines that put the object into its pre-call state.
5. For every assertion that observes the object, directly or through a value computed from it (follow the read path), write "fails when <state>". Skip assertions that pin a write's partner invariant.
6. The name must describe the passing state and agree with the verbs of the unit's own comments. Comment flip in a changed unit: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -U0 -- <file> | grep -n '^@@\|^[-+] *//'`, keeping comment lines under a `@@` whose new-side start lies inside the unit. A new unit has no old comment to flip: compare the name verb with `awk -v S=<S> -v E=<E> 'NR>=S && NR<=E' full/<file> | grep -n '//'` and stop when they agree.
7. Rename sites: `grep -n '<name>' full/<file>` and the PR body; commit messages only if the PR will not be squashed. List them inside the one finding.
8. (B) Table of the whole file at HEAD, multi-line declarations flattened: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | tr '\n' ' ' | grep -o -E '(TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEST_CASE|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\([^{]*\{' | sed 's/ \+/ /g'`. Declaration lines: `grep -n -E '^(TEST_CASE|TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\(' full/<file>`. Per-tag membership with multi-tag strings split: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | tr '\n' ' ' | grep -o -E '(TEST_CASE_METHOD|TEST_CASE|TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE)\([^{]*\{' | grep -o -E '"\[[^"]*\]"' | tr -d '"' | sed 's/\]\[/\n/g; s/[][]//g; s/^\.//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`. Record per unit: new or pre-existing (step 1), tag count, and for each tag whether it is spelled from the name. Definition: a tag is spelled from the name when every word of the tag (split on `_`, leading `.` removed, case folded) equals a word of the name (split on `_` and space) or is a prefix of one (`poly` for `polymorphic`). Convention: the tag count that every pre-existing unit shares, and tags spelled from the name in all but at most one pre-existing unit. If the pre-existing units share no tag count, or their tags are topic tags shared by several units (t/t_llama_unit.cpp: `[kv_data]` has 12 members at a9a9cf30a4; t/t_hwattention_2.cpp mixes one-, two- and three-tag units at 05b6ac0549), the file has no convention and (B) stops. Candidate = a new unit whose tag count differs from the shared count, or any of whose tags is not spelled from its name. "A tag no sibling uses" is not a discriminator in a file where every tag has one member; keep it only as the wording of the question to the author.
9. (C) Unit range: S = the declaration line, E = the next declaration line minus 1 (end of file for the last unit). Counter prints only: `awk -v S=<S> -v E=<E> 'NR>=S && NR<=E' full/<file> | grep -n -A3 -E 'spdlog::(info|warn|error)\(' | grep -B3 -E '(REQUIRE|CHECK)\(.*== *0\)'`; keep a print only when the counter in its argument list is the one the REQUIRE compares. Banner and progress prints (no counter argument) are dropped without reading context. For each kept print record whether the preceding non-blank line is an `if (` whose condition names the counter.
10. Sibling summary prints of the same counter kind: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -B1 -E 'spdlog::(info|warn|error)\(".*(found|overall)'`; drop any hit whose preceding line is `++<counter>;` or that prints a per-element index (`K mismatch (head {}, idx {})`, b0e53be7e0:561, :592, :708, :739). A guard is any `if (` on the preceding non-blank line whose condition names the counter, including `if (a || b)` (9d64b4a8bf:1308) and `if (count > 0)`. (C) fires only when at least one sibling summary print exists, every one is guarded, and the new one is not; the finding is a suggestion block adding the guard in the siblings' spelling. Do not comment on the log level or on indentation.
11. Report A, B and C as separate nits anchored at the name, the macro line and the print line.

finals.label: buffer-lifetime-or-alignment

skill_entry.name: 14. A buffer's lifetime and alignment follow its consumer, not its declaration
skill_entry.trigger: Any one arm, each a grep over added production lines. Arm A, asynchronous release: an added line is an ownership transition of a DMA-heap buffer: allocation (`dma_allocate*`, `alloc_buffer`), release (`dma_deallocate`, `release_buffer`, `free_staging_if_idle`), submission (`xfer_blocks`, `xfer_n_blocks`, `xfer_gof(s)`), tracker push or pop, `reset()`/`abandon()` of the owning record, a destructor body, or a new owning member of a record handed to the engine (`pending_xfer`, `pinned_gof`, `pinned_batch`). Arm B, reserve literal: the diff adds `v.reserve(<number>)` on a std::vector and the same function holds a reference or pointer into `v` across `push_back`/`emplace_back`/`insert`/`resize`. Arm C, scratch to SIMD: a new `std::array<bf16|float|uint8_t|__m256i|__m512i, N>` or C array without `alignas`, whose pointer goes to `destination`/`dest`/`scratch`/`out` or a `std::function` member.
skill_entry.procedure: Arm A: per owning struct read destructor, `complete()`, `abandon()`, every holder. Write allocate -> populate -> submit -> tracker push -> completion (`poll_completions`, `hwcacheblock::wait`) -> release. List every other drop path (record destructor, `clear()`, `~dma_tracker` and whether it calls `clear()` before its queues die, `reset()`, queue out of scope); each waits, leaks on purpose (nulls `data`), or frees. A free after submission with no wait is the finding; a missing exclusivity assert is a nit inside it. Arm B: record the reserve value and what bounds the pushes; absent next to the reserve, the finding is the question. Then follow each growth call to the next read of the reference; a read reached without `continue`/`break`/`return` upgrades it to a defect (growth-call arguments are evaluated before reallocation). Arm C: resolve the consumer to one overload (match the destination pointer type; for a `std::function` member, every assignment site), grep its body for aligned intrinsics (`_mm256_*` 32 bytes, `_mm512_*` 64), compare with `alignas` or the element type's definition (bf16 = `__bf16`, 2 bytes), grep siblings in the file for `alignas`, check whether any test drives the real consumer. Runtime proof: a standalone UBSan reproducer (no tron build) or a `-S` stack offset; else `Insufficient data: not compiled`.
skill_entry.question: After the line that frees this buffer, hands it to its consumer, or could reallocate its container, who still reads it, does the declared alignment reach the consumer's widest aligned store, and what bounds the pushes past the reserve literal?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A drop path that runs only before submission (7f80aa17da:h/tron/gof.hpp:267-271). A buffer submitted and never freed (PR 1722 `hwcacheblock` blocks `new`ed into rings, no delete; APPROVED at aac65930a5). Type or parameter renames inside an owning struct (PR 3756, APPROVED at 7206e88cc2). A wait covering the wrong device set (check index-count-or-wait-set-mismatch); a readiness predicate exposing unfinished pages (concurrency check). Consumers using only unaligned forms, `memcpy`, `std::copy_n`, scalar code. Heap buffers from `dma_allocate_aligned(size, HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES)` or `alloc_align`. A new aligned store through a pointer parameter with no new buffer (PR 2693 added `page::get_v` with `_mm256_store_si256`, APPROVED silently). ## Check 14: buffer lifetime and alignment follow the consumer

Common setup additions: reuse pr.diff for the three greps. Diff greps return pr.diff line numbers; to get the HEAD line of a hit run `git -C WT grep -n -F '<matched text without the leading +>' HEAD -- <file>`, or add the hit's offset inside its hunk to the `+start` of the nearest `@@` header above it (`git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <file>`). If HEAD is the commit next to a reviewer comment and `git -C WT cat-file -t HEAD` fails (force-pushed away), fetch each file the comment names with `gh api "repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD" -q .content | base64 -d > old/<path>` and build the diff with `diff -u <(git -C WT show BASE:<path>) old/<path>`; run the greps on that file instead of pr.diff.

Arm A (asynchronous release):
1. `grep -nE '^\+[^/]*(dma_allocate|dma_deallocate|release_buffer|free_staging|abandon\(|\.pop\(\)|\.reset\(\)|xfer_(n_)?blocks\(|xfer_gofs?\(|dma_tracker::push|~[a-z_]+\(\)\s*\{)' pr.diff` (the `[^/]*` drops comment lines; `\s*\{` keeps only destructor definitions). Keep hits inside a struct that owns the pointer or a function that submits it; a hunk that only renames a parameter or member type inside such a struct does not count.
2. Per owning struct S: `git -C WT show HEAD:<header> | awk '/struct S/,/^};/'` and `git -C WT grep -n 'S' HEAD -- h src` for the destructor, `complete()`, `abandon()` and every holder. Write the sequence allocate -> populate -> submit -> push -> completion observed -> release.
3. Drop paths: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'clear\(\)|~dma_tracker|q\.pop\(\)|\.reset\(\)|std::optional<pending_xfer>' HEAD -- src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp h/pos/dma_tracker.hpp`. For each, read until the record dies and record: waits (`hwcacheblock::wait`), leaks on purpose (`abandon()` sets `data = nullptr`), or frees. For `~dma_tracker` the deciding line is whether it calls `clear()` before its queue members are destroyed; if not, queue destruction reaches the record destructor, whose outcome is the path's outcome. For the record destructor read whether the free is conditional on completion; an unconditional `if (data) dma_deallocate` is "frees". A free with no wait after submission is the finding.
4. Exclusive fields: `git -C WT show HEAD:h/pos/dma_tracker.hpp | grep -n 'pinned_'` and `git -C WT grep -n 'TRON_ASSERT.*pinned' HEAD -- src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp`; no assert that `pinned_gof` and `pinned_batch` are exclusive is a nit inside an Arm A finding, never standalone.

Arm B (reserve literal with a held reference):
5. `grep -nE '^\+.*\.reserve\([0-9]+\)' pr.diff` lists literal reserves; take the container name V from each line. For each V: `grep -nE '^\+.*&\s*[a-z_]+\s*=\s*V(\.(back|front)\(\)|\[)|= *V\.data\(\)' pr.diff` finds held references (the `\s*` after `&` is required: Wade's site is `frame_t& f = stk.back();`), and `grep -nE '^\+.*V\.(push_back|emplace_back|insert|resize|assign|pop_back)\(' pr.diff` the growth calls. Keep only triples on one container inside one function (confirm with the HEAD-line mapping). `.data()` on a std::array or std::span never counts. A named constant as the reserve argument does not trigger.
6. `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<ref line>,<last use>p' | grep -n -E 'V\.(push_back|emplace_back|insert|resize|assign|pop_back)\(|continue;|break;|return'`. Record what bounds the pushes (tree depth, shard size, an assert); if not written next to the reserve, the finding is the question. For each growth call follow every path to the next read of the reference; a read reached without `continue`, `break` or `return` upgrades the question to a defect. After `pop_back()` every later use must re-take `back()`.

Arm C (scratch handed to a SIMD consumer):
7. `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -nE '^\+.*(std::array<(bf16|float|uint8_t|__m256i|__m512i), *[A-Za-z_0-9]+>|^\+\s*(bf16|float|uint8_t) [a-z_]+\[)' | grep -v alignas` (the comma excludes pointer-element tables such as `std::array<uint8_t const*, N>`; `-- h src` keeps test-local arrays out, they are read in step 10).
8. Consumers: the direct callee; for a `std::function` member `git -C WT grep -n '<member> =' HEAD -- h src t` and the production call inside each lambda. Resolve to one overload: take the pointer type of the callback's destination parameter and keep the overload of the production call whose last parameter has that type (`git -C WT show HEAD:<consumer file> | grep -n '<fn>('`, read each signature). Bound the grep to that body: `START=<signature line>; END=$(awk -v s=$START 'NR>s && /^}/ {print NR; exit}' <file>); sed -n "${START},${END}p" <file> | grep -n -E '_mm256_store_si256|_mm256_load_si256|_mm512_(store|load)_(si512|ps|epi)|_mm256_store_ps|_mm512_stream'`, adding START-1 to each hit. A whole-file grep is not a result (kv_cache.hpp has 57 intrinsic lines). Needed alignment: 32 bytes for `_mm256_*` aligned forms, 64 for `_mm512_*`.
9. Declared alignment: `alignas(N)` on the line; otherwise open the element type's definition (`git -C WT grep -n -E '^(struct|class) <T>\b' HEAD -- h`) and take its alignas if present, else the alignment of its single member (`__bf16`, `uint16_t` 2 bytes, `float` 4); for `bf16` this is h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp:12-13 `struct bf16 { __bf16 content; }`, 2 bytes. Heap buffers: the allocator argument. Sibling: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n alignas`; `git -C WT grep -n 'HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES =' HEAD -- h/pos/config.hpp` gives the constant.
10. Test reach: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<consumer>\(|<production fn>\(' HEAD -- t/` and read whether the test's callback calls the real consumer or copies with `std::copy_n`.
11. Runtime proof, two forms. (a) Needs no tron build: a 15-line file that declares an `alignas(64)` array, passes `array + 8` (16 bytes past the boundary) to a `__attribute__((noinline))` function that executes the consumer's exact store intrinsic; build with `g++ -O1 -mavx2 -fsanitize=alignment -fno-sanitize-recover=alignment` (`-mavx512f` for `_mm512_*`); run on any host with the instruction set (`grep -o -m1 avx2 /proc/cpuinfo`). "store to misaligned address ... requires 32 byte alignment" is the proof; the aligned pointer must print ok. (b) Needs the tron build: compile the declaring function with `-S` and read the stack offset. If neither runs, write `Insufficient data: not compiled` and say which was blocked. An optimizing compiler can fuse the store into an unaligned form, so a green normal build is not proof.

On PR 4128, Arm C at 97de6ee02c (in WT, BASE 130ad3a652): step 7 gives 1 hit, src/tron/gof.cpp:436 `std::array<std::array<bf16, HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE>, HW_MAX_KV_HEADS> v_scratch;` (the draft regex without the comma gave 3: also gof.cpp:270 `qdatas` pointer table and t/t_phase1_integration.cpp:832); :445 passes `v_scratch[h].data()` to get_v_head, which calls `page.v_head_into_fn(layer, head, scratch)` at :34-35; member h/tron/gof.hpp:76; one production assignment h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2519 whose lambda calls `pg_ptr->get_v(slot, kv_head, off, dest)` with `bf16* dest`; the bf16* overload h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2096-2120 stores with `_mm256_store_si256` at :2109 and :2117 (32 bytes); declared alignment 2 bytes (bf16.hpp:12-13); sibling alignas(HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES) at gof.cpp:371, constant 64 at h/pos/config.hpp:120; only test callback t/t_phase1_integration.cpp:945-951 is `std::copy_n`; standalone UBSan reproducer fails at +16 bytes and passes aligned (Wade: 'misaligned by 16 bytes'). Fix at 7f80aa17da gof.cpp:417-419 plus t/t_llama_unit.cpp:994-1017 (REQUIRE `dest % HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES == 0`, then the real `page->get_v`). Arm A at 442ed0dd1a (not in WT; gh api contents): h/tron/gof.hpp:267-281 gof_dma_batch; src/tron/gof.cpp:40-42 `~gof_dma_batch() { if (data) dma_deallocate(data, size); }` unconditional, :44-52 complete() decrements pins only, :54-58 abandon() nulls `data`; src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp:152-166 clear() calls `abandon()` then `q.pop()` without waiting; :57-61 `~dma_tracker` erases itself from the registry and does NOT call clear(), so a tracker destroyed with queued records reaches the batch destructor and frees under live DMA = the forwarded item; pinned assert 0 hits. 97de6ee02c is not an ancestor of 7f80aa17da; its twin fd9fa17f9d (same subject, 2026-09-03) is; at both, clear() :159-190 waits (`hwcacheblock::wait` :180, `complete()` :188) and `~dma_tracker` :58-68 calls clear() at :67, so Arm A does not fire there (the author chose wait-in-clear, not abandon-in-destructor; `~gof_dma_batch` :278-280 still frees unconditionally). Text = one Wade comment, review body or conversation comment in the corpus (269 texts on 115 PRs he did not author: 243 inline, 11 conversation, 15 review bodies with words). Top-level text = a text that is not a reply (232 of 269). Id = the GitHub comment or review id. ### Rules for an agent writing in his name

style.verdict_calibration:
## Verdict calibration

Words used here: PR = pull request. Review = one GitHub review event with a state (APPROVED, COMMENTED or CHANGES_REQUESTED). Silent PR = a PR where Wade left no words at all. Top-level comment = an inline comment that is not a reply, a conversation comment, or a non-APPROVED review body with words. Counts are from style-stats.json over 115 PRs and 334 reviews unless marked "recount".

### Review states

- 334 reviews: 100 APPROVED (30 percent), 234 COMMENTED (70 percent), 0 CHANGES_REQUESTED.
- 113 of 115 PRs have at least one review. Reviews per PR: 1 review on 59 PRs, 2 on 21, 3 to 5 on 17, 6 or more on 16 (maximum 23 on one PR).
- 0 of the 100 APPROVED reviews carry an inline comment. Inline comments go under a COMMENTED review. The approval is a separate, later review.
- 12 of 100 APPROVED reviews carry words. 4 of those 12 are 40 characters or shorter ("looks good to me", "nice catch...", "Looks sensible to me!").

### Final verdict by number of top-level comments (115 PRs)

- 0 comments: 57 APPROVED, 1 COMMENTED (58 PRs).
- 1 to 2 comments: 21 APPROVED, 8 COMMENTED, 2 with no review (31 PRs).
- 3 to 5 comments: 9 APPROVED, 3 COMMENTED (12 PRs).
- 6 or more comments: 11 APPROVED, 3 COMMENTED (14 PRs).

Reading: comment count does not predict the verdict. 11 of the 14 PRs with 6 or more comments ended APPROVED.

### How a must-change is signalled

He never uses CHANGES_REQUESTED. A must-change is carried by words, in four forms (ids and counts over 269 texts, from codex-factcheck.md claim 6 and a recount):

- "before merge" or "before merging": 2 texts by Wade. 3124878965 (PR 2499, 2026-04-22): "can we comment this back out before merge?". 4265644124 (PR 2698 review, 2026-05-11): "Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs against these changes before merging." (A third hit, 5544513215, is pasted assistant text.)
- "needs": 4 texts. 3002050036 (PR 2233, 2026-03-27): "looks like this still needs fixed". 2897190682 (PR 2089, 2026-03-06): "the pre_attn scalar needs to come from the model... 1.0f is not the correct value, currently". 4373886636 (PR 2766 review, 2026-05-27): "Also needs rebased."
- "Please <verb>": 3 texts, all 2026-09 onward. 5420005787 (PR 4557 review, 2026-10-05): "please split them out", "Please squash", "Please re-run them or mark them as pre-merge". 3960538177 and 3960538961 (PR 4128, 2026-09-08): "Please extend an existing CI suite ...".
- Withheld approval: 16 of the 67 PRs with Wade text have no APPROVED review from him: tron 1485, 1860, 2089, 2233, 2287, 2426, 2674, 2695, 2777, 2872, 3016, 3738, 4128, 4258, 3879, 2898.
- "must" as a directive: 0 texts. "blocking": 0 texts, except the negation "non-blocking nit" in 6021333114.

### Conditional approvals (verbatim)

- 4373886636 (PR 2766, 2026-05-27, APPROVED): "Overall looks good to me. Approved, assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments. Also needs rebased."
- 4265644124 (PR 2698, 2026-05-11, state COMMENTED, words say approved): "Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs against these changes before merging." The GitHub state and the words disagree here. Read the words.
- 5156698046 (PR 4267, 2026-09-09, APPROVED): "I'm ok approving this as-is, although I'm wondering if you looked at the possibility of using FUSE for this?"
- 4800935083 (PR 3490, 2026-07-28, APPROVED): "I do think there's some merit to a few of them, but could be a follow-up if you prefer. I'll approve as-is."
- 5371062950 (PR 4596, 2026-09-30, APPROVED): "Approved... I think your PR description is stale at this point (after all the updates from reviews), and you currently have a merge conflict. But overall looks good."
- 5431977719 (PR 4557, 2026-10-06, APPROVED): "Approved. Updates look good and clean... left one response to coding style. Trivial nit though."

Reading: he approves with open nits, a stale description or a merge conflict still present. Approval is withheld for a correctness or coverage item, not for style.

### The 48 silent PRs

- 48 of 115 PRs have no Wade words. Each has exactly one review, state APPROVED (recount).
- Size (recount from corpus.json file lists, nearest-rank quantiles): median 2 files, 19 of 48 touch one file. Median 39 changed lines, 25th percentile 10 lines, 75th percentile 130 lines (merged-taxonomy.json reports 161 for the 75th percentile with a different quantile method). 27 of 48 change at most 50 lines.
- The 67 PRs with Wade words: median 8 files, median 426 changed lines. 9 of 67 change at most 50 lines.
- 15 of 48 silent PRs target the hwattention_sync branch. By author: mcherba 11, BillBaumann 10, bham0n 7, mitchelldalvirosen-positron 6, jeremyconner1975 5, others 9.

style.assisted_text:
## Assisted text (pasted from an AI assistant)

Words used here: PR = pull request. Disclosed paste = a Wade text that says in its own words that an assistant (Claude, "CC" for Claude Code, or GPT) wrote the block that follows. Id = the GitHub comment or review id. Register B = the long, file:line, "So"-consequence form described under "How Wade words a finding".

### The nine disclosed pastes (9 of 269 texts; ids, dates and the disclosing sentence, verbatim)

1. 3002297607 (PR 2233, inline, 2026-03-27): "Claude had this to say about below:"
2. 4131374395 (PR 2461, APPROVED review, 2026-04-17): "I think CC is onto something with that `attn_launchers` finding."
3. 3342904643 (PR 2872, inline, 2026-06-02): "(which I let Claude summarize for me below)"
4. 4674512577 (PR 2906, conversation, 2026-06-10): "So I asked Claude to summarize my concern (cuz it often words things better than I can):"
5. 3437517809 (PR 3008, inline, 2026-06-18): "GPT had this to say about `first_desc`:"
6. 4800935083 (PR 3490, APPROVED review, 2026-07-28): "I did ask claude to do a review as well. Below are the items it came up with. I do think there's some merit to a few of them, but could be a follow-up if you prefer. I'll approve as-is."
7. 5498556672 (PR 4128, conversation, 2026-09-01): "So I prompted Claude with that (and told it to look at the PR overall). I also asked it to evaluate any collateral concurrency risks... below are those results:"
8. 5544513215 (PR 3879, conversation, 2026-09-04): "below is Claude's evaluation of this PR:"
9. 3970590653 (PR 4191, inline reply, 2026-09-09): "I asked GPT to evaluate this... it agrees:"

The earliest disclosure is 2026-03-27 (CONTEXT.md says the first is in PR 2233; codex-factcheck.md claim 7 confirms the date). Two further texts mention an assistant without pasting analysis: 3227565141 (PR 2713) and 3463077403 (PR 3016).

### How to treat a paste

- The pasted block is the assistant's claim. Wade's own words are the frame sentence around it. Quote the frame as Wade; quote the block as "assistant text pasted by Wade in <id>".
- Wade's weight on a pasted item is the frame sentence, not the block. "I think CC is onto something" (4131374395), "I do think there's some merit to a few of them" (4800935083) and "it agrees" (3970590653) are endorsements. "could be a follow-up if you prefer" (4800935083) and "Maybe it won't materialize" (4674512577) are not must-changes.
- A paste can carry words Wade never uses himself. "Blocking" in 5544513215 is in the pasted block; Wade's own texts never use "blocking" except as "non-blocking" (6021333114). "must" as a directive appears only inside pasted text.
- A pasted list is answered item by item, with a fact per item, and the reply is addressed to Wade.
- A paste is not independent verification. When a pasted item cites a line, re-check the line at the reviewed head before conceding it.

### PR 4557: register B, no disclosure (Insufficient data)

- PR 4557 has 10 Wade texts: review 5420005787, inline 4188336250, 4188336256, 4188336267, 4188336279, 4188336302, 4188336316, 4188336324, reply 6021333114, approval 5431977719. None of the 10 mentions an assistant (codex-factcheck.md claim 7).
- The style markers of the 2026-10-05 texts match the disclosed-assisted PR 4128: "So" consequence in 4188336267, backticked file:line in 5420005787 ("`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:355` builds with `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON`"), "(line 197)" in 4188336256, "Please" three times in 5420005787.
- In PR 4128 the inline comments of 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-08 (3907183627, 3907185740, 3907214892, 3960506641, 3960538177, 3960538961; 762 to 1486 characters each) carry no disclosure. The disclosure sits in the same-day conversation comment 5498556672. In PR 4596 the 2026-09-28 inline comments (4125033634 to 4125033686, 548 to 946 characters) carry no disclosure anywhere.
- The 2026-10-06 reply 6021333114 returns to the hand-written register: "Fair enough for the AMX kernel files", "This is simply a non-blocking nit though ;-p."
- Verdict: whether PR 4557 was assisted is Insufficient data. A statement from Wade, or a disclosure sentence in the PR, would resolve it. Treat the PR 4557 findings as Wade's own words (he posted them under his name and approved on them), and treat the register as what he now writes, whatever the tool.

### Rule for an agent

- Record for every quoted text whether it is hand-written, disclosed paste, or undisclosed register B. Never cite a pasted block as "Wade said".
- When drafting in his name, write in the register, but never add a disclosure sentence he did not write and never remove one he did.
